We performed full-length mRNA sequencing on CHL1 and A375 melanoma cell lines treated with the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib and the PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 and CTX085 and analysed data for differential gene expression and differential pre-mRNA splicing induced by these agents.

title: Genomic and transcriptomic determinants of response to neoadjuvant therapy in rectal cancer
summary: We performed RNA-seq on pre-treatment endoscopic biopsies from 114 patients, including 97 patients treated with NAT that qualified for outcome analyses We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq

title: WRN promotes bone development and growth by unwinding SHOX-G-quadruplexes via its helicase activity in Werner Syndrome [RNA-seq]
summary: Werner Syndrome (WS) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by premature aging due to mutations of the WRN gene. A classical sign in WS patients is short stature, but the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. Here we report that WRN is indispensable for chondrogenesis, which is the engine driving the elongation of bones and determines height.

title: Gene expression profiles affected by Sam68-knockdown in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells
summary: The changes in the transcriptome via Sam68-knockdown were investigated in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells. The candidate genes which are regulated by Sam68 were demonstrated.
design: Oral squamous cell carcinoma cells with Sam68 siRNA or control siRNA were analysed using mRNA-sequencing.

title: Gene expression of cardiomyocytes exposed to L-lactate
summary: We evaluated the effect of L-lactate supplementation in cell culture media on cardiomyocyte gene expression

title: Jurkat T cell exposure to short hypergravity on a ground-based facility
summary: Jurkat T cells have been lysed after exposure to 3 or 15 minutes of 9g hypergravity in a ground-based pipette centrifuge. The RNA samples were analyzed with RNA-Seq transcriptomics.
design: 1 short hyptergravity condition (12 minutes of 1g + 3 minutes of 9g), 1 long hypergravity condition (15 minutes of 9g), 1 ground control condition (15 minutes of 1g). 4 samples per condition.

title: ZCCHC4 Interacts with AL133467.2 and gamma H2AX to Promote Chemoresistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma [HepG2_ZCCHC4 KO]
summary: Purpose: We performed RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis of ZCCHC4 KO1 cells and wild type cells to find differentially expressed genes regulated by ZCCHC4 in HCC cells. The goal of this study is to investigate the biological effect of ZCCHC4 in HCC progression and prognosis.

title: Next Generation Sequencing identifies differentially expressed genes regulated by PM2.5 exposure in BEAS-2B cells [RNA-seq]
summary: We report the application of RNA-sequencing for high-throughput profiling of transcriptomes in BEAS-2B cells after exposure to PM2.5 for 24 hours..

title: RNA Sequencing of L1-FGGY- and L1-FGGY+ lung squamous cell carcinoma tissues
summary: We uncovered the roles of Long Interspersed Nuclear Element-1 (LINE-1, L1) in cancer development in this study. In order to elucidate the underlying oncogenic roles of L1-FGGY in tumorigenesis and tumor progression, we collected an independent Chinese cohort of 109 LUSC tumor samples (52 L1-FGGY+ vs. 57 L1-FGGY-) from Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital (TJMUCH) and performed RNA sequencing for them.The functional Gene Ontology enrichment of those genes in L1-FGGY+ tissues revealed the significant functions in multiple metabolic processes, including glutathione metabolism, arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism, and drug metabolism.

title: Transcriptomic  analysis of HCC1954 Parental(Pa),  synchronous (S-BM), latent residual (Lat) or metachronous (M-BM) brain metastases cells
summary: We did the transcriptomic profiling of HCC1954 Parental(Pa),  synchronous (S-BM), latent residual (Lat) or metachronous (M-BM) brain metastases cells

title: NXN suppresses metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma by promoting degradation of Snail through binding to DUB3
summary: To investigate the function of NXN in the regulation of metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells, we established NXN knock down Hep-3B cells by shRNA. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of 2 different cells at three time points.

title: The role of core circadian component BMAL1 or CLOCK in human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells osteogenic capacity
summary: To elucidate how the core circadian component BMAL1 and clock regulate the osteogenic capacity of human bone marrow MSCs, RNA-seq was performed to study the impact of diminishing core component BMAL1 or CLOCK in MSCs by lentiviruses.
design: Examination of the mRNA profiles in human bone marrow MSCs with diminishing  BMAL1 or CLOCK during osteogenic differentiation

title: RNA-binding protein ELAVL4/HuD ameliorates Alzheimer's disease-related molecular changes in human iPSC-derived neurons
summary: We generated ELAVL4 knockout (KO), overexpression (OE), and rescue human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons to study the effect that ELAVL4 has on AD-related cellular phenotypes. To gain insight into the molecular cascades involved in neuronal ELAVL4 signaling, we then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq using triplicate samples for each condition

title: Longitudinal multi-omics analysis identifies early blood-based predictors of anti-TNF therapy response in inflammatory bowel disease [RNA-Seq]
summary: We investigated the dynamics of gene expression in blood samples of IBD patients treated with infliximab and vedolizumab and analyzed the predictive potential regarding therapy outcome.
design: We performed a longitudinal, blood-based multi-omics study in two prospective IBD patient cohorts receiving first time infliximab therapy (discovery: 14 patients, replication: 23 patients) and one prospective IBD patient cohort receiving first time vedolizumab therapy (17 patients). Samples were collected at up to 7 timepoints (from baseline to 14 weeks after therapy induction).

title: The RNA sequencing analysis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) cell line S18 upon circIPO7 knockdown
summary: The development of therapeutic resistance and metastatic dissemination takes place in 20-30% patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), resulting in poor survival. Hence, a better understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms will help improve clinical outcome. We have identified a novel circRNA, circIPO7, as a promoter of metastasis and cisplatin chemoresistance in NPC cells. High-throughput RNA sequencing analysis was performed in the human nasopharyngeal carcinoma cell line S18 after transfection with control siRNA or circIPO7 siRNA.

title: mRNA expression levels in Jurkat cell lines treated with or without IFN-alpha and with shaking or static
summary: Throuth RNA sequencing analyses, we report that shaking did not affect transcriptome in Jurkat cells and differential expressed genes by IFN-alpha were detected.
design: mRNA expression profiles in the Jurkat T-cell lines in shaking culture without IFN-alpha (n=3), static culture without IFN-alpha  (n=3), shaking culture with IFN-alph treatment for 24h (n=3) and static culture with IFN-alpha treatment for 24h (n=3) were generated by RNA sequencing. RNA was extracted using RNeasy Mini kit (Qiagen). RNA sequencing was conducted in Medical & Biological Laboratories, co (Nagoya, Japan).

title: Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) Facilitates Quantitative Analysis of Wildtype and Zmynd8-Overexpressing Transcriptomes in E14 Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells (mESCs)
summary: Purpose: The goal of this study is to identify Zmynd8-regulated genes.

title: Chloroquine enhances the effectiveness of 5 Fluorouracil in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma via activation of p53 signaling
summary: To investigate the molecular mechanisms of chloroquine, 5 Fluorouracil, and their combination in ESCC cell line TE11
design: We have treated ESCC cell line TE11 with 10 µM of chloroquine, 25 µM of 5 Fluorouracil, and their combination for 48 hours. Then we performed RNA sequencing.

title: RNA-seq analysis of MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells with NF1 deficiency
summary: RNAseq analysis of NF1 loss of function in immortalized, nontumorigenic human breast epithelial cell line MCF10A.  CRISPR guides targeting exon 21 within the GRD domain were constructed and used either as single or dual-guide RNAs with Cas9 nuclease. We established three cell lines (i.e., g1, g2, g1/2) and NF1 loss was validated by PCR and Western blot analysis (Figure S6B).
design: 15 samples derived from the human MCF10 cell line. The samples are divided into 5 genotypes, each with 3 samples. The genotypes are parental MCF10,  empty vector control, and three NF1 mutants: guide RNA 1, guide RNA 2, and guide RNA 1 and 2.

title: Effect of CD33 and/or CD123 KO in the NPM1-mutated AML cell line OCI-AML3
summary: To reveal which pathways linked to CD33 and CD123 overexpression could be involved in leukemic proliferation, we performed unbiased bulk RNA sequencing comparison between OCI-AML3 wt and CD123 and or CD33 KO clones

title: Analysis of cellular transcripts targeted by ZAPL or  ZAPS  in HEK293T cells
summary: To investigate the differential functions of two major ZAP variants, ZAPL and ZAPS, in the regulation of cellular RNA abundance, we established HEK293T cell lines in which either ZAPL or ZAPS has been knockout with CRISPR-mediated deletion.

title: Investigating the role of cholesterol in regulation of expression using RNA-seq and ATAC-seq
summary: Our work demonstrates that nuclear cholesterol plays a direct role in transcriptional regulation through its interaction with BASP1.

title: Genome-wide transcriptome analysis of SARS-CoV-2 positive patients' mucosa, compared with negative controls.
summary: We report the application of genome-wide RNA-sequencing analysis for SARS-CoV-2 positive patients' mucosa. We analyzed the correlation between gene expression levels and viral load (assessed with qPCR) and found a gene signature that might be relevant for diagnosis and treatment of SARS-CoV-2 infection. We performed such analyses in samples with assigned lineage B.1 or B.1.617 (Delta). We compared the expression of these genes in negative patients and observed low abundance, thus confirming their significance.

title: Maturation and circuit integration of transplanted human cortical organoids
summary: We show that human stem cell-derived cortical organoids transplanted into the somatosensory cortex of newborn athymic rats develop mature cell types that integrate into sensory and motivation-related circuits. Magnetic resonance imaging allows monitoring of post-transplantation organoid growth across multiple stem cell lines and animals, while single nucleus profiling reveals high cell diversity and progression of corticogenesis, as well as the emergence of an activity-dependent transcriptional program in neurons.

title: RNA sequencing reveals the expression profiles of long noncoding RNA in lipopolysaccharide-induced sepsis
summary: There are currently no specific diagnostic biomarkers and effective pharmacological treatments for sepsis, which makes the mortality rate remains high. Although non-coding RNAs seem to be superior candidates as biomarkers and therapeutics for sepsis, the role of long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) in sepsis remains not completely understood. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of 2 different cells at the same time point.
design: Comparative gene expression profiling analysis of RNA-seq data for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induced sepsis  human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs)  and normal HUVECs.

title: RNA-sequencing of IRF5+ and IRF5- circulating monocytes from patients with Type-2 Diabetes
summary: Purpose: To characterise the transcriptomic landscape in monocytes associated with IRF5 expression Methods: RNA sequencing from FACS sorted IRF5+ and IRF5- CD14+ monocytes Results: Differential expression based on IRF5 postiivity provides insight into its roles in monocyte function and in type-2 diabetes Conclusions: This study represents the first analyses of IRF5-dependent transcriptome in circulating monocytes from patients with Type-2 diabetes

title: Endothelial Gsα regulates post-ischemia angiogenesis
summary: In the present study, we investigated the role of endothelial Gsα in post-ischemic angiogenesis.

title: Effect of native or citrullinated histone peptides on gene expression of THP-1 cells
summary: To examine the cellular effects of histones, we analyzed the RNA-seq data of THP-1 cells treated with native or citrullinated H2B-α1 peptide.

title: Regulation of metablism by mitochondrial MUL1 E3 ubiquitin ligase
summary: To investigate how the absence of MUL1 affects metabolic changes as reflected by gene expression.

title: Gene expression profile of cardiac stromal cells from ACM patients in adipogenic medium with and without MB-3 treatment
summary: Human primary cardiac stromal cells were isolated from arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy patients and were cultured either in adipogenic medium (ADIPO, A) or in adipogenic medium supplemented with MB-3 (MB-3, M), that is a specific inhibitor of GCN5. The gene expressiona analysis was aimed to investigate the molecular effect of GCN5 inhibition.

title: Transcriptional data of tissues in pacients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma
summary: Transcriptional data of 12 pairs NPC tissues with high or low intratumoural bacteria load

title: RNAseq analysis of SARS-CoV-2 infection of iAT2 cells
summary: Analysis of histone mimicry by SARS-CoV-2 Orf8 encoded protein
design: SARS-CoV-2 WT virus, Orf8 deletion virus, or mock infection of A549-ACE cells was performed and RNA was collected at 24 or 48 hours after infection

title: RNAseq analysis of SARS-CoV-2 infection of A549ACE cells
summary: Analysis of histone mimicry by SARS-CoV-2 Orf8 encoded protein
design: SARS-CoV-2 WT virus, Orf8 deletion virus, or mock infection of A549-ACE cells was performed and RNA was collected at 24 or 48 hours after infection

title: Dissecting the process of human neutrophil lineage determination by using alpha-lipoic acid inducing neutrophil deficiency model
summary: Neutrophil deficiency or differentiation disorder might cause serious diseases, such as neutropenia and neutrophilia. To reveal the molecular mechanism of human neutrophil lineage commitment, single cell RNAseq and bulk cells RNAseq were performed to reveal the characteristics and essential genes of neutrophil lineage determination.
design: To explore the molecular mechanism of early commitment of neutrophil progenitors derived from GMPs, we performed single cell RNAseq for GMPs derived early progenitors, early neutrophil bias progenitors (CD34+CD15- NbP1, CD34mid CD15mid NbP2, CD34int/-CD15+NbP3) gated from CD115-CD73-CD1C-CD116- cells and CD34midCD115+MoPs. In addition, we also performed bulk cell RNAseq for ALA treated NbP1/NbP2, ELK1 and S-ELK1 overexpressed NbP1. The single cell RNAseq and bulk cell RNAseq were performed as we described in previous published paper (PMID:29434353, 31443434). 10X single cell RNAseq was performed for human bone marrow derived Lin- CD371+ progenitors.

title: The effect of CBX2 knockdown on gene expression in MCF-7 cells
summary: To identify potential CBX2-regulated genes in ER positive cancer cells we assessed global gene expression changes in CBX2-depleted MCF-7 cells by RNA-sequencing analysis using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. Through Gene Set Enrichment Analysis we identified that CBX2 promotes cell growth, mTORC1 activation, E2F signalling.
design: MCF-7 cells were transfected with either a non-silencing scrambled control siRNA (siSCR) or CBX2 targeting siRNA (siCBX2#3), using Lipfectamine RNAiMAX (Invitrogen) to a final concentration of 25 nM. Cells were grown for 72 hours prior to RNA extraction using the RNeasy mini kit (Qiagen). Library preparation and sequencing using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform was performed by Novogene Co Ltd (Cambridge, UK). Read alignment was performed using the HISAT2 algorithm and FPKM calculated to estimate gene expression in each sample.

title: The effect of CBX2 knockdown on gene expression in MDA-MB-231 cells
summary: To identify potential CBX2-regulated genes in triple negative breast cancer cells we assessed global gene expression changes in CBX2-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells by RNA-sequencing analysis using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. Through Gene Set Enrichment Analysis we identified that CBX2 promotes cell growth, mTORC1 activation, E2F signalling and inhibits RBL2-mediated DREAM-complex activity.
design: MDA-MB-231 cells were transfected with either a non-silencing scrambled control siRNA (siSCR) or CBX2 targeting siRNAs (siCBX2#2/siCBX2#3), using Lipfectamine RNAiMAX (Invitrogen) to a final concentration of 25 nM. Cells were grown for 72 hours prior to RNA extraction using the RNeasy mini kit (Qiagen). Library preparation and sequencing using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform was performed by Novogene Co Ltd (Cambridge, UK). Read alignment was performed using the HISAT2 algorithm and FPKM calculated to estimate gene expression in each sample.

title: Analysis of the transcriptome of CD34+38- cord blood cells treated with 3-deazaadenosine (3DA)
summary: Cord blood cells were cultured in the presence of 10 mM 3-deazaadenosine (3DA) or DMSO. After 9 days, the CD34+38- population was sorted using FACS and subjected to RNAseq. Our previous experiments have shown that treating other cell types with 3DA partially prevents senescence. By performing RNAseq, we show how treating cord blood cells with 3DA affects senescence, stemness and differentiation
design: 8 different samples. CD34+38- cells were obtained from cord blood cells (from 4 different donors: 338, 522, 535, 545) that have been treated for 9 days with DMSO (DMSO) or 10 mM 3-deazaadenosine (3DA).

title: Longitudinal analysis reveals that probiotics are a significant driver of gut microbiome development in very preterm infants
summary: Impact of small molecules from different microbial gut community types on gene expression from preterm intestinal derived organoids

title: RNA-seq profiling of 22Rv1 prostate cancer cells exposed to repeated DNA damage for 6 weeks.
summary: RNA-seq profiling of 22Rv1 prostate cancer cell line either untreated, 6 weeks in culture (age matched) or treated daily for 6 weeks with 1 microgram per ml phleomycin to induce DNA damage (n=3 per sample).

title: Trisomy 21 human iPSC derived interneuron progenitors
summary: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS, Ts21) have impaired neurogenesis during development. Using Ts21 human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and isogenic controls, we carried out single cell RNA-sequencing of Ts21 interneuron progenitors .

title: RNA-seq on HER2+ cell line upon treatments
summary: We proceeded RNA-seq on HER2+ breast cancer line HCC1954 cells treated with DMSO, SNXB, Lapatinib and combination for 24 hours. By analyzing resulting data, we are trying to figure out the possilble mechanisms of Lapatinib resistance and how our regimen is able to potentiate and overcome resistance.
design: HCC1954 cells were treated with DMSO, SNXB, Lapatinib and Combination for 24 hours. Samples were from three biological repeats.

title: Gene expression profile at single cell level of human TILs treated with PD1-TIM3, PD1-LAG3, anti-PD1 or control isotype.
summary: Several next-generation cancer immunotherapies are designed to target LAG3 and TIM3 checkpoints, though the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which both receptors operate to mediate their anti-tumour effects are still poorly understood. Here, we examined the phenotypical and transcriptional consequences of treatment with bispecific antibodies (bsAbs), currently being tested in clinical trials, which co-target PD1 and either TIM3 or LAG3, respectively, using scRNAseq.

title: Single cell RNA-sequencing of Cushing's disease adenomas
summary: Cushing's disease causes severe morbidity and mortality, yet its underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. We used scRNAseq to compare the transcriptomes of CD adenomas to their normal adjacent pituitary glands

title: RNA-seq comparing Cushing's disease adenomas and surrounding normal tissues
summary: To investigate transcriptomic differences between Cushing's disease adenomas and adjacent normal tissues We performed RNAseq analysis on CD adenomas versus their adjacent normal tissues

title: Transcriptome effects of media and methotrexate on T-ALL cell lines
summary: Human T-ALL cells become chemoresistant to multiple chemotherapies if exposed to adipocyte-secreted factors.   To identifiy gene alterations underlying adipocyte-mediated chemoresistance, we performed RNA-sequencing analysis on untreated human T-ALL cells and those treated with the chemotherapy metotrexate.

title: Lens epithelial cells transcriptome analysis
summary: We performed RNAseq of passage 15 and passage 42 lens epithelial cell (FHL124), a lens epithelial cellular aging model.

title: The m6A methyltransferase Mettl3 deficiency attenuates hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis [RNA-seq]
summary: RNA sequencing of LX2 cell line (a human hepatic stellate cell line). METTL3 overexpression or downreguation were achieved by lenti-virus transduction.

title: RNA-seq analysis in triple negative breast cancer cells after knocking down DDX18
summary: To assess the function of DDX18 in TNBCs, we performed transcriptome analysis through high-throughput RNA-Seq of control and DDX18 knockdown cells

title: Chronically radiation-exposed survivor GBM cells display poor response to Chk1 inhibition.
summary: To investigate radiation response of reccurent glioblastoma models after radiotherapy, we have utilized clinically relevant radioresistant cell model. We have generated to radiation survivor GBM population from 1 cell line and 1 primary cell line. To investigate transcriptomic alterations we have performed RNA-seq to our both naive and IR survivor samples as triplicates.
design: Examining transcriptomic alterations in radiation-survivor and naive GBM cells.

title: mRNA expression profiling (QuantSeq3' mRNA) analysis of human glioblastoma cell line U87MG treated with ID Family (ID1, ID2, ID3, and ID4) overexpression
summary: To understand the changes in the expression of genes in U87MG cells due to ID Family, we analyzed the transcriptome of U87MG cells overexpressing ID Family. As a result, we identify differentially expressed genes patterns so that the signaling mechanism regulated by ID Family in GBM and changes in cells were observed. These mRNA expression profiling analysis results enable an understanding of the signaling mechanism by ID Family in GBM.
design: Transcriptome of U87MG treated with control vector (GFP) and treated with ID Family (ID1, ID2, ID3, and ID4) overexpression vector

title: Transcriptome analysis of long non-coding RNA Smyca knockdown in breast cancer cells
summary: Gene expression profiles of Smyca or Control shRNA expressing MDA-MB 231 cells were generated by Illumna RNA sequencing.

title: EZH2 T367 phosphorylation activates p38 signaling through lysine methylation to promote breast cancer progression [RNA-seq]
summary: To investigate the gene expression deregulation in Breast Cancer Tumors treated with P38i, EZH2i, the combination and controls.

title: The key factors of drug resistance with cell-cell interactions
summary: The inductional abilities of drug resistance by the knockout of C9orf89, MAGI2, MLPH, or RHBDD2 in supporting cells were solidly confirmed by the reduction of apoptosis by cell-cell interactions.

title: Novel azetidine-based Stat3 inhibitors induce misfolded protein response, endoplasmic reticulum stress and mitophagy, and inhibit breast tumor growth in vivo
summary: To identify differentially expressed genes and pathways in human breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 cells that are treated with a novel Stat3 inhibitor or DMSO control.

title: Cancer specific microbiome revealed by cell-free RNA reads in patients' plasma
summary: We sequenced cell-free RNA (cfRNA) for five cancer types (colorectal cancer, stomach cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer and esophageal cancer) and healthy individuals in 230 plasma samples collected from 6 clinical centers in China.  Cancer related signaling pathway and microbial genus were identified. Cancer detection and specific classification were achieved through combining both host and microbial cfRNA reads.

title: Gene expression of peripheral blood in healthy, moderate asthma, and severe asthma patients from the IMSA cohort
summary: Identification and characterization of gene expression using Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) of mRNA sequence from whole peripheral blood obtained from asthma patients with varying clinical disease severity

title: RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) of iPSC-derived astrocytes from control and Parkinson's disease patients carrying LRRK2 G2019S point mutation.
summary: Purpose: The goal of this study is to compare the NGS-derived from transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) of human iPSC-derived astrocytes from control and Parkinson’s disease LRRK2 G2019S to gain insight into the mechanisms driving astrocyte's alterations in PD.

title: Knockdown of ZIP11 impairs growth in HeLa cells.
summary: We report the effect of knocking down a nuclear Zn transporter, ZIP11, in HeLa cells

title: Transcriptome analysis of methionine restriction and folate metabolism inhibitor SHIN1 treatment in P3HR-1 cells
summary: RNAseq was used to identify host and viral transcriptome changes in methionine restricted or SHIN1 treated P3HR-1 cells.

title: Transcriptome analysis of methionine restriction or CRISPR knockout of AHCY or MAT2A in Rael cells
summary: RNAseq was used to identify host and viral transcriptome changes in methionine restricted Rael cells or Rael cells expressing control, AHCY or MAT2A sgRNAs.
design: For methionine restriction, Rael cells were washed with PBS and then cultured in methionine free RPMI-1640 media supplemented with 10% dialyzed FBS and 0.01mM L-methionine for 3 days.  Control cells were cultured in methionine free RPMI-1640 media supplemented with 10% dialyzed FBS and 0.1mM L-methionine for 3 days. Control or  methionine restricted cells were then subjected to RNAseq analysis. For CRISPR KO, Rael cells expressing control, AHCY, or MAT2A sgRNAs were subjected to the RNAseq analysis.

title: RNA-seq analysis of hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: Dysregulation of genes and associated mRNAs plays critical roles in the etiology and progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Previous transcriptomic studies of HCC have been largely focused on Asian populations based on microarray platforms. Next generation-based RNA sequencing has provided an unparalleled power and opportunities to comprehensively characterize HCC at the whole transcriptome level.

title: Stable CDK12 knock-out ovarian cancer cells do not show an increased sensitivity to cisplatin and PARP inhibitor treatment
summary: We stabily knock-out CDK12 in A2780 cell line and performed RNA-Seq profiling comparing WT and KO conditions.
design: We stabily knock-out CDK12 in A2780 cell line and performed RNA-Seq profiling comparing WT and KO conditions.

title: RNA-seq analysis of MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells following MYC activation
summary: We profiled gene expression and splicing changes in MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells expressing MYC fused to a portion of estrogen receptor (MYC-ER) (Eilers et al., 1989; Littlewood et al., 1995).   We performed RNA-seq, in triplicate, on 3D-grown MCF-10A MYC-ER cells at 0, 8, and 24 hours (h) after 4-OHT-induced MYC activation.   As a control for 4-OHT-induced effects, 3D-grown parental MCF-10A cells lacking the MYC-ER fusion protein were treated with 4-OHT at the same timepoints.
design: For 3D culture assays, MCF-10A and MCF-10A MYC-ER cells were seeded at a density of 10,000 cells per well in triplicate on a 4-well glass chamber slide coated with Matrigel Growth Factor Reduced (BD Biosciences) as described (Debnath et al., 2003; Liberzon et al., 2015). Media was replaced at 72h. Starting on day 3, cells were treated with 1μM 4-hydroxy tamoxifen (4-OHT) (Sigma) for 48h, 24h, 8h, or 0h, prior to collection. All samples were collected at the same time on day 5.  Cells were washed with PBS (1X) and the Matrigel was dissolved by incubating slides at 4°C in Cell Recovery Solution (BD Biosciences). Total RNA was extracted using the RNeasy kit (Qiagen) including DNase I treatment per manufacturer instructions.   Barcoded RNA libraries were prepared starting with 1ug for MCF-10A of total RNA using the TrueSeq stranded mRNA kit with polyA selection (Illumina), and quantified using a Bioanalyzer DNA 1000 chip (Agilent).   Libraries were sequenced as 150bp paired-end reads at 100-200 million reads per library on an Illumina HiSeq, equal amounts of 3 libraries were pooled per lane.

title: The effect of Kaposi's sarcoma herpesvirus infection on endothelial progenitor cell (EPC) gene expression profile
summary: The alterations induced by KSHV-infection of EPCs with lymphatic characterictics was investigated with gene expression profiling analysis using data from RNA-seq of EPCs 7 days post infection compared to non-infected cells, and from 3 biological replicates.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of lung adenocarcinoma associated alleles in A549s
summary: Based on the previous eVIP study (Cancer Cell, 2016), we profiled the transcriptomes of lung adenocarcinoma cell lines expressing oncogenes to compare methods and investigate the effects of these oncogenes on the cells' whole transcriptomes, differential expression, and alternative splicing
design: mRNA profiles

title: A Bidirectional Single-Cell Migration and Retrieval Chip for Quantitative Study of Dendritic Cell Migration
summary: We describe a microfluidics-based single-cell migration platform that enables high-throughput and precise bidirectional chemotaxis assays (BM-Chip), which allows controllable retrieval of cell subpopulations that have different migratory potentials. We investigated dendritic cell (DC) migration in response to different chemoattractants and inhibitors. We quantitatively described DC migration patterns and retrieved DC subpopulations of different migratory potentials for differential gene expression analysis.

title: HeLa cells treated and untreated with Clinacanthus nutans DCM fraction
summary: To investigate the effects of C. nutans DCM fraction on HeLa cells using transcriptomic analysis. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of two different condition at two replicates.

title: Cyclin B1 expression as an independent prognostic factor for lung adenocarcinoma and its potential pathways
summary: To investigate the functional mechanism of CCNB1 in lung adenocarcinoma, we knocked down CCNB1 in H1299 cell line and performed sequencing analysis.We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq.

title: RNAseq in breast cancer cells with EBF1 knockdown
summary: Transcriptional analysis of MDA-MB-157 and MDA-MB-436 with EBF1 knockdown

title: Next Generation Sequencing of human first trimester placental EVTs (pEVT), decidual interstitial EVTs (iEVT), and trophoblast organoid (TB-ORG)-derived extravillous trophoblasts (TB-ORG-EVTs).
summary: Aim of the study was to verify signaling pathway-provoked EVT specification in human first trimester placental and decidual tissue. We further provide improvement for in-vitro differentiated TB-ORG-EVTs to more closely mimic in-situ placental EVT geno- and phenotypes.

title: Analysis of   M229-Par and M229-Res cells by Illumina HiSeq instrument (4000 or equivalent)  seq analysis .
summary: Briefly,  Melanoma M229-Par and M229-Res  were analysed for transcriptional changes using RNA seq Analysis.

title: Ribosome profiling and RNA-seq of human corneal epithelial cells upon mild osmotic stress
summary: We present ribosome profiling(for activaly translated RNA) and RNA-seq (for total RNA) data for human corneal epithelial cells exposed to mild osmotic stress (500 mOsm) for 1h and 6h (additionally torin1 (mTOR inhibitor) or MeAIB (SNAT2 inhibitor were added for the last hour of treatment.

title: Cell type-specific gene expression profiles in CNS of patients with DM1
summary: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a multisystem genetic disorder involving the muscle, heart, and central nervous system (CNS). The pathogenesis of CNS symptoms prevalent in patients with DM1 remains unelucidated. To elucidate the CNS pathogenesis in DM1, we investigated cell type-specific abnormalities in cortical neurons, white matter glial cells, and spinal motor neurons of patients with DM1 via laser-capture microdissection(LCM).

title: Transcriptomics analysis of human iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons reveals a novel model for sporadic Parkinson’s disease
summary: First, we differentiated human iPSCs into dopaminergic neurons. To reproduce and to study sporadic PD, the cells were subsequently exposed to increasing concentrations of the neurotoxin MPP+, which is considered the standard for experimentally inducing Parkinsonism. Resulting cells were examined using temporal transcriptomics analysis at various time-points after 24h of exposure. The transcriptomics analysis revealed a strong time- and dose-dependent response with genes overrepresented across pathways involved in PD etiology such as “Parkinson’s Disease”, “Dopaminergic signaling” and “calcium signaling”.

title: RNA demethylase ALKBH5 promotes tumorigenesis in multiple myeloma [RNA-seq]
summary: We here report ALKBH5, a m6A RNA demethylase, as a crucial oncogene in multiple myeloma (MM). Using various MM models, we demonstrated a critical requirement of ALKBH5 for MM cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo. RNA-seq was applied to compare the expression profile of MM cells with or without ALKBh5 knockdown.
design: RNA-seq of RPMI-8226 and CAG cells with or without shRNA-mediated ALKBH5 konckdown

title: Single Transcriptional Factor (PU.1) Efficiently Leads Human iPS Cells to Functional Microglia
summary: We developed an efficient method of generating microglia (hiMGLs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) through forcing the expression of single transcription factor, PU.1. By using this method, we were abled to harvest a great deal of microglia in about three weeks. Transcriptome profile revealed that our hiMGLs well resembled characteristics of human primary microglia. Furthermore, we confirmed that transient over-expression of PU.1 would not change gene expression of microglia in central nervous system or neurological diseases.

title: eIF1-eIF4G1 inhibitors uncover alternative translation activation of stress-response genes via enhanced ribosome loading and 5’UTR translation [MARS-seq]
summary: The Ribo-seq and TI-seq analysis following i14G1s (eI1-eIF4G1 inhibitors) treatments uncover opposing roles of eIF1-eIF4G1 and eIF4E-eIF4G1 in scanning-dependent and independent translation. Furthermore, i14G1s inhibition of eIF4G1-eIF1 resulted in translation activation of ER/UPR stress-response genes via enhanced ribosome loading, elevated 5’UTR translation at near cognate AUGs, and unexpected concomitant upregulation of coding-region translation.

title: RNA-seq of HEK293-TRDMT1-KD and HEK293 control
summary: RNA-seq of 6 samples, 3 of them are TRDMT1 knockdown in HEK293 cells named HEK293-TRDMT1-KD and 3 of them are HEK293 control.

title: Effects of methamphetamine on gene expression in Jurkat, NK-92, THP-1 cells
summary: To investigate the effects of methamphetamine on immune cells, we established three methamphetamine abuse immune cell models. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of 3 different immune cell models.
design: Comparative gene expression profiling analysis of RNA-seq data for immune cells and their methamphetamine-treated (250 μM, 24 h) derivatives.

title: Bulk RNAseq analysis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and the isogenic control
summary: To investigate HCM mutation-associated molecular details at the early stage of disease development, we performed bulk RNA-seq analysis at Day 15 of differentiation using RNA isolated from the isogenic control and mutant hiPSC-CMs. We performed pair-end sequencing with >30 million reads per sample with clean read counts of more than 96% for each sample.

title: Transcriptomic characteristics and impaired immune function of patients with sepsis
summary: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.Although our understanding in the pathophysiological features of sepsis has increased  significantly during the past decades, there is still lack of mechanism of sepis.Neutrophils are important regulators against invading pathogens, and their role during  sepsis has been studied extensively. However, whether neutrophils could inhibit the immune response of CD8+T cells and the mechanism is unkown in sepsis.

title: Pathways and patient-specific gene targets associated with anti-tumor activity of HSP90 inhibitor, SNX2112 in papillary renal cancer
summary: We aimed to use next-generation sequencing that may provide intriguing insights into the molecular pathways mediating anti-tumor activity for HSP90 inhibitor, SNX2112 in papillary renal cancer. Our findings uncovered unique set of target genes and pathways of significance in papillary renal cancer that have potential to be translated into clinically effective therapeutic strategies for patients.
design: Examination of treatment of drug SNX2112 in Papillary renal cell cancer (PRCC).

title: Circular RNA expression analysis of orbital venous malformation [RNA-Seq]
summary: This research aimed to investigate the aberrant expression of circRNA, messenger RNA, and microRNA in orbital venous malformation. A competitive endogenous RNA network was constructed to elucidate their potential roles in orbital venous malformation.

title: RNA sequencing of endoscopic biopsies from patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma
summary: This SuperSeries is composed of the SubSeries listed below.

title: RNA sequencing of Normal Human Fibroblasts and Patient Fibroblasts with Novel SCP2 Variant
summary: The purpose of this study was to identify differentially expressed genes beween normal and SCP2 mutant fibroblasts

title: INSM2 promotes the development of neuroblastoma by regulating lipid metabolism
summary: Lipid metabolism plays important roles in neuroblastoma. To explore INSM2-dependent gene regulation, RNA-seq analysis was performed. Compared with the control group, INSM2 knockdown SK-N-BE(2) cells showed differently expressed genes. We found that INSM2 regulates lipid metabolism to promote the development of neuroblastoma.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of compensated and decompensated human right ventricles
summary: In order to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying right ventricular failure in human PAH, a RNA sequencing analysis was performed in RV tissues obtained from subjects clinically categorized as compensated RV (n=11), decompensated RV (n=7) and donor controls (n=14). The study unveils a plethora of factors dysregulated in the RV of PAH patients, which opens new perspectives for translational research.

title: Combined MEK and JAK/STAT3 pathway inhibition effectively decreases medulloblastoma tumor progression.
summary: RNA sequencing was carried out to identify the signaling pathways and hallmarks that change following MEK and/or JAK/STAT3 pathway inhibition.
design: (1) 2.5x10^5 UI226 cells were injected into the cerebellums of NOD SCID mice. Mice were treated with either vehicle controls of selumetinib twice daily (drug holiday on the weekend) via oral gavage. Tumor were extracted at endpoint and human cells were isolated by FACS with HLA. Human cells from vehicle and selumetinib treated xenografts were subject to RNA-seq. (2) We performed RNA sequencing on selumetinib and/or pacritinib treated UI226 tumorspheres (N=4-6 biological replicates for each condition) to characterize the sustained transcriptomic changes 5 days following treatment in vitro. Tumorspheres were treated with vehicle, selumetinib only, pacritinib only or selumetinib + pacritinib

title: METTL3 inhibits inflammation of retinal pigment epithelium cells by regulating NR2F1 in an m6A-dependent manner [RNA-seq]
summary: To investigate the fuction of METTL3 in autoimmune uveitis, we established ARPE-19 cell lines in which target gene has been knocked down by shRNA. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq between sh-Control groups and sh-METTL3 groups.
design: Comparative gene expression profiling analysis of RNA-seq data for ARPE-19 (sh-Control) cells and its KD derivatives(sh-METTL3).

title: mTORC1 couples SREBP-dependent transcription and splicing of de novo lipid synthesis enzymes via FAM120A  de novo lipid synthesis enzymes via FAM120A
summary: FAM120A as a transcriptional co-activator that couples transcription and splicing of lipid synthesis enzymes downstream of mTORC1-SRPK2 signaling. Mechanistically, the mTORC1-activated SRPK2 phosphorylates a splicing factor SRSF1, enhancing its binding to FAM120A. FAM120A directly interacts with a lipogenic transcription factor SREBP1 at active promoters, thereby bridging newly transcribed lipogenic genes to the RNA splicing machinery.

title: GCB subtype DLBCL with BCL2 translocation
summary: RNA-seq data for 6 de novo GCB subtype DLBCL patients with BCL2 translocation

title: Next-generation Sequencing contributes to Quantitative Analysis of Transcriptomes in circBNC2-KO HK2 cells
summary: Purpose: We idenficied a circRNA, circBNC2, that was downregulated during tubular epithelial cell (TEC) injury. To study the function of circBNC2, we performed CRISPR-Cas9 to knock out circBNC2 in HK2 (a well recognized TEC) cells.  Next-generation Sequencing was used to identified the differentially expressed mRNA between circBNC2-KO HK2 cells and wild-type HK2 cells.

title: Bromodomain targeting overcomes treatment resistance in distinct molecular subtypes of melanoma
summary: NSG mice bearing tumors from the MM-300 PDX line were treated with vehicle or the combination of bromosporine + cobimetinib (bromo+cobi)

title: Transcriptomic analysis of the effects of CDK8 and CDK19 knockout and re-expression and selective CDK8/19  kinase inhibitor Senexin B treatment on gene expression in HEK293 cells
summary: RNA-Seq analysis was carried out to investigate the effects of selective CDK8/19 inhibitor Senexin B (different treatment period) and knockout/re-expression of CDK8 and CDK19 proteins) on gene transcription in HEK293 cells
design: Parental HEK293 cells (WT), CDK8/CDK19 single-knockout derivatives (8KO, 19KO), CDK8/19 double-knockout (dKO), and dKO-reexpression derivatives (dKO-V, dKO-8, dKO-19) were treated with Vehicle control (XXX.C) or 1μM Senexin B (XXX.S) for different period of time (3hr, 5hr, 24hr, 3d and 15d). Each treatment condition was done in biological triplicate.

title: Colonic CD8 T Cell Topography in IBD revealed by Single-Cell Profiling
summary: 10x Chromium 5' single cell RNA-Seq and VDJ sequencing of colonic CD8+ T cell cell populations in health and Ulcerative Colitis in human patients.

title: BRD4 promotes gastric cancer progression and metastasis through acetylation-dependent stabilization of Snail
summary: The puropose of this study is to reveal a noncanonical post-transcriptional regulatory function of BRD4 that maintains cancer growth and dissemination, with immediate translational implication for treating metastatic malignancies with clinically available bromodomain inhibitors. The next-generation RNA sequencing was used to confirm the transcriptom overlapping change after BRD4 and Snail knockout separately.
design: mRNA profiles of gastric cancer cells which were generated by depletion of control, Snail and BRD4 were generated by deep sequencing, in triplicate, using Illumina hiseqxten .

title: Identifying Novel Molecules Implicated in Early Mesendoderm Specification by a Broad Transcriptomic Approach
summary: H1 embryonic Stem Cells maintained in pluripotency by Activin A and  induced with BMP4
design: H1 cells were adapted to Activin A based mTeSR for at least 10 passages. The cells were subsequently split in 3 full 6-well plates and incubated in the same medium until they reached approximately 50% confluency. At that point, the cells were induced with 50ng/mL BMP4 for 1hr or 4hrs. A full 6-well plate served as a non-induced control. RNA was extracted from all the conditions with the experiment being repeated 3 times using cells from three consecutive passages for statistical significance.

title: Context-dependent genetic effects on gene expression
summary: We profiled genome-wide gene expression levels across 12 cellular environments using 544 immortalized B cell (lymphoblastoid) lines from the 1000 Genomes Project.
design: mRNA-seq of RNA extracted from lymphoblastoid cell lines

title: Transcriptomic analysis of LN229 cell treated by unit of bortezomib and panobinostat
summary: We report the application of  unit of bortezomib and panobinostat on LN229 cell , and further explored the mechanism of drugs on GBM cells.

title: Comparison of NAT-lncRNA knockout effect by next-generation sequencing
summary: Analysis of different expression after lncRNA DHRS4-AS1 knockout with two strategies in immortalized human pancreatic duct epithelial cell line HPDE6-C7. The strategies include promoter-exon1 (PE) and branch point and 3‘ splicing site (BESST). The results provide transcriptome comparison between PE and BESST knockout approach, indicating the superior effect of BESST.

title: Bulk and single cell profiling of the transcriptional response to Trichostatin A and Valproic Acid using CAGE
summary: To better understand the transcriptomic changes that occur in response to HDACi treatment, we perform CAGE on dermal fibroblasts, HepG2, and MCF7 cells after TSA or VPA treatment, at both bulk and single cell level. We make detailed annotation of the identified coding and noncoding RNA transcription start sites and enhancers, in addition to their expression levels.
design: Overall, 3 cell types are subjected to 3 different treatments, including control, TSA, and VPA. For bulk CAGE, 3 replicates of each cell type x treatment were made. For C1 CAGE,

title: Next Generation Sequencing Facilitates Quantitative Analysis Transcriptomes of dHL-60 cells after capsaicin processed
summary: To uncoverthe capsaicin effects on the neutrophil activation, we performed transcriptomic of dHL-60 cells after capsaicin stimulation in degree of different time. this study revealed the functional changes of neutrophils in the presence of capsaicin. The transcriptomic data with different time stimulation gradients can contribute to the revealing of dynamic alternation in gene expression and annotate the time-dependent effect of the neutrophil respond to capsaicin.

title: Multiomics analyses reveal the mechanical-stress-dependent changes in trabecular meshwork cytoskeletal-extracellular matrix interactions
summary: The purpose of this study was to understand the response of trabecular meshwork under mechanical stretch using a multi-omics approach.
design: Gene expression analysis of trabecular meshwork cells subjected to cyclic mechanical stretch compared to unstretched controls. Primary HTM cell cultures were subjected to 15% stretching at 0.69 Hz frequency for 8 h for mRNA sequencing analysis.

title: Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) analysis in control and melatonin treated human coronary artery endothilial cells (HCAECs).
summary: To explore the detailed mechanism by which melatonin allivates TNF-α induced HCAECs damage, we performed RNA-seq in control and melatonin treated HCAECs, and identified 213 upregualted and 103 downregulated genes with the criterion of |FC|≥2 and p≤0.05.
design: We prepared 3 replicates for control and melatonin group, respectively, to perform the RNA-seq analysis.

title: Transcriptome  analysis of YTHDF2 kockdown(KD) and wildtype(WT) cells in Multiple Myeloma
summary: RNA-seq experiments was conducted to analyze changes in related signaling pathways and gene expression in colon cancer cells when YTHDF2 was knocked down.

title: NMT inhibition in the context of MYC levels
summary: Characterisation of the impact of 24 hours of NMT inhibition (100 nM IMP1088) on the P493-6 cell line with medium levels of MYC and high levels of MYC.

title: Establishment of radioresistant U87MG glioblastoma cell line
summary: To explore factors contributing to radioresistance in GBM, we established GBM radioresistant cell line using U87MG human GBM cells.
design: Comparative gene expression profiling analysis of RNA-seq data for U87MG cell liness and its radioresistant cell lines.

title: RNA sequencing and integrative analysis reveal pathways and hub genes associated with TGFβ1 stimulation on prostatic stromal cells (PrSCs)
summary: To examine the effect of TGFβ1 on prostatic stromal cells, we firstly isolated primary prostatic stromal cells from five benign prostatic hyperplasia sample. Then RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to reveal important pathways and hub genes associated with TGFβ1 stimulation on PrSCs.

title: RNA sequencing of HECTD3 knockdown during TNFalpha stimulation in primary HUVEC cells
summary: We isolated and validated primary HUVECs from the neonatal umbilical cord vein, and performed genome-wide expression analysis to profile differentially expressed genes in control and HECTD3-KD HUVECs treated with or without TNFα for 2 hours. Compared with control HUVECs, 59 genes showed lower expression in HECTD3-KD HUVECs in response to TNFα. Most of them are NF-κB target genes, including adhesion molecules SELE (E-selectin), ICAM-1, and VCAM-1.

title: Hepatic senescence is associated with clinical progression of NAFLD/NASH: Role of BMP4 and its antagonist Gremlin1 (Hepatocytes)
summary: We performed RNA sequencing of IHH cells incubated with GREM1 in order to identify novel genes and their associated biological pathways.

title: Hepatic senescence is associated with clinical progression of NAFLD/NASH: Role of BMP4 and its antagonist Gremlin1 (Visceral adipose cells)
summary: To understand the role of adipose tissue senescence in NAFLD/NASH,  RNA sequencing was performed in the visceral adipose tissue of NAFLD and NASH pateints.

title: Melatonin alters the transcriptome of human granulosa cells and improves fertilization and blastocyst formation
summary: Granulosa cells in the ART cycle before and during melatonin treatment from the three patients and analyzed the transcriptome changes by RNA-sequence. The other four patients had good ART outcomes. Their GCs were also subjected to RNA-sequence as controls of good ART outcomes.
design: mRNA profiles of human granulosa cells in the ART cycle

title: RNA-seq analysis of nasopharyngeal swabs from asymptomatic and mildly symptomatic COVID-19 patients
summary: We used total RNA of nasopharyngeal swabs from COVID-19 patients to identify their gene expression profile. Multiple biological process were significantly enriched in either asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic patients. These significantly expressed genes were suggested to contribute to the severity of the disease. We also performed metagenomics analysis to identify differences in the microbiome profile of the two groups of patients.

title: Biological effect of azacitidine (CC-486) on diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
summary: Biomarker study for a phase 1, Open-Label, multicenter trial of azacitidine (CC-486) plus R-CHOP in subjects with high-risk previously untreated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
design: RNA and DNA methylation profiles of DLBCL tissue samples and CD3+ circulating cells methylation profiles pre and post CC486 treatment were generated by Illumina sequencing. *Please note that authors has not provided the 'pre and post CC486 treatment' status for each Sample record.

title: Effect of formoterol and tumor necrosis factor (TNFα) alone and in combination on gene expression changes in human primary bronchial epithelial cells: a comparison with forskolin treatment
summary: RNA sequencing was performed to study the genomic effects of formoterol, a long acting β2-adrenoceptor agonist, alone and in combination with the pro-inflammatory cytokine, TNFα in human primary bronchial epithelial cells, and to compare its effect to forskolin. Our results show that formoterol promoted a profound genomic response alone and on background of an inflammatory stimulus. Moreover, formoterol and forskolin regulated transcriptomes were highly rank order correlated which suggests that formoterol-mediated gene expression changes are cAMP dependent
design: Human primary bronchial epithelial cells obtained by proteinase digestion of non-transplanted, normal airways of five lung donors obtained from a tissue retrieval service at the International Institute for the Advancement of Medicine (Edison, NJ, USA), were grown as monolayers in submersion culture. Confluent cells were cultured for 1, 2, 6 and 18 h with vehicle, TNFα (10 ng ml-1), formoterol (1 nM), TNFα and formoterol in combination or forskolin (10 µM). Total RNA was extracted, quantified, processed into mRNA libraries, and sequenced across five high-throughput sequencing kits on a NextSeq 500 instrument (Illumina).

title: HLA-B*46 associates with rapid HIV disease progression in  Asian cohorts and prominent differences in NK cell phenotype
summary: In an unbiased transcriptomic screen we observed reduced NK cell activation phenotypes in HLA-B*46 positive people with HIV. These findings show that contemporaneous treated cohorts can be used to analyze host genetic effects in HIV disease, and support a role for NK cells in HIV control revealed by unique properties of the recombinant HLA-B*46 allele which is frequent only in Asia.

title: High-fidelity Cas13 variants for targeted RNA degradation with minimal collateral effects
summary: We found that several variants with 2-4 mutations on Higher Eukaryotes and Prokaryotes Nucleotide-binding (HEPN) domains showed undiminished on-target activity but markedly reduced collateral effects. Furthermore, transcriptome-wide off-target effects and cell growth arrest induced by wild-type Cas13d were found to be absent for a Cas13d variant. Thus, high-fidelity Cas13 variants with minimal collateral effects are now available for the targeted degradation of RNAs in basic research and therapeutic applications.
design: We have designed a dual-fluorescent reporter system that revealed substantial collateral effects of Cas13-mediated RNA knockdown of both exogenous and endogenous genes in mammalian cells. This reporter system was used to screen over 200 Cas13 variants obtained by structure-guided mutagenesis. To study transcriptome-wide off-target effect induced by wild-type Cas13d (RfxCas13d) and its absence in cfCas13d ( named hfCas13d in the publication) variant, we designed a three groups experiment using HEK293 cell lines, including an inactive dead Cas13d control (dCas13d with gRNA targeting endogenous genes), a wild-type Cas13d treatment groups (Cas13d with the corresponding gRNA targeting endogenous genes) and a "collateral cleavage-free" Cas13d treatment groups (cfCas13d  with the corresponding gRNA targeting endogenous genes). We chose 2 gRNAs targeting PPIA, and 1 gRNA each targeting RPL4, CA2, or PPARG, respectively. Three replicates were prepared for each group for whole transcriptome sequencing. We finally have 44 RNAseq samples in total, three for each groups except one sample missing in cfCas13d for targeting PPIA with gRNA g1.

title: Mitochondrial protease Lonp1 localizes to the nucleus in response to heat shock
summary: We analyzed the effects of Lonp1 silencing on the response to heat shock by analyzing the transriptomic profile of SW620 colon cancer cells undergoing heat shock. Briefly, Lonp1 has been silenced by using a specific siRNA, then cells have been kept at 42°C for 1 hour, and left at 37°C for one hour.

title: Gene regulation by m6A demethylase ALKBH5 in osteosarcoma [RNA-seq]
summary: To identify target genes regulated by ALKBH5 in osteosarcoma,  we silenced the expression of ALKBH5 in osteosarcoma cell line-143B and tested its effect on 143B transcriptome.

title: RNA sequencing of undifferentiated and differentiated SH SY5Y cells
summary: DNA topoisomerase IIB has an important role in ligand mediated transcriptional regulation of gene expression. SH-SY5Y  is a neuroblastoma cell line that can be induced to differentiate into neuronal-like cells in response to retinoic acid. In this study TOP2B has been knocked out using crispr-cas9 to determine the role of TOP2B in the transcriptional response to retinoic acid. RNA was prepared from untreated wild type and TOP2B null SH-SY5Y cells and from cells exposed to 10 uM All Trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA) for 24 hours.
design: 4 replicates of each of  untreated WT, untreated TOP2B-/- , ATRA treated WT and ATRA treated TOP2B-/-

title: Chronic responses to direct Ras-targetted therapies
summary: To investigate the response of H358 lung cancer cells to long term treatment with a panel of direct Ras and Ras pathway inhibitors. H358 cells harbour a heterozygous G12C mutation of KRAS.

title: Assessing Radiation Therapy induced changes in Androgen Receptor Pathway activity using hK2-targeted PET imaging
summary: To investigate the effects of external beam radiation therapy on androgen receptor pathway transcriptomic expression in prostate cancer, we performed RNAseq on EBRT-treated LNCAP xenograft tumors.
design: Gene expression was compared between untreated LNCAP tumors and EBRT-treated tumors using data from RNAsequencing.

title: Circular and fusion RNAs in medulloblastoma development
summary: The expression of circular RNAs in cerebellar cancer versus medulloblastoma subgroups SHH, WNT, Group3 and Group4 has been interrogated. Fusion RNAs containing exons from distinct genes joined at canonical splice sites were also identified.

title: IL-6 driven pSTAT1 response is linked to T cell features implicated in early immune dysregulation
summary: Here, we performed an in-depth characterization of the effect of classic IL-6 signaling in primary human T cells from healthy individuals. We generated a detailed map of IL-6 signaling in CD4+ and CD8+ naïve and memory T cell subsets, linking mbIL-6R expression levels to the magnitude and balance of phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3 and the transcriptomics response to IL-6 in these subsets.
design: Primary human CD3+ T cells derived from healthy donors with the rs2228145 AA genotype were cultured with or without IL-6 (20 ng/mL) for 4 hours and the transcriptomic response to IL-6 signaling was determined in flow sorted T cell subsets including CD4+ naïve (CD4+CD45RA+), CD4+ memory (CD4+CD45RO+) and CD8+ naive (CD8+CD45RA+) T cells.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of the Transcriptome-Wide m6A Methylome in Lung Adenocarcinoma by MeRIP Sequencing
summary: To investigate the role of m6A modification,MeRIP-seq was used to identify differential m6A modifications in lung adenocarcinoma .

title: Transcriptomic analysis of adrenergic and mesenchymal neuroblastoma cells using RNA-sequencing
summary: RNA-sequencing was performed on the following human neuroblastoma cell lines: Kelly, NBL-S, CHP-212, SH-SY5Y, SH-SY5Y LDK-resistant and SH-EP.

title: Effect of depletion of UHRF1, DNMT1, DNMT3B during differentiation
summary: To investigate gene regulation by UHRF1, DNMT1, DNMT3B in THP-1 cells during differentiation, we established stable knockdown THP-1 cell lines.

title: Maggot extracts overcome cisplatin resistance of ovarian cancer cells by targeting HSP90AB1/IGF1R signaling
summary: To investigate the main mechanism underlying cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer, A2780/CDDP and SKOV3/CDDP cell lines were treated with both maggot extracts and cisplatin. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of A2780 and A2780/CDDP cells.

title: Gene expression profile of monocytes from healthy donor and triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) co-cultured with FAP and CD29 [bulk RNA-seq]
summary: These samples were either treatment naive or samples co-cultured with FAP and CD29. Myeloid cell subpopulation comprises denditric cells (DC), monocytes and macrophages. We used RNA sequencing to analyze the response of monocytes to FAP/CD29 co-culture.

title: RNA-Seq analysis for giant cell tumour of the bone
summary: CircRNA sequencing was performed on 5 pairs of giant cell tumors of bone and their adjacent tissues.

title: Enforced MAB21L4 expression enhances epidermal diferentiation
summary: RNA-seq was used to define the role of MAB21L4 in epidermal differentiation by placing primary human keratinocytes transduced to overexpress MAB21L4 onto human dermis and grown for three days at the air-liquid interface to generate organotypic skin tissue.

title: CACYBP is required for epidermal homeostasis
summary: RNA-seq was used to define the role of CACYBP in epidermal differentiation by first employing CRISPR/Cas9 to disrupt CACYBP with two independent single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) to create pools of CACYBP-ablated primary human keratinocytes that were immortalized with HPV E6/E7 and then placed onto human dermis and grown for three days at the air-liquid interface to generate organotypic skin tissue.

title: Role of FGF-2 induced non-coding RNA in cancer [II]
summary: We show that IER3 and IER3-AS1 protein coding and non-coding genes mediates oncogenic properties in cancer cell lines when they are induced by FGF-2 which is fibroblast growth factor. Comprehensive analysis of mechanisms behind the regulation of these genes by FGF-2 induction is shown in this study.

title: Role of FGF-2 induced non-coding RNA in cancer [I]
summary: We show that IER3 and IER3-AS1 protein coding and non-coding genes mediates oncogenic properties in cancer cell lines when they are induced by FGF-2 which is fibroblast growth factor. Comprehensive analysis of mechanisms behind the regulation of these genes by FGF-2 induction is shown in this study.

title: Investigating human T cell development in the human pediatric thymus using scRNA-seq
summary: To study human T cell development at the single cell level we profiled thymocytes from 3 pediatric donors using scRNA-seq. The data was subsequently used in the construction of a cell atlas of human thymic development across the life span. This allowed the identification of over 50 cell states in the human thymus and helped map the developmental trajectories of conventional and unconventional T cells throughout development.

title: High Expression Level of ROR1 and ROR1-signaling Associates With Venetoclax Resistance In Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
summary: We examined the CLL cells transcriptome data of six patients who fail to clear their leukemia cells and develop progressive disease on venetoclax therapy. Methods: CLL cells were collected prior to venetoclax therapy (Sample Collection 1 (SC1)) and then more than 1 year later (Sample Collection 2 (SC2)). Negative isolation of CLL cells to ≥95% purity was performed prior to RNA isolation.
design: Transcriptome profiles of CLL cells prior to venetoclax therapy and more than 1 year later on venetoclax

title: T cell transriptome in chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
summary: We performed transcriptome analysis via RNA sequencing of T cells isolated from participants with and without 22qDS and T cells of 22qDS participants with low or normal number of T cells.

title: Oxidative stress alters transcript localization of disease-causing genes in the retinal pigment epithelium
summary: To evaluate the effect of oxidative stress on transcript localization in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), we performed poly-A RNA sequencing on nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions from induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal pigment epithelium (iPSC-RPE) cells exposed to hydrogen peroxide, as well as untreated controls.
design: RNASeq analysis of nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions from control iPSRPE cells and iPSRPE cells subjected to hydrogen peroxide

title: Transcriptome analysis of eutopic endometrium stromal cells by RNA-sequencing in patients with adenomyosis
summary: To identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and molecular pathways in eutopic endometrial stroma cells (EuESCs) from adenomyosis patients and provide a new insight into disease mechanisms at transcriptome level.Gene expression profiling of normal endometrial stromal cells (N-ESCs) and adenomyotic eutopic endometrial stroma cells (A-EuESCs) were analyzed by using RNA-sequencing.

title: RNA-seq analysis of sporadic and Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome-associated odontogenic keratocysts (OKCs)
summary: The aim of this study was to decode the gene expression program characterizing odontogenic keratocyst (OKC) development, by performing a comprehensive transcriptomics analysis applied on whole OKC tissue derived from sporadic and Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome (BCNS)-associated OKCs, and control samples of pericoronal tissues of impacted teeth (dental follicles, DFs) derived from healthy individuals.

title: Analysis of gene expression in lung adenocarcinoma cells following ectopic expression of proliferation-suppressive lncRNAs (PSLR).
summary: RNA-sequencing was performed to gain insight into the transcriptome-wide molecular changes induced by FAM198B-AS1 (PSLR-1) or SEPTIN9-DT (PSLR-2) ectopic expression in lung adenocarcinoma cells. Following expression of PSLR-1 or PSLR-2 lncRNA or control RNA, RNA-sequencing was performed. This high-throughput data revealed elevated expression of these lncRNAs reduced the expression of genes and pathways known to induce proliferation in lung adenocarcinoma cells.

title: Construction and comprehensive analysis of the ceRNA network to reveal key genes for benign tracheal stenosis.
summary: Whole transcriptome sequencing was performed on blood samples collected from patients with benign tracheal stenosis and normal controls. To explore the possible biological functions of the differentially expressed genes in patients with benign tracheal stenosis, and to provide a valuable molecular basis for investigating the pathogenesis of benign tracheal stenosis.

title: Gene-regulatory potential of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 and D2
summary: In this study, we compared the modulation of the transcriptome of human PBMCs by the vitamin D metabolites 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (25(OH)D3), 25(OH)D2 and 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25(OH)2D3).
design: PBMCs of a healthy male donor were isolated within one hour after peripheral blood collection and treated for 4, 8 or 24 h either with 1,25(OH)2D3 (0.1, 1 and 10 nM), 25(OH)2D3 (100, 250, 500, 750 and 1000 nM), 25(OH)D2 (100, 250, 500, 750 and 1000 nM) or solvent (0.1% EtOH).

title: Innate immune role of Rnd1 during H5N1 infection
summary: Intracellular and cell surface molecules are an essential part of the innate immune system. We describe a novel cellular defense mechanism based upon a membrane-associated protein RND1. RND1 belongs to the Rho GTPase family, but unlike other members, it is constitutively active. We show that RND1 is induced by pro-inflammatory cytokines during viral and bacterial infections and provides protection against these pathogens through two distinct mechanisms.

title: Delamination of trophoblast-like syncytia from the amniotic ectodermal analogue in human primed embryonic stem cell-based differentiation model [RNA-seq]
summary: Human embryonic stem cells were converted into GATA3-expressing extraembryonic cells (GATA3+ ExE cells) when they were exposed to chemical inhibitors for ACTIVIN/NODAL (A83-01, 1uM) and FGF signaling (PD03714, 100nM). We refer here to this inhibitor-induced differentiation method as an 'AP' protocol. To understand the transcriptome dynamics during AP-induced differentiation, we performed timecourse profiling of genome-wide gene expression by RNA sequencing.

title: Adult type Maturation of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Derived Cardiomyocytes
summary: Cardiac tissue constructs from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) have been  heralded for their possibilities to serve as disease models, utilized in drug screening and cardiac  regeneration. That potential remains to be realized because human iPSC derived cardiomyocytes  (hiPSC-CMs) are immature, and do not reflect the characteristics of adult human myocytes. Here,  we present a method to accelerate hiPSC-CM maturation by maintaining them on a substrate,  Cardiac Mimetic Matrix (CMM), which mimics the adult human heart matrix ligand chemistry  and submicron ultrastructure.

title: Different transcriptomic response to T. cruzi infection in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from Chagas disease patients with and without chronic cardiomyopathy
summary: Investigate transcriptional responses of T. cruzi infected hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from chagasic patients with and without cardiomyopathy.

title: Single-cell sequencing of infusion products and T cells after administration of non-viral PD1-targeted anti-CD19 CAR T cells
summary: We successfully developed a two-in-one approach to generate non-viral genome specific targeted CAR T cells through CRISPR/Cas9. In the adoptive therapy for relapsed/refractory aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, we observed durable responses without serious adverse events and complete remission in patients treated with PD1 knockin CAR T cells. Here we applied single-cell sequencing to analyze the characteristcis of infusion products and T cells after administration.

title: Transcriptional effects of YAP/TAZ knockdown in human fibroblasts
summary: We compared the transcriptomes of control and YAP/TAZ-depleted fibroblasts, in the presence or absence of cGAS or STING depletion

title: EZH2 KO RNA-seq in HSC-5 cells
summary: CRISPR was used to deplete EZH2 in HSC-5 cells. RNA-seq was then carried out to identify changes in the transcriptome following EZH2 loss in these cells. Critically, we identified TP63 to be downregulated in the EZH2-depleted cells, and also RUNX3 to be significantly upregulated.

title: The novel circle-RNA ZNF208 regulates the proliferation of cervical cancer fibroblasts through a ceRNA network
summary: Cervical cancer is one of the major cancers that threaten the health of women. CircRNA is an important factor in the regulation of cancer development and progression. The role of circRNA in cervical cancer is less well studied. The aim of this study was to explore the mechanism of circRNA effects on cervical cancer using circRNA-seq technology to study the expression profile data of 9 pairs of primary cervical cancer and paracancerous tissues.

title: Targeted degradation of GSPT1 causes TP53-independent cell death in leukemia whilst sparing normal stem cells
summary: To investigate the effect of drugs that degrade GSTP1 on leukemia cell biology.

title: 4hpi - 6wpi Gene Expression in HCMV-Infected Primary Human Monocytes
summary: To investigate how HCMV alters monocyte gene expression over time, we collected RNA from HCMV-infected primary human monocytes (3 donors) from 4 hours to 6 weeks post infection and analyzed the differential gene expression by RNAseq.
design: Primary human monocytes were mock-infected or HCMV-infected. RNA was collected at 4 hpi, 24 hpi, 2 wpi, 4 wpi, and 6 wpi. 3 replicates are included.

title: Targeting ESR1 mutation-induced transcriptional addiction with BET inhibition
summary: We investigated the therapeutic potential of BET inhibition to target ESR1 mutation-induced “transcriptional addiction” in ER-positive breast cancer. Our studies show that ESR1 mutant (Y537S and D538G) cells activate unique transcriptional programs that are targeted by OTX015, a BET inhibitor

title: Developing High-Affinity Decoy Receptor Optimized for Multiple Myeloma and Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma Treatment [RNA-seq]
summary: This study demonstrates the dichotomous activities of APRIL and BAFF in MM and DLBCL, which can be safely targeted by an engineered fusion protein designed to trap both ligands with ultrahigh binding affinity.

title: Measuring the transcriptomic response to targeting kinases correlated with estrogen receptor activity in Breast Cancer
summary: We undertook a phosophotranscriptomic network analysis of published patient tumour RNA-seq and phosphoproteomic data to identify kinases that correltated with Estrogen Receptor activity in Breast Cancer. The most sucessful canidates were selected for targeting by siRNA and the effects monitored by RNA-seq.  The code for generation of the expression matrix is available from https://github.com/andrewholding/SimonaVIPER
design: Expression data characterising the effects of siRNAs targeting CAMK2D, CDK8, CSNK1A1, ESR1, GRB2, HIPK4, KSR1, LIMK1, MKNK2, NEK9 in both MCF7 and T47D.

title: Allele-specific gene regulation, phenotypes, and therapeutic vulnerabilities in estrogen receptor alpha mutant endometrial cancer
summary: This SuperSeries is composed of the SubSeries listed below.

title: Effect of depletion of alt-LAMA3 on gene expression of HEK293T cells
summary: To investigate the depletion of altLAMA3, we established HEK293T cell lines in which alt-LAMA3 gene has been knocked out by CRISPR-Cas9. We then performed gene expression profiling analysis using data obtained from RNA-seq of 2 different cells

title: Inhibition of EZH2 with GSK343 in the LIMe-Hi-C K562 clone
summary: We characterized the the effect of EZH2 inhibition on gene expression in the LIMe-Hi-C K562 clone
design: For RNA-seq preparation, the M.CviPI-Lamin-B1 inducible K562 clone was treated in triplicate with either with vehicle (DMSO 0.1% v/v) or GSK343 (1µM) for 72 hours and induced with doxcycline (1µg/mL) for the final 24 hours of the drug treatments. Upon completion of the treatments, RNA was isolated and sequenced to assess changes in transcription.

title: Asparagine starvation on histone methylation and gene expression
summary: We are determining the impact of asparagine starvation on histone H3K4 trimethylation deposition across the genome and how they may affect the gene expression.

title: Genome-wide analysis of KSHV splicing regulation by ORF57
summary: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated virus (KSHV) ORF57 is a viral RNA-binding protein required for proper posttranscriptional processing of viral transcripts including RNA splicing. To identify the viral splicing events regulated by ORF57 we performed a genome-wide analysis of RNA splicing of viral RNAs in wild type (WT) versus ORF57 knock-out (57KO) primary effusion lymphoma cells line BCBL-1 after induction of KSHV lytic replication by 24h treatment with valproic acid (VA).
design: The obtained reads were mapped to human/KSHV chimeric genome by STAR aligner to identify KSHV splicing events. To detemine ORF57 activity on viral RNA splicing, we compared the number of splice reads mapped to unique splicing junction in WT versus 57KO BCBL-1 cells.

title: Transcriptional response to PORCN inhibition using an in vivo model of RNF43 mutant pancreatic adenocarcinoma (HPAF-II) in EP300 knockout and WT cells
summary: RNF43-mutant pancreatic tumors are driven by Wnt signaling and sensitive to Wnt inhibition, e.g. PORCN inhibitors. However, some RNF43-mutant pancreatic cancers are intrinsically resistant to Wnt inhibition. We identified that EP300 mutations confer resistance to PORCN inhibitors in RNF43-mutant pancreatic cancers. We found that EP300 knockout down-regulated GATA6 expression and GATA6-regulated differentiation program, making the anti-differentiation roles of Wnt signaling dispensable.
design: To decipher the underlying drug resistance mechanisms, we performed transcriptome analysis in EP300 wildtype and knockout HPAF-II orthotopic xenografts treated with vehicle or PORCN inhibitor ETC-159 (5 mg/kg q.d. x 3 days or 15 mg/kg q.d. x 3days). Orthotopic tumors were harvested 8 hours post the last dose (56 hours of treatment). Total RNAs were extracted and subjected to RNA-seq.

title: Annotation of estrogen-regulated enhancer RNAs
