summary: LRGASP_WTC11  For data usage terms and conditions, please refer to http://www.genome.gov/27528022 and http://www.genome.gov/Pages/Research/ENCODE/ENCODE_Data_Use_Policy_for_External_Users_03-07-14.pdf

title: total RNA-seq from foreskin keratinocyte (ENCSR527SSD)
summary: RiboZero RNA-seq on primary keratinocytes in day 6 of differentiation  For data usage terms and conditions, please refer to http://www.genome.gov/27528022 and http://www.genome.gov/Pages/Research/ENCODE/ENCODE_Data_Use_Policy_for_External_Users_03-07-14.pdf

title: Transcription and splicing kinetics are coordinated within both genes and higher-order chromatin domains [dataset2]
summary: In this study, we performed mRNA sequencing on IMR90 and A549 cells in order to understand the differences in gene expression patterns and alternative splicing patterns between the two cell lines.

title: Ex vivo scRNA-Seq of CD4+ cells in T-bet deficiency and wild type
summary: Starting from frozen PBMCs of a patient with T-bet deficiency and a wild type control, CD4+ cells were enriched by magnetic sorting. The cells were either activated with plate-bound anti-CD3/anti-CD28 monoclonal antibodies for 14 hours or left untreated. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) was performed to study differentially expressed genes in the T helper cell compartment in T-bet deficiency.

title: Differences in vaginal microbiota, host transcriptome and proteins in women with bacterial vaginosis are associated with metronidazole treatment response
summary: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) treatment failures or recurrences are common. To identify features associated with treatment response, we compared vaginal microbiota and host ectocervical transcriptome before and after oral metronidazole therapy. Response to metronidazole is characterized by significant changes in chemokines and related transcripts suggesting that strategies to promote these pathways may prove beneficial.

title: RNAseq analysis of PS+ vs PS- non-naive CD8 T cells sorted from peripheral blood of COVID-19 patients
summary: We report the transcriptional profile of phosphatidylserine (PS) positive and PS negative non-naive peripheral blood CD8 T cells from patients infected with SARS-CoV-2. PS+ CD8 T cells showed increased expression of cell cyclce and cell division associated genes and reduced expression of genes regulating translational initiation, when compared to PS- CD 8 T cells. Furthermore, PS+ CD8 T cells show increased expression of effector T cell genes.

title: Drug Combination Signatures for Prediction and Mitigation of Toxicity.
summary: Baseline transcriptomic signatures of cardiomyocytes differentiated from hiPSC lines generated from clinically well-characterized, diverse healthy human individuals. We provide mRNAseq data of various replicate samples of cardiomyocytes differentiated from 6 hiPSC lines.

title: Elevated HIV trans-infection of CD4 T cells in MRKAd5 vaccine recipients due to CD8 T cells targeting of adapted epitopes
summary: We report the application of single-cell-based RNA sequencing technology for high-throughput profiling of antigen specific CD8 T cells induced by MRKAd5 vaccine (HVTN502 trial). Based on the transcriptomic data, we identified 68 differentially expressed genes comparing adapted versus non-adapted epitope specific CD8 T cells. Interestingly, CLOCK and HNF1B, which are critical for circadian rhythm, were found to be upregulated in both recipients with the non-adapted epitope specific CD8 T cell responses.

title: Gene expression analysis of neurons differentiated from iPS cells generated from the fibroblasts of monozygotic twins discordant for schizophrenia
summary: Schizophrenia is heterogenious and polygenic disorder, and thus obtaining geneticly close control samples are valuable to increase the effect size. We obtained skin biopsies from five identical twin pairs discordant for schizophrenia and reprogrammed the cells to induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). They are all Finnish/Caucasians, and the study was approved by ethical commitee in Finland. As schizophrenia affects mostly cognitive functions, we differentiated iPSCs to cortical neurons, moslty excitatory glutamatergic neurons and performed RNA sequencing for transcriptomic changes in neurons from patients with schizophrenia.

title: MAML3 overexpression in neuroendocrine cell lines
summary: The goal of this study was to determine differentially regulated pathways in neuroendocrine cells (SK-N-SH, BON-1, QGP-1) that over-expressed full length or exon 1 deleted MAML3 compared with vector control.

title: Multiplexed transcriptome-based profiling of drug combinations using deterministic barcoding in picolitre-sized droplets [large_scale_drug_screen]
summary: K562 cells were perturbed with drug combinations for 12h in droplets. Subsequently cells were processed to generate libraries for RNA-Seq.

title: Targeted RNA sequencing of archived giant cell arteritis temporal artery biopsies reveals viral signatures
summary: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) temporal artery sections from GCA subjects were stained for VZV antigen. Samples testing positive (VZV+) and negative (VZV-) from both GCA and control subjects without GCA were analyzed by targeted RNA sequencing of the whole-human transcriptome (BioSpyder TempO-Seq™).

title: Multiplexed transcriptome-based profiling of drug combinations using deterministic barcoding in picolitre-sized droplets [small_scale_drug_screen]
summary: K562 cells were perturbed with drug combinations for 12h in droplets. Subsequently cells were processed to generate libraries for RNA-Seq.
design: Small drug screens followed by RNA-Seq, with 16 combinatorial treatment conditions (small_scale_matrix).  The barcoding scheme on the microfluidic pipeline was changed and therefore  a total of six raw files (2x 3 replicates). For each replicate in the two screen, an additional separate control was performed called DMSO_[1-3]_dT or DMSO _[1-3]_BIO.

title: Comparisons of Nasal Polyp ASC, Nasal polyp IgD+ (naïve-like) B cells, and Blood naïve B cells
summary: Here we investigate the transcriptional landscapes of nasal polyp IgD+ (naïve-like) B cells, nasal polyp ASC, and blood naïve B cells using RNA-seq.  These data found that nasal polypP IgD+ naïve-like B cells are activated and similar to nasal polyp ASC and distinct from circulating B cells in the blood.

title: KIF15  confers resistance to enzalutamide in castration resistant prostate cancer [RNA-Seq]
summary: The aim of this research was to confirm the regulatory effect of KIF15 on gene expression in castration resistant prostate cancer.

title: Mapping translation in wild-type and METTL5 knockout (KO) HepG2 cells
summary: We performed ribosome profiling on wild-type and METTL5 KO HepG2 cells to investigate translation changes due to loss of METTL5.

title: Characterization of Early Gilteritinib Resistant Cell Lines
summary: Expression analysis performed on Early Gilteritinib Resistant cell lines vs Acute (48hr) treatment and MOLM14 Parental

title: Single cell RNA sequencing of CD41+ and CD41- CD34+ HPC in model of RUNX1 insufficiency
summary: To gain insights into the global and local transcriptomic changes underlying defects in adult RUNX1in HSPCs, we then performed scRNA SEQ on sorted CD41a- and CD41a+ HSPCs from cultures expressing NT or RUNX1-targeting lentiviral shRNA.
design: Examination of gene expression in 12 sorted samples from control  (3 CD41- and 3 CD41+) and RUNX1 haploinsufficient (3 CD41- and 3 CD41+) iHPCs based on CD42 expression.

title: BCL11B enhancer hijacking defines a subtype of lineage ambiguous stem cell leukemia
summary: This SuperSeries is composed of the SubSeries listed below.

title: CRISPR Screening of CAR T Cells and Cancer Stem Cells Reveals Critical Dependencies for Cell-Based Therapies
summary: This SuperSeries is composed of the SubSeries listed below.

title: RNA-seq of human gastric cancer
summary: We compared transcriptomic profiles of gastric carcinomas between patients carrying the ATG16L1 T300A SNP and patients without the SNP.

title: Distal regulation mediated Core Transcriptional Regulatory Circuitry in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma [RNA-seq]
summary: In esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), the core regulatory circuitry is ill-defined and the limited clinical approaches are available currently for the treatment of ESCC. Here, using enhancer profiling and CRC programme, we generated ESCC-dependent epigenomic-transcriptional regulatory circuitry, elaborated the exquisite work model mediated by core TFs and SEs through physical interaction between enhancers and promoter, and identified the crucial target of ESCC regulatory network.

title: Cortical Overgrowth in a Preclinical Forebrain Organoid Model of CNTNAP2-Associated Autism Spectrum Disorder
summary: We performed bulk-RNAseq on 8-week-old forebrain organoids grown from 3 patient derived cell lines and 3 control derived cell lines and subsequently of 3 technical replicates of one patient derived line and 3 technical replicates of the CRISPR rescue of this patient derived line

title: Human vascular smooth muscle cells undergoing cell senescence
summary: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) undergo cell senescence in a number of diseases, both due to stress and loss of replication. Here we have cultured human VSMCs to replicative senescence, or induced stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS), and compared their transcriptome with cells treated with doxorubicin for 1d or control cells
design: Bulk RNAseq from primary human VSMCs undergoing (1) doxorubicin-induced SIPs (dox 1d+21d), (2) replicative senescence (RS), (3) Doxorubicin treatment for 1d (dox1d), or control cells (Ctr)

title: RNAseq in JARID2 siRNA-treated in vitro differentiated human primary adipocytes
summary: RNAseq was performed in siJARID2 and control siRNA-treated human adipose tissue derived stem cells (hASC). The tretment of siRNA was performed by electroporation one day before induction of differentiation in vitro. The cells were lyzed and RNA was purified on day 6 (mid differentiation) and day 13 (full differentiation) from differentiation start.

title: New prognostic factor identification by screening changes in differentially expressed genes during oral squamous cell carcinoma progression
summary: Identification of differentially expressed genes in human oral squamous cell carcinoma cell line UPCI-SCC-040 after TGF-ß1 treatment compared to untreated controls
design: Differentely expressed genes after treatment

title: Pulsed cisplatin treatment of A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells
summary: A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells were pulsed for 2h with cisplatin and allowed to recover for 3 days. Cells were then FACS sorted based on size and enriched populations analysed for RNAseq.
design: Next-generation RNAseq analysis of cisplatin pulsed A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells pre and post FACS sorting for cell size, in biological triplicate.

title: Effect of methanol fixation on single-cell RNA sequencing data
summary: We report how methanol fixation influences transcriptome profile in single cell RNA-seq. We generatad Smart-seq2 data from two cell lines, and both live  and fixed cells from each cell line were processed and analyzed to illustrate fixaiton effect.

title: RNA-seq analysis of HeLa METTL5-KO cells compared to WT HeLa cells
summary: To identify transcripts upregulated and downregulated upon METTL5 knockout in HeLa cells.

title: RNA sequencing analysis of MCF7 cells treated with several combinations of steroids
summary: We report the transcriptomic profile induced on MCF7 cells by several combinations of steroids (estetrol, estradiol, progesterone, R5020).
design: Routinely cultured MCF7 cells were treated in red phenol-free DMEM medium, supplemented with 2% heat-inactivated and dextran-coated charcoal- treated FBS with estradiol (10-9M), estetrol (10-7M or 10-10M) or vehicle (DMSO 0.001%) for 20h, then progesterone (10-7M) or R5020 (10-8M) were added in some conditions for 4 additional hours. After 24h total treatment, RNA was extracted, quantified and submitted to RNAseq analysis.

title: Pooled CRISPR screening in pancreatic cancer cells implicates co-repressor complexes as a cause of multiple drug resistance via regulation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition [RNA-Seq]
summary: Over expression of co-repressor complexes implicated as a cause of multiple drug resistance in pancreatic cancer.

title: Transcriptional analysis of SARS-CoV-2 specific CD4 T cells
summary: The objective of this analysis was to determine if there was a transcriptional difference in the CD4 T cell response elicited by SARS-CoV-2 infection in individuals that quickly resolved their infection compared to those individuals with prolonged SARS-CoV-2-associated symptoms

title: Effect of ZIC3/TEAD2/TEAD4 on Reprogramming of Human Urine Cells
summary: We performed RNA-seq and ATAC-seq on UCs from healthy humans and human embryonic stem cell line H1. By analyzing the transcriptome expression profile and chromatin accessibility bettween them, we find new transcription factors that can be used for reprogramming to study the mechanism of reprogramming.

title: shRNA mediated PAR1 downregulation in PANC-1 cell line
summary: shRNA against PAR1 and control haripin sh004 transduced PANC-1(Pancreatic cancer) cell line

title: microRNAs Restrain Proliferation in BRAFV600E Melanocytic Nevi [RNA-Seq]
summary: We conducted small RNA sequencing on low passage human melanocytes derived from melanocytic nevi and normal skin.
design: 8 normal skin derived melanocyte cultures and 6 nevus derived melanocyte cultures were sequenced.

title: Meloxicam and Filgrastim for Mobilization of Autologous Peripheral Blood Stem Cells in Patients with Multiple Myeloma
summary: The purpose of this RNA sequencing dataset was to analyze transcriptional changes in human stem cells when Meloxicam is added to the standard Filgrastim mobilization regimen in patients with Multiple Myeloma.

title: A comprehensive map of alternative polyadenylation in African American and European American lung cancer patients
summary: We report the application of a novel method and analysis pipeline that sequences 3’end -enriched RNA to comprehensively map the APA landscape in lung cancer. The goals of this study are to identify the functional role of APA in determining transcriptomic heterogeneity in lung cancer and  population differences in APA.

title: Mediator of DNA damage checkpoint 1 (MDC1) is a novel estrogen receptor co-regulator in invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast
summary: We identified MDC1 as a putative novel transcriptional co-regulator of estrogen receptor alpha (ER) in models of invasive lobular carcinoma. In this study, our goal was to define the contribution of MDC1 to regulation of the ER transcriptome in ILC cell lines versus invasive ductal carcinoma cells.
design: RNAseq was used to examine estrogen-driven changes in gene expression, with or without knockdown of MDC1, ER, or FOXA1. We compared gene expression in invasive lobular carcinoma cell lines (MM134/MDA MB 134VI, MM330/MDA MB 330) to invasive ductal carcinoma cell line HCC1428.

title: Effect of platelets on 3D models of ovarian cancer
summary: A 3D multicellular model (MCM) of high grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) consisting of primary human adipocytes, fibroblasts, and mesothelial cells co-cultured with HGSOC cell lines was used to examine the effect of platelets on the ovarian metastasis microenvironment.
design: RNA sequencing was performed on multicellular models with (n = 3) or without addition of platelets (n = 3) as well as co-cultures of mesothelial cells and fibroblasts (n = 3) and adipocyte monocultures (n = 1).

title: Effect of platelets on ovarian cancer cell spheroids
summary: The effect of platelets on malignant cell growth was assessed on high-grade serous ovarian cancer cells grown in spheroids.
design: RNA sequencing on the G164 HGSOC malignant cell line grown in spheroids (n =3) and spheroids with addition of platelets (n = 3).

title: The SCP4-STK35/PDIK1L complex is a dual phospho-catalytic signaling dependency in acute myeloid leukemia (RNA-Seq)
summary: Transcriptome analysis by high throughput sequencing

title: Functional role of CPPED1 in trophoblasts.
summary: Analysis of the effect of CPPED1 siRNA experiment with and without P4
design: RNA-seq analysis of silenced CPPED1 (n = 3) and negative control (n=3) samples, and the samples treated with P4 (in EtOH) or EtOH This submission is part of the study of which the first part is already submitted under GSE103035 accession number

title: A transcriptomic analysis of SH-SY5Y cells with Varicella-Zoster Virus-Infected
summary: In this study, we screened the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in SH-SY5Y cells  with Varicella-Zoster Virus-Infected using RNAseq technique to explore the molecular mechanisms of Herpes zoster pain
design: SH-SY5Y cells with Varicella-Zoster Virus-Infected

title: Comprehensive analysis of the complexity and heterogeneity of the lncRNAs transcriptome in multiple myeloma
summary: RNA-seq analysis comparing the transcriptional landscape of LINC-SMILO silenced cells versus control cells in KMS-11 multiple myeloma cell line.

title: Gene expression data from BM1 (1833) tumors that are wild type or overexpressing RKIP in a xenograft mouse model
summary: RKIP is a metastasis suppressor that is lost or silenced in most metastatic cancers. Here we reintroduce RKIP exogenously into BM1 cells (bone-tropic derivative of MDA-MB-231 cells, also known as 1833) that lack RKIP expression, in order to study transcriptomic changes that lead to metastasis in vivo and identify actionable targets to be used in anti-metastatic treatment strategies.

title: Gene expression changes upon siCTNNB1 and compound treatment
summary: To investigating gene expression changes in HCT116 cells upon siCTNNB1 for 48 hr, or upon treatment with iCRT3, GB1874, GB6853, and GB8679 for 24 hr
design: HCT116 cells are transfected with siNeg or siCTNNB1 (20 nM each) in triplicate for 48 hr. HCT116 cells are also treated with DMSO (1%) or compounds iCRT3, GB1874, GB6853, GB8679 at 50 uM, in triplicate for 24 hr

title: miR-146a regulates many lncRNAs in RAS induced senescence [Anti-146a]
summary: miR-146a is a known anti-inflammatory miRNA. Intringuigly, it is overexpressed in RAS-induced senescent cells which is accompanied with a rich pro-inflammatoy secretpry phenotype. We aim to study possible sponges for miR-146a.

title: miR-146a regulates many lncRNAs in RAS induced senescence [miR-CLIP]
summary: miR-146a is a known anti-inflammatory miRNA. Intringuigly, it is overexpressed in RAS-induced senescent cells which is accompanied with a rich pro-inflammatoy secretpry phenotype. We aim to study possible sponges for miR-146a.

title: Next generation sequencing to find new medical targets for the treatment of conduit stenosis
summary: To find new medical tagets for the treatment of conduit stenosis, 11 pulmonary bioartificial valved conduits were explanted from patients with a congenital heart defect and next generation sequencing was performed using material from the thickened stenosis-causing conduit wall and the respective leaflet. Deregulated genes between 9 samples from the thickened conduit-wall and 8 leaflets were determined and all receptor tyrosin kinases were selected for further experiments.

title: Rate of recipient-derived alveolar macrophages development and major histocompatibility complex cross-dressing after lung transplantation in humans
summary: Analyzing the kenetics of alveolar macrophage turnover after human lung transplantation and identifying protein and transcriptional differences between donor and recipient-derived alveolar macrophages

title: Next Generation Sequencing of Acidosis Response in Intestinal Epithelial Cells
summary: Purpose: The goal of this study is to define the impact of extracellular acidosis on transcriptional regulation in intestinal epithelial cells. We identify a significant induction of CREB target genes and upregulation of several genes associated with MAPK signaling. This work provides a frame work for the identification of acidosis signaling pathway in intestinal epithelial cells
design: mRNA profiles of T84, human intestinal epithelial cells, treated wth pH 7.4 or 6.0 Hanks buffered saline for 3 or 6hr

title: Increased Systemic HSP70B Levels in Spinal Muscular Atrophy Infants
summary: RNA sequencing in whole blood from spinal muscular atrophy patients and healthy control infants

title: Enhanced efficacy of aurora kinase inhibitors in G2/M checkpoint deficient TP53 mutant uterine carcinomas is linked to the summation of LKB1-AKT-p53 interactions [RNA-seq]
summary: We report bulk RNA sequencing, low pass whole genome sequencing, and targeted exome sequencing data of six uterine cancer organoids and show how specific molecular defects in these organoids make them sensitive to cell cycle targeting therapies.
design: Transcriptomic and genomic sequencing of uterine cancer organoids.

title: RNA-seq WT vs TLE3KO ( treated with AR inhibitor)
summary: Transcriptome analysis of LNCaP control and TLE3 KO cells treated with AR inhibitor

title: RNA-seq in untreated and Cadherin-11 Knockdown Human Intestinal Myofibroblast cells (HIMF)
summary: The goal of this experiment was to identify if there are any genes differentially expressed in Cadherin-11 KD HIMF

title: Regulation of TLR8-activated gene expression in human neutrophils [RNA-seq neutrophils & monocytes]
summary: The transcription factors that regulate gene expression in stimulated neutrophils are poorly characterized. Herein, we found that the genomic distribution of the myeloid lineage determining transcription factors PU.1 and C/EBPβ, as well as that of the histone modification H3K27Ac, which marks active chromatin, significantly change in human neutrophils treated with R848, a ligand of TLR8.
design: Examination of histone modification, transcription factor binding and transcriptome in human neutrophils and granulocytic-differentiated HL-60 cell line

title: Regulation of TLR8-activated gene expression in human neutrophils  [RNA-seq HL-60]
summary: The transcription factors that regulate gene expression in stimulated neutrophils are poorly characterized. Herein, we found that the genomic distribution of the myeloid lineage determining transcription factors PU.1 and C/EBPβ, as well as that of the histone modification H3K27Ac, which marks active chromatin, significantly change in human neutrophils treated with R848, a ligand of TLR8.
design: Examination of histone modification, transcription factor binding and transcriptome in human neutrophils and granulocytic-differentiated HL-60 cell line

title: CCM3 is a gatekeeper in focal adhesions regulating mechanotransduction and YAP/TAZ signalling
summary: We report that loss of CCM3/PDCD10 in fibroblasts induces FAK/Src-paxillin signalling driving actomyosin-dependent mechanotransduction leading to YAP/TAZ signalling. In vivo, loss of CCM3 in fibroblasts drives excessive tissue remodelling leading to the dissemination of breast cancer cells to distant organs.
design: Examination of the varying RNA levels in control human vulval cancer-associated fibroblasts versus CCM3-depleted cells

title: HP1γ/CBX3 Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma by Activating Rho GTPases Signaling Pathway
summary: We performed CBX3 knockdown in lung adenocarcinoma cells along with RNA sequencing. The expression profiling showed Rho GTPases signaling as a potential CBX3 target and the conclusions were also verified in clinical samples.

title: Oncogene-induced maladaptive activation of Trained Immunity in the pathogenesis of human inflammatory myeloid neoplasm [BRAF]
summary: Trained immunity (TI) is a pro-inflammatory program induced in monocyte/macrophages upon sensing of specific pathogens and characterized by immunometabolic and epigenetic changes enhancing cytokine production. Maladaptive activation of TI (i.e., in the absence of infection) might result in detrimental inflammation and disease development; however, the exact role and extent of inappropriate activation of TI in the pathogenesis of human diseases is undetermined.
design: We reveal oncogene-induced, maladaptive induction of TI in the pathogenesis of a human inflammatory myeloid neoplasm (Erdheim-Chester disease, ECD, characterized by the BRAFV600E oncogenic mutation in monocyte/macrophages and excess cytokine production).

title: Oncogene-induced maladaptive activation of Trained Immunity in the pathogenesis of human inflammatory myeloid neoplasm [ECD]
summary: Trained immunity (TI) is a pro-inflammatory program induced in monocyte/macrophages upon sensing of specific pathogens and characterized by immunometabolic and epigenetic changes enhancing cytokine production. Maladaptive activation of TI (i.e., in the absence of infection) might result in detrimental inflammation and disease development; however, the exact role and extent of inappropriate activation of TI in the pathogenesis of human diseases is undetermined.

title: A novel vitronectin peptide facilitates differentiation of oligodendrocytes from human embryonic stem cells (Synthetic ECM for oligodendrocyte differentiation)
summary: Differentiation of oligodendrocytes (ODs) presents a challenge in regenerative medicine due to their role in various neurological diseases associated with dysmyelination and demyelination. Here, we designed a peptide derived from vitronectin (VN) using in silico docking simulation and examined its use as a synthetic substrate to support the differentiation of ODs derived from human embryonic stem cells.

title: Human blastocyst model by self-organization of naïve pluripotent stem cells
summary: Human naïve pluripotent cells can differentiate to extraembryonic trophoblast and hypoblast cells. Here we report formation of human blastocyst models by self-organization solely of naïve pluripotent stem cells. The embryo models comprise the three founding lineages, epiblast, trophoblast and hypoblast, arranged to mimic the natural blastocyst. Single-cell RNA sequencing validated the identity of each cell type.

title: YTHDF2 inhibits gastric cancer cell growth by regulating FOXC2 signaling pathway
summary: we found that YTHDF2 has lower expression in GC tissues and GC cells, and promotes the growth, migration and invasion of GC cells. In addition, the analysis of clinical data found that the expression level of YTHDF2 was closely related to the stage of GC and the survival of patients with GC. RNA-seq showed that overexpression of YTHDF2 significantly reduced protein expression in the FOXC2 (Forkhead box protein C2, FOXC2) signaling pathway.

title: Effects of aging and exercise on peripheral blood mononuclear cell gene expression
summary: Aging is associated with altered gene expression and dysregulation of non-coding RNAs, including repetitive element transcripts. The purpose of this study was to characterize age- and exercise-related differences in gene and repetitive element expression in humans using RNA-seq.

title: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma and paracancerous tissue
summary: We reported RNA-seq data for three nasopharyngeal carcinoma tissues and three counterparting paracancerous tissues.

title: RNA-seq analysis of HNSCC cells after JQ1 treatment
summary: We performed RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of HNSCC cells to examine genome-wide gene expression pattern following JQ1 treatment. BET inhibition by JQ1 significantly inhibits a cohort of key oncogenes associate with tumorigenesis and metastasis. Suggesting BET inhibition is effective strategy to suppress the tumorigenesis and metastasis of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
design: Examination of RNA-seq of  HNSCC cells treated with JQ1.

title: Macropinocytosis requires Gal-3 in a subset of patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells
summary: GBM cells were treated with GAL3 shRNA vs sh ctrl. Gal3 forms a complex with Rab10 to potentiate macropinocytosis in the mesenchymal subpopulation of GBM tumors

title: Host-dependent Phenotypic Resistance to EGFR Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors
summary: RNA-Seq comparison of Dacomitinib resistant PC9 lung adenocarcinoma cells vs the parental cells.

title: Transcriptome analysis by RNA sequencing of human trisomy 21 and normal control blood cells
summary: The aim of this study is to analyse trisomy 21 (T21) transcriptome. We generated RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) paired-end data from ribosomal RNA-depleted total RNA isolated from blood cell samples of four T21 and four normal control individuals.

title: Photosensitivity and c-GAS-dependent type I IFN activation in lupus patients with TREX1 deficiency
summary: High throughput screening comparing gene expression in human wildtype and patient (TREX1-mutated) fibroblasts, Next-generation sequencing (NGS) has revolutionized systems-based analysis of cellular pathways. The goals of this study are to compare NGS-derived retinal transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) to microarray and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT–PCR) methods and to evaluate protocols for optimal high-throughput data analysis

title: Analysis of the effect of clofarabine treatment on gene expression in K562 cells using mRNA sequencing
summary: Clofarabine blocks the progression of cell cycle at the G1-S boundary. It induces upregulation of cyclin E and downregulation of histones and several other cell cycle related genes.

title: The role of MacroH2A1.2 in cancer (RNA-Seq)
summary: MacroH2A1.2 is a histone variant from H2A family. Expression of macroH2A1.2 is found to be dysregulated in cancer especially lung cancer. However, the role of macroH2A1.2 in lung cancer remains relatively unknown. Our study showed that macroH2A1.2 stabilized FASN expression, increased fatty acid production and hence improved rate of mitochondria respiration. As a result, the cancer cells with higher macroH2A1.2 expression were more metastatic.

title: MicroRNA-138 Suppresses Glioblastoma Proliferation through Downregulation of CD44
summary: MicroRNA-138 Suppresses Glioblastoma Proliferation through Downregulation of CD44

title: EZH2 deficiency induced gene expression change in CRCs
summary: Knockdown of EZH2 in colorectal cancer cells by lentivirus-mediated shRNA, and use total RNA for sequencing analysis after determining the efficiency of EZH2 knockdown in order to analyze the gene expression affected by EZH2.

title: Mechanistic Targets of Diallyl Trisulfide (DATS) in Human Breast Cancer Cells Identified by RNA-seq Analysis
summary: We report differential gene expression changes by DATS in breast cancer cells
design: Examination of DATS-regulated transcriptome in two human breast cancer cells with different subtypes including MCF-7 (luminal type) and MDA-MB-231 (basal type).

title: The prevalence of human cytomegalovirus in colorectal cancer and viral gene expression profiles
summary: Five HCMV (+) CRC tissues detected by PCR were selected for RNA-seq. GEPs were pre-processed by Cutadapter and FastQC to remove jointed reads and low-quality reads. Tophat (v.2.0.0) was used to compare the sequences with Homo sapiens and HCMV genomes. The GEPs of HCMV was determined by Integrated Genomics Viewer (IGV) and Partek® Genomics Suite™ (version 6.5 beta, Partek Inc., St. Louis, MO, USA).

title: Global Gene Expression Changes in Cholangiocytes Treated with P300 inhibitor SGC-CBP30 (10 μM; Selleckchem, #S7256)
summary: Histone modification is a critical epigenetic regulatory mechanism that is under-explored in cholestatic liver disease. Lysine 27 on histone 3 (H3K27) is a key regulatory residue that can be acetylated by the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) p300, which acts as a transcriptional coactivator.
design: Cholangiocyte cell line, HiBEC,  were treated with DMSO or SGC-CBP30 (10uM)  to look at the gene expression changes due to pharmacological inhibition of P300

title: Genome wide expression change by RNF31 knocking down in MCF-7 cells
summary: We aim to the investigate the role of RNF31 in breast cancer progression. MCF-7 cells were used as the model and RNF31 was silenced by siRNA.

title: Genome wide expression change by MCF-7 cells treated with MST1/2 inhibitor
summary: We aim to the investigate the role of MST inhibitor in breast cancer progression. MCF-7 cells were used as the model.

title: Differential gene expression of a gamma secretase inhibitor treated human oral squamous cell carcinoma cell line
summary: Notch signalling regulates various cancer cell beahviors. Influence of notch signaling inhibitor, a gamma secretase inhibitor (DAPT) on human oral squamous cell carcinoma is not yet widely investigated. Here, the differential mRNA expression of DAPT treated HSC4 cell line was examined using RNA sequencing technique. Results demonstraetd that DAPT regulated various pathways in HSC4, including cell cycle and DNA replication pathways.
design: HSC4 cells were maintained in normal growth medium and supplemented with 50 uM DAPT for 24 h. Total RNA was collected and RNA sequencing was performed. Differential gene expression and pathway enrichment was also performed.

title: The HIF target MAFF promotes tumor invasion and metastasis through IL11 and STAT3 signaling
summary: Using RNA-sequencing and ChIP-sequencing, we identified direct target genes of the transcription factor MAFF in MDA-MB-231 under normoxia and hypoxia.
design: MDA-MB-231, a human breast cancer cell line, was treated either under normoxia or hypoxia. After ChIP or RNA extraction, sequencing was performed. After knocking down endogenous MAFF in MDA-MB-231, we overexpressed V5-tagged MAFF with mutations on shRNA target sites. Then nuclei was extracted and we proceeded to ChIP procedures using V5 antibody to further determine direct targets of MAFF.

title: Time-course transcriptomic profiling of cell-cycle entry in MCF10A cells
summary: To identify potential novel regulators of G1/S transition and S-phase progression, we performed an RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) time-course analysis of non-transformed human breast epithelial cells (MCF10A) released into the cell cycle from serum starvation, in the presence of DMSO or a specific CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib.
design: Conditions include: 0hr, 3hr DMSO, 6hr DMSO, 9hr DMSO, 9hr palbociclib, 12hr DMSO, 12hr palbociclib, 15hr DMSO, 15hr palbociclib, 24hr DMSO, 24hr palbociclib. A total of 31 samples containing triplicates (except 24-hour time point, which was performed in duplicates) were analyzed.

title: Gene Expression Profiling of Cancer Cells after STBD1 overexpression
summary: We compare the gene expression profiles of shSTBD1/plvx neo, shSTBD1/WT, and shSTBD1/W203C cells

title: Gene Expression Profiling of Cancer Cells after STBD1 depletion
summary: To understand how STBD1 inhibits tumor growth, we compare the gene expression profiles of shControl and shSTBD1 HCT116 cells using RNA-seq

title: Loss of function of MALAT1 on primary human OA osteoblast transcriptome
summary: Cells: Primary human osteoblasts from subchondral bone of osteoarthritis patients (n=3 patients). Treatments: Cells transfected using Lipofectamine 3000 (Qiagen) with either control LNA (NC) or MALAT1 LNA1 or MALAT1 LNA2 for 24 hours. Total RNA extracted by Qiagen RNeasy columns. RIN values >7 via Agilent Bioanalyser. Analysis: RNA subjected to Quantseq 3' RNA sequencing (Lexogen) and sequenced reads mapped to the hg38 reference human genome.
design: 9 samples analysed in total. Primary OA subchondral bone osteoblasts from n=3 patients transfected for 24h with either (i) LNA control, (ii) MALAT1 LNA1 or (iii) MALAT1 LNA2.

title: The human memory T cell compartment changes across tisses of the female reproductive tract
summary: We report transcriptomic analysis of CD4 T cells isolated from vaginal, ectocervical, and endocervical tissues from 4 individuals.

title: A single-cell atlas of the peripheral immune  response in patients with HFRS.
summary: Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS) is a regional infectious disease of epidemic potential caused by the Hantaan Virus (HTNV).The studies  on immunological responses during HTNV infection have continuously been performed. During HTNV infection, lymphocytes are following a tightly controlled genetic programme.The pathological changes of PBMCs also occured during HTNV infection. We used single cell RNA sequencing to detail the cellular components and gene expression profiles of PBMCs underlying HTNV infection.

title: The Bromodomain and extraterminal (BET) inhibitor attenuates inflammatory response and cell migration in human microglia
summary: We investigated the mechanisms underlying the anti-inflammatory and anti-migratory function and genes targeted by JQ1 in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-activated human microglia HMC3 cells using RNA sequencing.  The BET inhibitor JQ1 attenuates the LPS-induced inflammatory and migratory response. In addition, LPS-induced IRF1 was inhibited by JQ1, and IRF1 suppressed microglial migration by regulating inflammation and migration genes.
design: The gene expression profile was performed with control HMC3 (Con), JQ1-treated HMC3 (JQ1), LPS-treated HMC3 (LPS), LPS+JQ1-treated HMC3 (LPS+JQ1). Samples were generated by deep sequencing, in triplicate, using Illumina 2500.

title: Transcriptome profiling of tumors from Caucasian and African American triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients.
summary: Triple negative breast cancer is an aggressive phenotypic breast cancer characterized by ER negative, PR negative and Her2 negative immunohistochemistry status. We embarked on a study to explore the transcriptome of African American and Caucasian TNBC patients and identify race specific biomarkers.

title: Transcriptome profiling of tumors from Kenyan triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients.
summary: Triple negative breast cancer is an aggressive phenotypic breast cancer characterized by ER negative, PR negative and Her2 negative immunohistochemistry status. We embarked on a study to explore the transcriptome of Kenyan TNBC patients and identify potential biomarkers specific to Kenyan population. The transcriptome sequencing of tumors from Kenyan TNBC patients and comparisons with African American and Caucasian TNBC transcriptomes revealed several interesting targets and dysregulated pathways.

title: RNA sequencing of control and CIP2A siRNA silenced basal-like breast cancer cell line HCC38
summary: The purpose is to study the transcriptional changes in basal like breast cancer cell line HCC38 on depletion of CIP2A. We have used 3 unique siRNA sequences of CIP2A and  3 control samples (Mock and 2 unique non-targeting sequences) for the RNA Seq. We identified differentially expressed genes in CIP2A knockdown conditions compared to the control samples and identified pathways regulated by CIP2A in this cell line using GSEA.
design: CIP2A was silenced using 3 unique CIP2A siRNAs. Oligofectamine was used as the transfection reagent and standard manufacturer's protocols were followed. Non transfection control (Mock) and two nontargeting control siRNAs were used as controls.

title: Unsupervised analysis of flow cytometry data in a clinical setting captures cell diversity and allows population discovery
summary: In our study, MegaClust - an unsupervised, data-driven algorithm - barely described mDCs and pDC subsets were identified. To confirm these findings we performed RNA sequencing Facs sorted of mDCs (CD123-CD11c+CD4+HLA-DR+), pDCs (CD123+CD11c-CD4+HLA-DR+) and monocytes (CD14+) from healthy donors and compared these with publicly available data.

title: mRNA-seq of peripheral blood monocyte- and human pluripotent stem cell-derived macrophages
summary: We investigate the impact of an initial stimulation and a re-stimulation in altering transcriptional responses in both peripheral blood-monocyte derived macrophages and human pluripotent stem cell derived macrophages.
design: mRNA-seq in 2-3 replicates of LPS stimulated macrophages derived from peripheral blood or human pluripotent stem cell-derived macrophages

title: Estrogen Receptor Activation Time Course at 3, 6, 12 & 24h in MCF7, T47D and MDA-MB-231 with and without ZMIZ1 knockdown
summary: To establish the role of ZMIZ1 in the Estrogen Recptor complex we undertook an time course following estrogen stimulation with and without ZMIZ1 knockdown monitored by RNA-seq.

title: Hypoxia-induced SETX links replication stress with the unfolded protein response
summary: Study of Transcriptomic changes upon Senataxin depletion in Normoxia and Hypoxia
design: Examination of RKO under normaxia and hypoxia condition with SETX depletion.

title: Distinct metabolic perturbations associated with pediatric Plasmodium falciparum malaria during Intra-erythrocytic development stage
summary: The goal of this study was to interrogate the impact of metabolic perturbations during P. falciparum infection on the host immune response in a cohort of West African children sampled and profiled before and during infection. Here, we use integrative metabolomics-transcriptomic approach to the investigate potential immunomodulatory effects of serum metabolites during the blood stage of infection.

title: Comparison of the RB loss-induced transcrptiome in hormone-therapy sensitive and castration-resistant prostate cancer [RNA-seq]
summary: These studies examine the biological networks altered after RB loss across prostate cancer progression.
design: Transcriptome alterations in resposne to RB loss after AR stimulation were assessed in early (LNCaP-shCon and LNCaP-shRB) and late (C42-shCon and C42-shRB) stage disease models

title: Evidence of superior and inferior sinoatrial nodes in the mammalian heart [Human]
summary: We report the application of RNA sequencing technology for high-throughput profiling of regionally separated sinoatrial nodal tissues from human hearts. We find that both the superior and inferior regions of these sinoatrial nodal tissues (termed sSAN and iSAN, respectively) possess statistically comparable levels of cardiac ion channels, receptors, neural proteins, and transcription factors. This study provides new insights into regional molecular expression of pacemaking tissue in the right atria.

title: Profiling of LNCaP-SL after circulating small extracellular vesicles treatment
summary: RNA was isolated from LNCaP-SL after 24 hours of circulating small extracellular vesicles (csEV) single dose treatment (1×10^10 particles/mL).

title: SF3B1 deficiency impairs human erythropoiesis via activation of p53 pathway: implications for understanding of ineffective erythropoiesis in MDS
summary: SF3B1 knockdown in human CD34+ cells leads to increased apoptosis and cell cycle arrest of early-stage erythroid cells and generation of abnormally nucleated late-stage erythroblasts. RNA-seq analysis of SF3B1-knockdown erythroid progenitor CFU-E cells revealed altered splicing of an E3 ligase Makorin Ring Finger Protein 1 (MKRN1) and subsequent activation of p53 pathway.Decreased expression of genes involved in mitosis/cytokinesis pathway including polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) was noted in SF3B1-knockdown polychromatic and orthochromatic erythroblasts comparing to control cells.
design: RNA-seq analyses between normal erythropoiesis and  SF3B1 knockdown erythropoiesis

title: Defining the AHR-regulated transcriptome in NK cells reveal gene expression programs relevant to development and function
summary: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a ligand activated transcription factor that plays a critical role in shaping innate and adaptive immune responses. However, the molecular mechanism by which AHR regulates the function of human NK cells remains largely unknown. Here, we use RNA sequencing on IL21-expanded NK cells in the presence of AHR agonists and antagonist to demonstrate that AHR directly regulates the expression of known regulators of phenotype, development, metabolism, and function.

title: Global transcriptomic changes in alveolar epithelial type II (ATII)  cells upon GRK6 depletion based on RNA-seq
summary: G protein coupled receptor kinase 6 (GRK6) is a member of the GRKs family, which is expressed in various tissues and involved in the development of several diseases, including lung adenocarcinoma. Our previous study suggested that GRK6 expression was significantly down-regulated in lung adenocarcinoma patients, and its level was an independent prognostic factor for overall survival. Here, by performing RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) in alveolar epithelial type II (ATII)  cells transfected with either short interfering RNA (siRNA) oligos against GRK6 or control siRNAs, several disease related alterations were identified.

title: Differential mRNA transcription in gingival tissues in periodontal health and disease [RNA-seq]
summary: We investigated differential mRNA expression in gingival tissues in states of periodontal health, gingivitis and periodontitis.

title: Transcriptomic data from  lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus-infected and mock-infected A549 cells
summary: We reported the transcriptomic analysis on A549 cells infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV).

title: Blood RNA signature RISK4LEP predicts leprosy years before clinical onset
summary: Exploratory RNA expression analysis during development of leprosy allows identification of RISK4LEP, a 4-gene blood RNA signature predicting leprosy years before clinical onset.

title: RNAseq of human brain cell lines
summary: In the murine brain, perivascular fibroblasts were recently identified as a novel potential constituent of the BBB. Here we present the existence of human cells, that could be the equivalent to the murine brain perivascular fibroblasts. Using RNA sequencing, we here show a similar transcriptomic profile of cultured human brain cells and murine perivascular fibroblasts. These data open up for new hypotheses on cell types involved in human CNS diseases.

title: The immune landscapes of primary central nervous system diffuse large B cell lymphoma
summary: Purpose: RNA-sequencing data was used to characterize the tumoral microenvironnement subtypes and its associated signaling networks.

title: KRAS and MEK activation promote antisense oligonucleotide uptake and activity by limiting collagen production
summary: Using RNAseq we describe transcriptional changes downstream of MEK1 affecting RNA kncokdown following free uptake RNaseH1 gapmer antisense oligonucleotides
design: We perform RNAseq on cell lines with a stimulated MAPK pathway via inducible expression of KRAS(G12D), inducible expression of MEK1(S218/S222DD) and by stimulation with the PKC activator, PMA

title: The synthetic opioid fentanyl elicited transcriptomic alterations related to viral replication, immune response, and inflammation in vitro.
summary: The US is in the midst of a major drug epidemic fueled in large part by the widespread recreational use of syntheticopioids such as fentanyl. we evaluated the impact of fentanyl using in cell lines that replicate infectious viruses. RNAseq identified a number of hepatocyte genes that were differentially regulated by fentanyl, including those related to apoptosis, the antiviral / interferon response, chemokine signaling, and NFkB signaling.

title: 3D-Bioprinting allows the establishment of long-term 3D culture model for Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia cells
summary: Studying primary Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia cells in vitro is very challenging due to their short survival in culture, and also due to the fact that traditional two-dimensional in vitro models lack cellular and spatial complexity present in vivo. Based on these considerations, we exploited three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting to advance in vitro models for CLL. Through RNA sequencing (RNAseq) analysis, we observed a consistent difference in gene expression profile between 2D and 3D samples, indicating a different behavior of the cells in the two different culture settings.
design: Examination of the transcriptomic differences between traditional two-dimensional (2D) cultured cells and cells cultured in three-dimensional (3D) bioprinted scaffolds. RNA from bioprinted 3D cells was extracted overtime, after 7 and 14 days.

title: Transcriptome analysis of Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2)-infected and Influenza A/H1N1-infected nasal turbinate and lung tissues
summary: We report the application of RNA sequencing for transcriptome analysis of SARS-CoV-2-infected and Influenza A-infected Human nasal turbinate and lung tissues, enabling the study of tissue responses to viral infections
design: Nasal turbinate tissues from three individuals and Lung tissues from five individuals, were either SARS-CoV-2-, Influenza A- or mock-infected and subjected to transcriptome analysis.

title: Divergent resistance mechanisms to HER2-targeted therapies in breast cancer (bulkRNA-Seq and Exome-Seq)
summary: Divergent resistance mechanisms to HER2-targeted therapies in breast cancer
design: Bulk RNA-Seq and exome seq on DNA and RNA of two HER+ PDX models treated with anti-HER2 drugs

title: Transcriptional profiling of control versus PAF depleted human lung cancer cell line (H1792)
summary: RNA-Seq analyses of shCtrl (control group) and shPAF (experimental group) H1792 cell lines

title: Transcriptome analysis in XACT deleted female human pluripotent stem cells
summary: In this study, we generated female human pluripotent stem cells with the deletion of large non-coding RNA XACT specifically expressed in human pluripotent stem cells. We obtained heterogenous knock out and compound null clones. In order to examine, the effect of XACT on X-linked genes expression states, we carried out allele specific expression analysis.

title: Transcriptome  analysis of G6PD overexpression(OE) and wildtype(WT) cells in Multiple Myeloma
summary: RNA-seq experiments was conducted to analyze changes in related signaling pathways and gene expression in multiple myeloma  cells when G6PD was overexpression.

title: Systemic and adipocyte transcriptional and functional metabolic dysregulation in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
summary: We examined the transcriptional profile of subcutaneous adipose tissue in Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) patients compared to a control cohort matched for gender and BMI

title: iPSC-derived Human Intestinal Organoids are permissive to SARS-CoV-2 infection
summary: We performed transcriptomic profiling of cells derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) using a directed differentiation protocol to generate mesenchyme free, regionally patterned intestinal organoids. These organoids were then infected with SARS-CoV-2, and sequencing was performed 1 and 4 days post infection
design: Global transcriptomic analysis of PSC-derived intestinal organoids infected with SARS-CoV-2 omparing 1 and 4 days post infection to matched mock controls in both proximal and distally patterned infestinal organoids. (n=3 per condition)

title: Identification of novel transcription factors that regulate prostate cancer cell metabolism
summary: To understand of the impact of KLF5 and NFYA on metabolism in prostate cancer cells
design: LNCaP cells were plated in RPMI 1640 media with no phenol red and with 5% charcoal stripped serum, sodium pyruvate, penicillin and streptomycin. After 48h (to allow adnrogen deprivation), fresh media was added, with 96% ethanol or the synthetic androgen R1881 (10nM concentration). After trypsinization cells were seeded in media with CSS and transfected with a pool of non-targeted control siRNAs or a pool of siRNAs targeted against KLF5 and NFYA

title: Analysis of subcellular transcriptomes by RNA proximity labeling with Halo-seq
summary: We have developed Halo-seq, an RNA proximity labeling method that allows the quantification of subcellular transcriptomes. We have demonstrated the efficacy of Halo-seq here by using it to quantify chromatin-proximal, nucleolar, and cytoplasmic transcriptomes. In Halo-seq, RNA molecules in close proximity to a spatially restricted protein are specifically marked and biotinylated, facilitating their separation from bulk cellular RNA and their quantification.

title: Transcriptome Analysis of HMGB1 knock-out iSLK BAC16 cell (2)
summary: Purpose: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has revolutionized systems-based analysis of cellular pathways. The goals of this study are to compare NGS-derived transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) to microarray and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT–PCR) methods and to evaluate protocols for optimal high-throughput data analysis. In addition, we have already registered the transcriptome analysis results of HMGB1 KO iSLK BAC16 cell in GSE157275, and this registration is to reproduce it.

title: Overexpression of circCUL2 in normal fibroblasts
summary: We have found through previous experiments that circCUL2 acts as a key regulator of cancer-associated fibroblasts activation. To determine how circCUL2 exert its function, we performed mRNA sequencing of normal fibroblasts (NFs) and circCUL2-transduced NFs. 48 hours after transfection, RNA was isolated and sent for total RNA sequencing. Differential gene expression between circCUL2-overexpression and empty vector revealed enrichment for several inflammation pathways implicating involvement of these pathways in inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts activation.

title: Genome-wide mRNA profiling of induced Medulloblastoma (iMB) from human iPS cells
summary: We used human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to establish tumors recapitulating the histological and transcriptional hallmarks of MYC-driven medulloblastoma (MB). We generated neuronal precursors from human iPSCs. These neuronal precursors were transformed by the MYC oncogene combined with p53 loss-of-function to generate MB xenografts for RNA-seq analysis.

title: An inter-dependent network of enhancers regulates INK4a/ARF locus
summary: By functionally dissecting  densest enhancer cluster in the gene desert at 9P21 locus, we identified a non-redundant inter-dependent enhancer network that functions over long distances, the perturbation in any enhancer in the network results in the complete collapse of entire enhancer cluster and target genes activity. The enhancer network can be targeted to regulate INK4a/ARF locus in associated pathophysiologies and cancers.

title: EGF-induced Transcriptome Changes in GBM stem-like cells
summary: GBM neurosphere line GBM1B were depleted of growth factors for 16 hours followed by EGF stimulation for 4 and 24 hours. RNA-seq was used to identify differentially-expressed (DE) genes after EGF treatment.

title: Activation of ERRγ enhances mitochondrial and sarcomere maturation in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
summary: We identified two cardiac maturation stimulators from 9,048 compounds using Troponin I1 (TNNI1) and Troponin I3 (TNNI3) double reporter  hiPSC-derived CMs. An estrogen-related receptor gamma (ERRγ)-specific agonist increased the size of hiPSC-CMs and their mitochondrial content and enhanced their mitochondrial function. In addition, combination of this agonist with an inhibitor of S-phase kinase-associated protein 2 (SKP2) increased the TNNI3 expression more highly than previous methods and enhanced cardiac maturation-related gene expression profiles.

title: OAS1 and OAS3 negatively regulate the expression of chemokines and interferon-responsive genes in human macrophages
summary: We report analysis of mRNA profiles from wild-type and OAS1 and OAS3-KO human cell lines stimulated with PolyI:C.

title: Differential mRNA expression analysis of EGFR-TKI-sensitive cells vs. EGFR-TKI-resistant cells
summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) resistance remains unknown. We determined gene expression profiling in EGFR-TKI-resistant cells using RNA-seq analysis

title: RNA-seq analyses of PDAC cells
summary: Total RNAs were subjected to RNA isolation and RNA-seq analyses were generated by deep sequencing using Illumina Hiseq.

title: Whole transcriptome analysis of endothelial cells (HUVECs) after treatment with plasma-sEVs from polytrauma patients
summary: To assess inflammation associated gene expression in endothelial cells mediated by small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), HUVECs were treated for 8hrs with plasma-Evs isolated from polytrauma patients 4 and 24hrs after trauma and healthy probands.

title: RNAseq in BRD4 reporter KBM7 cells (REDS1 and REDS15) with purine metabolism perturbation
summary: To investigate the transcriptional profile in two BRD4 reporter clones (REDS1 and REDS15) with purine metabolism perturbation

title: Effect of infection with VSV-G pseudotyped HIV on the DNA damage response in HCT116 cells
summary: Effect of infection with VSV-G pseudotyped HIV partiles on HCT116 cells at different time points.

title: Host transcriptome response to SARS-CoV2 infection
summary: HEK293T stable express hACE2 was infected by SARS-CoV-2 (WA1) and RNA-seq was performed to profile host gene expression in response to SARS-COV-2 infection

title: Impact of the bone microenvironment on phenotypic plasticity of ER+ breast cancer cells [MCF7]
summary: Translating Ribosome Affinity Purification (TRAP) sequencing revealed that human osteogenic cells (FOB1.19) strongly alter the transcriptional profile of ER+ breast cancer cells (MCF7) in 3D coculture system.
design: 3D monocultures or cocultures of MCF7 cells with FOB1.19. Translating Ribosome Affinity Purification was performed to purify transcriptome from MCF7 cells, followed by NSG sequencing and data analysis.

title: Impact of the bone microenvironment on phenotypic plasticity of ER+ breast cancer cells[Osteogenic cells]
summary: RNA sequencing was used to evaluate the effect of cancer cells on osteogenic cells (FOB 1.19) in presence of estrogen or androgen. Here, we unbiasely evaluated the expression level of fibroblast growth factor receptors (FGFs) in osteogenic cells (FOB) alone.
design: Osteogenic cells (FOB 1.19) were cultured in mono- or co-culture with mouse breast cancer (4T1) or prostate cancer (TRAMP) cells. Total RNA was sequenced and human reads were extracted using in silico sorting before analysis

title: All-Trans-Retinoic Acid Treatment of IDH Mutant Astrocytes
summary: Immortalized human astrocytes were stably transfected to express IDH1 R132H. These cells were treated with 1uM ATRA

title: Characterizing the invasive tumor front of aggressive uterine adenocarcinoma and leiomyosarcoma
summary: Invasive tumor front (ITF, the tumor-host interface) is vitally important in malignant cell progression and metastasis. Tumor cell interactions with resident and infiltrating host cells and with the surrounding extracellular matrix and secreted factors ultimately determine the fate of the tumor. Herein we focus on the invasive tumor front, making an in-depth characterization of reticular fiber scaffolding, infiltrating immune cells, gene expression and epigenetic profiles of classified aggressive primary uterine adenocarcinomas (uADC)  and leiomyosarcomas (uLMS).

title: Developmental chromatin programs determine oncogenic competence in melanoma [RNA-seq II]
summary: Transcriptional profile of 3xKO dox melanocytes and 3xKO ATAD2 dox melanocytes

title: Developmental chromatin programs determine oncogenic competence in melanoma [RNA-seq]
summary: Transcriptional profile of human ES-cell (hPSC) derived melanoma cell models
design: Human ES cells were differentiated into neural crest (NC), melanoblast (MB) or melanocytes (MC). These were either WT or triple knockout (3xKO) for p53, p16, RB1. A dox-inducible cassette was integrated into the cells to activate the BRAFV600E oncogene upon addition of doxycyline.

title: Single-cell RNA-seq of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells in COVID-19
summary: We carried out sex-balanced sampling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from confirmed COVID-19 inpatients (hospitalized) and outpatients (infected), uninfected close contacts (exposed), and healthy controls.

title: BCOR modulates transcriptional activity of a subset of glucocorticoid receptor target genes involved in cell growth and mobility
summary: The effect of BCL6 corepressor (BCOR) on glucocorticoid signaling and was analyzed in HEK293-based cell lines using ChIP-seq and RNA-seq.
design: Chromatin binding of BCOR was analyzed using ChIP-seq from two biological replicates of HEK293 cells constitutively expressing GR (HEK293-GR; Paakinaho et al., 2014). Fragmented de-crosslinked chromatin was used as an input control. Gene expression was analyzed from three (rep1-3) biological replicates using RNA-seq. Poly-A RNA was extracted from BCOR depleted (siBCOR) or control siRNA-transfected (siNON) HEK293-GR cells treated with vehicle (ethanol, EtOH) or dexamethasone (100nM, 6h).

title: Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Hepatocyte-like Cells Provide Insights on Parenteral Nutrition Associated Cholestasis in the Immature Liver
summary: Our findings provide insights into altered bile acid and lipid metabolizing processes in the immature human liver and support the use of iHLC as a relevant in vitro system for modeling the developing liver to study lipid metabolism and PNAC.

title: Genomic landscapes of VEGF family members in endothelial cells
summary: Role of novel long intergenic (lincRNA) and enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) in the regulation of vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFs), in endothelial cells.

title: Impact of LXR activation on alternatively activated human macrophages
summary: To investigate how LXR activation potentiates expression of Th2 cytokine-dependent genes in primary human macrophages, we pulsed macrophages with synthetic LXR ligand T0901317 then polarized cells to alternatively activated macrophages with IL-4 or IL-13.
design: Human monocytes derived from three individual donors were differentiated into naïve macrophages with RPMI 1640 medium containing 5% AB-positive human serum for 7 days. Naive macrophages were pulsed with T0901317 (1 µM) for 3 hours, then media was aspirated and cells were polarized to alternatively activated macrophages with IL-4 (5 ng/ml) or IL-13 (10 ng/ml) for 24 hours.

title: Transcriptome analysis of SREBF1 silencing and overexpression in thyroid cancer cells
summary: Malignant thyroid tumors have altered lipid metabolism. Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBF1), also known as sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP-1), regulates cellular lipid homeostasis. We found that SREBF1 expression is a prognostic factor in patients with thyroid cancer and planned to elucidate its oncogenic mechanisms.

title: Sequencing of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) cell lines upon upregulation or downregulation of G0/G1 switch gene (G0S2)
summary: Current treatment for CML involves tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), which turned it into a managable disease. In a transcriptional profile of TKI-resistant versus newly diagnosed CML patient samples, G0S2 was shown to be profoundly downregulated.

title: Multi-omics profiling of living human pancreatic islet donors reveals heterogeneous beta cell trajectories toward type 2 diabetes
summary: To gain insight into the history of islet cell deterioration along the progression from normal glycemic regulation to T2D, we collected surgical pancreatic tissue samples from 133 metabolically phenotyped pancreatectomized patients (PPP). Gene expression profiles of islets isolated by laser capture microdissection (LCM) from resected and snap-frozen pancreas samples were assessed by RNA sequencing.

title: Transcriptome analysis of human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) with KLF11 knockdown
summary: HAECs were infected with Ad-shlacZ (10MOI) or Ad-shKLF11 (10MOI) for 48 hours and harvest for RNA-sequencing

title: Comparison between MCF7-IKKe overexpressing cells and MCF7 control cells
summary: Analysis of differentially expressed genes in MCF7 cancer cells transiently transfected with an expression vector containing the ORF of IKKe and as a control, cells were transfected with a vector containing the ORF of Lacz.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics of human intestinal organoids infected with  SARS-CoV-2
summary: In this work we have employed a single cell sequencing approach of both ileum and colon organoids using 10x Genomics scRNAseq and TAP-seq targeted single-cell RNA-seq.

title: Overexpression of CYGB led to differential gene expression in HCT116 cells (RNA-seq)
summary: The goal of this study was to define the cohort of genes whose expression is regulated by CYGB function in colorectal cancer. Towards this goal, HCT116 cells stably expressing CYGB (HCT-CYGB) were established. In addition, a control cells (HCT-MOCK) was generated by transfection with empty vector. Subsequently, total RNA was isolated and then performed transcriptome RNA sequence.

title: Klotho inhibits neuronal senescence in human brain organoids
summary: We report the application of brain organoids to study cellular senescence, in particular Klotho declining in expresssion mediates neuronal senescence, bulk RNA-sequencing further identified the potenital downstream target tha may modulate cellular senescence in the brain.

title: Total RNA sequencing of FXN knockdown in pulmonary artery endothelial cells
summary: This data set provides different RNA expression data for primary human pulmonary endothelial cells with and without FXN deficiency achieved by RNAi transfection in an effort to understand the endothelial-specific effects of acquired frataxin (FXN) deficiency and their implications for pulmonary vascular disease.

title: Selective inhibition of CDK7 reveals the influence of CDK7 on psoriatic CD4+ T cells
summary: Purpose: The goals of this study are to compare the differential gene of psoriatic CD4+ T cells treated with THZ1 and DMSO Methods: RNA sequencing of psoriatic CD4+ T cells which treated with THZ1 (10 nM) or DMSO

title: Mechanistic understanding of the combined immunodeficiency in complete human CARD11 deficiency
summary: From lymphoblastoid cell lines derived from two homozygous CARD11-deficient patients and two heterozygous parents of the first patient, we performed differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and pathway analyses by RNA-Seq to demonstrate impaired activation of critical immune pathways.

title: Effect of type I interferons against HSV infection in cerebral organoids
summary: Administration of recombinant interferons to 3D brain organoid cultures infected with HSV reveals a strong antiviral effect of IFN-alpha against HSV

title: Organoid phenotypic testing identifies IFN-beta as neuroprotective compound against ZIKA virus (ZIKV)
summary: Administration of recombinant interferons to 3D brain organoid cultures infected with ZIKV identifies IFN-beta as compound that alleviates organoid damage and inhibits ZIKV
design: Comparison of transcriptomes from ZIKV infected or MOCK organoids treated with IFN-alpha or IFN-beta or left untreated (6 conditions) at two time points

title: RNAseq of KMT2D and KDM6A human lymphoblastoid cell lines
summary: RNA-seq of lymphoblastoid cell lines from KMT2D/MLL2 and KDM6A patients.

title: The chromatin accessibility landscape reveals distinct transcriptional regulation in the induction of human primordial germ cell-like cells from pluripotent stem cells
summary: The  accessibility chromatin patterns during hPGCLCs undergo a diverse changes in absence of SOX15. The consequence of these changes lead to a somatic gene network activation that leads to decrease hPGCLC at late stage

title: Identification and Functional Analysis of MYEOV, KCNN4, S100A16 and DDX60L in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
summary: siRNA of MYEOV, KCNN4, S100A16 and DDX60L treated MiaPaCa2 and PANC-1 cells were used for RNA-seq to identify the transcriptomic alterations.
design: Examination of  knockdown MYEOV, KCNN4, S100A16 and DDX60L in MiaPaCa2 and PANC-1 cells.

title: Identification and Functional Analysis of Novel Oncogenes in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
summary: For identifying the specific expressed genes in PDAC, we constructed sequencing libraries from polyadenylated-RNA extracted from 6 PDAC specimens and 6 non-tumor adjacent tissues.

title: Arcuate organoid cells
summary: We report the application of bulk and single-cell RNAseq profiling to arcuate organoid cells

title: Human hypothalamus
summary: We report the application of single-cell RNAseq profiling of human hypothalamus cells

title: Lifespan charactarization of the nasal mucosa
summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of the nasal mucosa across the lifespan

title: Genome-wide DNA Methylation and Transcriptome Analysis of Non-invasive and Invasive Melanoma Cell Lines (RNASeq)
summary: Melanoma is a very aggressive type of skin cancer, which renders it difficult to treat because of extensive heterogeneity frequently observed in melanoma tumours. Here we hypothesized that gene expression and DNA methylation differences would correlate with invasiveness in melanoma cells. To address this question, we carried out genome-wide transcriptome and methylome investigations in non-invasive and invasive groups of melanoma cell lines.

title: Small molecule inhibitor of PRC1 E3 ligase activity induces differentiation of leukemia initiating cells [RNA-Seq]
summary: We have developed small molecule inhibitors of PRC1. These inhibitors target PRC1, decrease H2A ubiquitination and differentiation of TEX cells.

title: Familial Thrombocyotpenia due to a WAC-ANKRD26 Gene Fusion
summary: Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients carrying a WAC-ANKRD26 gene fusion caused by a duplication-inversion-duplication and healthy controls

title: Single-cell transcriptomic resolution of human pancreatic islets reveals cellular states and intercellular interactions associated with type 1 diabetes
summary: Our transcriptomic phenotyping of pancreatic cell types provides novel insights into pancreas biology, as well as the initial pathogenic events in T1D.

title: RNA-seq profile of stimulated Tregs containing co-receptor signaling domain variant chimeric antigen receptors (CARs).
summary: Initial CAR therapies were designed and tested in conventional T cells, however several recent reports indicate that CAR Tregs may be effective in solid organ transplant or hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Since Tregs have different activation requirements, we sought to characterize the transcriptional profile of Tregs that were transduced with second-generation CARs containing various co-receptor signaling moieties to determine which bestows Tregs with the most desireable properties.
design: Human Tregs/Tconv were transduced with second-generation chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) that contain various co-receptor signaling domains, then stimulated via CAR or T cell receptor.

title: Transcriptomic analysis by RNA-seq unveils distinct gene expression profile of U397 cells depleted of NSPs
summary: Characterization of transcriptomic changes associated with genetic ablation of three neutrophil serine proteases (CTSG, ELANE, PRTN3). U937 cells depleted of CTSG, ELANE, and PRTN3 simultaneously (ΔNSPs) were generated using the CRISPR-Cas9 system and sgRNAs. RNA-Seq analysis revealed transcriptomic changes between control cells and ΔNSPs, with 170 and 220 genes up- or down-regulated respectively.

title: Protein neddylation as a therapeutic target in pulomonary and extrapulonary small cell carcinomas [FHSC39]
summary: Gene expression in human small cell carinoma PDX models treated with MLN4924

title: Protein neddylation as a therapeutic target in pulomonary and extrapulonary small cell carcinomas [JHU-LX108]

title: A Thrombin-PAR1/2 Feedback Loop Amplifies Thrombo-Inflammatory Endothelial Responses To The Viral RNA Analogue Poly(I:C)

title: T3-Dependent Transcriptional Programming by TR-beta Requires SWI/SNF Chromatin Remodelers (RNA-Seq)

Total RNA was isolated from control as well as drug treated cells and apoptosis induction was confirmed by Annexin V and 7AAD staining. Total RNAs were subjected to deep-sequencing to identify differentially expressed RNAs. We then took advantage of bioinformatic tools to identify which lncRNAs are differentially expressed upon cisplatin treatment

title: RNA Sequencing of human liver hepatocellular carcinoma cell line HepG2 transcriptomes

Moreover, unique patterns of nasal gene expression demonstrate how specific molecular pathways underlie distinct respiratory phenotypes, including allergic and non-allergic asthma.

Principal compenent analysis of normalized proteins was used to produce UMAP plots that clustered like cell types. After identifying pro-B cells on UMAP plots and further refining these populations by filtering on CD19 expression and absent CD20/IgM expression, we identified differentially expressed genes between patient and control pro-B cells.

title: RNA-Seq analysis EIF5A2 knockdown effect on ovarian cancer cells
summary: Eukaryotic initiation factor 5A2 (EIF5A2) acts as a candidate oncogene and is located on human chromosome 3q26, a region frequently amplified in several tumors. Accumulating evidence shows that EIF5A2 plays important roles in enhancing anchorage-independent growth, xenograft tumour growth, increasing cancer cell metastasis and promoting treatment resistance through multiple pathways. Here, we showed that EIF5A2 knockdown reduced the expression of KLF4, which could partially rescue stem-like properties abolished by EIF5A2 knockdown or strengthened by EIF5A2 overexpression, through the transcription factor E2F1, which directly bind to KLF4 promoter.

title: The subcellular redistribution of NLRC5 promotes angiogenesis via interacting with STAT3 in endothelial cells
summary: We investigated the role of NLRC5 in the endothelial cells (ECs) and in-vivo angiogenesis. The results showed that the deficiency of NLRC5 decreased angiogenesis in vitro and vivo.And the subcellular redistribution of NLRC5 was regulated by VEGFA-165. RNA-seq and Co-IP indicated the potential relationship of NLRC5 and STAT3. ChIP assay determined that the mRNA expression of  angiopoietin-2 (Ang2) and cyclin D1 (CCND1) were orchestrated by the interaction of NLRC5 and STAT3.

title: Global transcriptional analysis of xeno-free and feeder-cultured human extended pluripotent stem cells by RNA-seq
summary: Extended pluripotent stem (EPS) cells have shown great applicative potentials in generating synthetic embryos, directed differentiation and disease modeling. However, the lack of a xenofree culture condition has significantly limited their wide applications. We developed a chemically defined and xeno-free culture condition for culturing and deriving human EPS cells, which can be long-term stably propagated in vitro, as well as preserve their embryonic and extraembryonic developmental potentials.

title: Gene expression changes in K562 upon USP7 inhibition
summary: K562 cells were grown in the presence of DMSO or the USP7 inhibitor FT671 (10 uM, 48h) after which RNA was isolated for transcriptome analyses.

summary: The goal of this study is to analyze the transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) after ISL1 knockdown. The objective of this study is to elucidate the mechanisms of ISL1 in gastric carcinogenesis, RNA-Seq is performed in BGC823 cells with stable ISL1 knockdown. Comparison and identification of the candidate genes based on the intersection of RNA-seq showed that upregulated and downregulated genes had ISL1-bound regions.

title: Transcriptome analysis of control and RBM6 KO cells before and after DNA damage
summary: Control and RBM6-KO MCF10A-Hras cells were subjected to RNA-sequencing before and after 12hrs exposure to 5Gy ionizing radiation (IR). Transcriptome analysis revealed a subset of genes that are differentially regulated in RBM6-KO cells compared to control cells. In addition, transcriptome of RBM6-KO cells after IR showed upregulation of DNA damage genes, suggesting impaired DNA repair compared to control cells.

title: Conserved DNA sequence features underlie pervasive RNA polymerase pausing
summary: This study reveals widespread Pol II pausing at single-nucleotide resolution across the human genome with the majority of Pol II pauses occur outside of promoter-proximal gene regions primarily along the gene-body of transcribed genes. We show DNA sequence properties underlying widespread transcriptional pausing including a new pause motif. The study indicates pervasive sequence-induced transcriptional pausing in human cells.

Finally, HiSeq 4000 was used to detect the fault.

title: Transcriptional profiling of Caco2 cells infected with Encephalitizoon intestinalis
summary: Encephalitizoon intestinalis infection occurs in immunocompromised individuals and has relatively few treatment options due to the lack of understanding of impact of microsporidia life cycle on host molecular effects.  We profiled transcriptome of a physiologically relevant intestinal epithelial cell line to understand what cellular processes are most impacted.
