Cells were washed with L15 medium and FAC-sorted for GFP positive NSCs using FACSariaIII (BD Biosciences) derived from Hes5::GFP transgenic embryos for NSCs and Tbr2::GFP transgenic embryos for BPs and NBNs.

title: Bulk RNA-seq of mouse cells from the dorsal cerebral cortex during its formation, with knocked-out Ski gene
summary: From mice treated with knocked-out Ski gene. Dorsal cortices from embryonic day E11.5 to E18.5 were micro-dissected and dissociated into single cell suspensions using Papain and Ovo-mucoid mix. Cells were washed with L15 medium and FAC-sorted for GFP positive NSCs using FACSariaIII (BD Biosciences) derived from Hes5::GFP transgenic embryos for NSCs and Tbr2::GFP transgenic embryos for BPs and NBNs.

title: Bulk RNA-seq of mouse cells from the dorsal cerebral cortex during its formation
summary: Dorsal cortices from embryonic day (E10.5) to postnatal day 1 (PN) were micro-dissected and dissociated into single cell suspensions using Papain and Ovo-mucoid mix. Cells were washed with L15 medium and FAC-sorted for GFP positive NSCs using FACSariaIII (BD Biosciences) derived from Hes5::GFP transgenic embryos for NSCs and Tbr2::GFP transgenic embryos for BPs and NBNs.

title: Tet2 is required for Socs activation in immune response cells [RNA-seq_mouse]
summary: Purpose: We have previously established an in vitro murine model that recapitulates the transformed phenotype of primary Tet2-/- mast cells expressing the Kit kinase domain mutant allele, D816V, that is both an oncogene and characterises patients with mastocytosis. To better understand the molecular basis of this cooperation and to further our understanding of role of Tet2 during inflammation and in other immune system disorders, we used this same in vitro primary cell system for genome wide studies to identify genes and genomic loci that are deregulated when these two mutations cooperate in mast cells.

title: Hepatic RNA expression profile analysis of antibiotics treated and untreated Clonorchis sinensis-infected mice
summary: Study whether IL-33 participates in the cholangiopathies during C. sinensis infection,and whether the gut microbiota participates in the pathogenesis of clonorchiasis
design: we performed transcriptional profiling analysis by RNA sequencing of liver RNA isolated from antibiotics treated and untreated 35 days post C. sinensis-infected WT and IL-33-/- mice,in quadruplicate,using Illumina HiSeq X-TEN

title: RNA-Seq analysis of melanoma cells, B16F10, in the presence of hypochlorous acid (HOCl)
summary: We evaluated the changes in the transcriptome of a melanoma cell line, B16F10, and spleen isolated murine T cells when in the presence of hypochlorous acid (HOCl) using RNA-sequencing technologies.

title: Zfp521 is essential for the quiescence and maintenance of adult hematopoietic stem cells under stress
summary: To further characterize Zfp521-dependent genes and the molecular pathways involved in the regulation of hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) function, we conducted RNA-Seq analysis of HSC sorted from Zfp521fl/fl and Zfp521-CKO chimeric mice 2 months after transplantation.

title: RNA-seq analysis of mice hypothalamus tissues.
summary: Analysis of mice hypothalamus genes differentially expressed in in weightlessness, noise and low air pressure condition.

title: Airway-Associated Macrophages in Homeostasis and Repair
summary: We isolated CD45+ cells after injury (Uninjured, Day1, Day4 and Day7) and CD45+F4/80+ cells from tracheal mesenchyme and dissociated lung, as well as CD45+ cells from peeled tracheal epithelium.

title: Next Generation Sequencing Facilitates Quantitative Analysis of Wild Type and Otud1-/- distal colonic tissue Transcriptomes adjacent to tumors
summary: Conclusion: Otud1-/- mice are more sensitive to azoxymethane(AOM)-Dextran sulfate (DSS) induced colon tumorigenesis
design: 6 weeks WT and Otud1-/- C57BL/6 male mice were Intraperitoneal injection AOM at the day 0, followed by 3 cycles of 4 days 1.5% DSS and 14 days water. At day 81, Then distal tumor-filled colon was taken out, then tumor were removed and the RNA of colon tissue adjacent to tumors is extracted by Trizol method, followed by eukaryotic RNA-seq and associated analysis

title: Transcriptomic analysis of hepatic genes in DEN-treated wildtype and Sesn3 knockout mice
summary: RNA-seq was performed on mRNA samples purified from the liver of wildtype (WT) and Sesn3 knockout (KO) mice.

title: RNA sequencing of Mus musculus thymic lymphomas [ATM and RAG2]
summary: RNA sequencing of Mus musculus thymic lymphomas

title: Transcriptome analysis of meiotic prophase spermatocytes in Zfp541 +/-  and Zfp541 KO mice
summary: ZFP541 is one of the candidates for a transcriptional regulator during mouse meiotic prophase. In order to address the role of ZFP541, transcriptomes of meiotic prophase-enriched population were compared between Zfp541 +/- and Zfp541 KO testes by RNA-seq. The meiotic prophase-enriched population was isolated from Zfp541 +/-  and Zfp541 KO testes at postnatal day 18 (P18), on the Rec8-3FH-GFP KI background by fluorescent sorting of GFP positive cells.

title: Transcriptional profiling of BoNT/A-induced lung injury in mice
summary: In this study, we performed time course RNAseq profiling on mouse lungs induced by  intratracheal inoculation of BoNT/A. We systematically identified the lung intrinsic responses related to pulmonary botulism. These data highlight the ability of BoNT/A to induce acute inflammatory respones

title: Gene Expression Profiling in progesterone-induced HGSC development.
summary: Here we show that ovarian progesterone is a crucial endogenous factor inducing metastatic ovarian cancer in a mouse model of high-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC). To examine the molecular signaling pathways underlying progesterone (P4)-induced HGSC development, we performed gene-expression profiling using RNA sequencing.
design: mRNA profiles of wild type (Ovid) mice, DKO (Dicer Pten conditional KO) mice and bilateral ovariectomy DKO mice, and  bilateral ovariectomy DKO mice with treated P4  were generated by RNA sequencing, in triplicate, using Illumina NextSeq500.

title: Mitochondrial transfer of the mutant human ND6T14484C gene causes visual loss and optic neuropathy
summary: In this study we investigated the effects of mutant human ND6 on mouse optic nerves

title: RNAseq data from intravascular vs parenchymal cells during Mtb infection
summary: Bulk RNAseq data looking at transcriptional differences between Mtb-specific T cells in the lung, vs those in the vasculature (with naive, CD44low controls) during Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Allowing us an unbiased way to discern differentially expressed genes in the two tissue spaces.

title: RNA-seq analysis of gene expression in cells during Ascl1 mediated astrocyte-to-neuron conversion.
summary: We analyzed the transcriptomic changes in cells sorted from astrocyte-to-neuron conversion at different stages, identified the differentially expressed genes (DEGs), and functionally validated the critical DEGs.

title: Mesenchymal stromal cells orchestrate the overhaul of leukemia bone marrow microenvironment via educating macrophages [in vivo]
summary: RNAseq were performed to analyze the transcriptomic differences between macrophage and MSC-educated macrophages in vivo.
design: RNAseq: Six macrophage samples and six MSC-educated macrophage samples from two individual mice.

title: Mesenchymal stromal cells orchestrate the overhaul of leukemia bone marrow microenvironment via educating macrophages [in vitro]
summary: RNAseq were performed to analyze the transcriptomic differences between macrophages and MSC-educated macrophages in vitro.

title: Mesenchymal stromal cells orchestrate the overhaul of leukemia bone marrow microenvironment via educating macrophages
summary: RNAseq were performed to analyze the transcriptomic differences between healthy homeostatic MSC, pre-leukemic MSC and recovered MSC.

title: Single cell RNA sequence discover the musculoskeletal tissue cell atlas during limb development
summary: By using single cell RNA-seq,We dissect the cellular heterogeneity and transcriptome profiles during limb development, and reveal the characteristic features of limb development and musculoskeletal stem/progenitor cell populations involved in limb lineage development. Our study therefore systematically decoded molecular markers and cellular program of limb development that would shed lights on limb developmental biology.

title: Single cell RNA seq analysis of postnatal mouse utricle
summary: Undamaged utricular sensory epithelia from P2, P4, and P6 mice were isolated using FACS and underwent Smartseq-2 protocol for single cell RNA seq. Data was generated using Illumina NextSeq 500, paired end, 75-150bp reads with median depth of ~0.5 million reads per cell.

title: TET1 regulates reprogramming with Vitamin C and relatively small molecules
summary: We found a small molecule-DKG, relative to Vitamin C, could replace the function of Viamin C during reprogramming. After comparing transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) of  this molecule to vitamin C, it could provide a framework for more mechanism.

title: Whole-transcriptome profiling of regenerating olfactory epithelium following loss of CBX paralogs
summary: The polycomb group protein, CBX8, is a neuron-specific component of Polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1) in the adult olfactory epithelium. We performed loss of function assays in an in vitro model of the regeneratng olfactory epithelium to determine the role of CBX8 in adult olfactory neurogenesis. Whole-transcriptome analysis highlighted the importance of CBX8-PRC1 in the regulation of adult neurogenesis in the olfactory epithelium.
design: Examination of cells treated with lentivirus-packaged short hairpin construct against non-targeting control (shCTR), Cbx7 (shCbx7), and Cbx8 (shCbx8); 3 biologic replicates per treatment.

title: Transcriptomic analysis of cultured primed synovial fibroblasts from monosodium urate crystal-induced arthritis in the mouse (validation set of samples)
summary: Repeated challenge of synovial fibroblasts with MSU crystals in vivo induced inflammatory priming

title: The Aim2 inflammasome exacerbates atherosclerosis in Jak2 clonal hematopoiesis bulk Cd11b+ cell RNA-Seq
summary: Bulk-cell RNA-Sequencing of CD11b+ cells harvest from spleens from wild-type or ldlr-/- mice harboring bone marrow with Jak2V617F mutations
design: Wild-type C57b6 mice with bone marrow from littermate control or mice with and Mx1-Cre drivin Jak2V617F expression were harvested and CD11b cells from spleens were isolated using magnetic beads and sequenced. In parallel ldlr-/- mice with bone marrow from littermate control or Mx1-Cre Jak2V617F were subjected to a seven week western type diet to induce hypercholesteremia, then CD11b cells were harvested from spleens and sequenced.

title: Cdkn2a loss in a model of neurofibroma demonstrates stepwise tumor progression to atypical neurofibroma and MPNST
summary: Plexiform neurofibromas (PN) are benign nerve sheath Schwann cell tumors, common in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), that are characterized by biallelic mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene. Atypical neurofibromas (ANF) show additional frequent loss of CDKN2A/Ink4a/Arf and may be precursor lesions of aggressive malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST). We combined loss of Nf1 in developing

title: Gene expression profile of WT and PD-1 -/- CD8+ T cells from murine skin (ear)
summary: Gene expression changes were computed between naïve, WT and PD-1 -/- T Cells. WT or PD-1 -/- OT-1+ CD8+ donor T cells were sorted from the ear skin of recipient mice at day 14 after VACV-OVA skin scarification. Naïve CD8+ OT-1 T cells were isolated from lymph node and spleen of naive mice by negative selection on MACS beads

title: RNA profiling of Suv39h1 overexpressed MLL-AF9 induced acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells
summary: Acute myeloid leukemias (AMLs) with rearrangement of the mixed-lineage leukemia (MLL) gene are the most aggressive hematopoietic malignancies. By analyzing the clinical data, we found the expression of SUV39H1 was significantly decreased in AML patients and MLL-AF9 (MA9) induced AML mice, in comparison with controls. Remarkably, when overexpress Suv39h1 in MA9 AML mice, the survival of AML mice was significantly prolonged.To examined the mechanism mediated by Suv39h1 overexpression (SUV-OE), we performed the RNAseq profiling of SUV-OE MA9 AML cells and control cells.

title: Gene expression profiling using RNA-Seq data of MMTV-Wnt1 tumor tissue from mice treated with E7386
summary: We conducted an RNA-Seq analysis using total RNA extracted from MMTV-Wnt1 tumor tissues resected from mice orally administered E7386 at 25 or 50 mg/kg twice daily, or vehicle, for 3 days (Day 4) or 7 days (Day 8) and examined the differentially expressed gene levels compared with vehicle at days 4 and 8.

title: Gene expression profile of ileum, jejunum and colon
summary: The gene expression of ileum, jejunum and colon.

title: Inducible stem cell-derived embryos capture mouse morphogenetic events in vitro
summary: We report the analysis by inDrop single cell sequencing of mouse embryos at embryonic day E5.5 and E6.5 as well as the analysis of stem cell derived synthetic embryos at day 4 of development generated with the standard protocol (Sozen et al., 2018) and the new protocol reported in this study. We find that the visceral endoderm-like layer of the synthetic embryos generated with the new protocol is much more similar to the visceral endoderm of mouse embryos than the layer of the synthetic embryos generated with the standard protocol, and this new and improved visceral endoderm-like layer endows these novel synthetic embryos with broader developmental potential

title: Gene expression profiling in murine mononuclear phagocyte lineage cells
summary: To understand the mechanism underlying monocyte and dendritic cell development through the regulation of Irf8 expression by the 56 kb downstream (+56 kb) Irf8 enhancer, we performed transcriptome analysis of bone marrow cells and splenocytes from wild-type, the Irf8 +56 kb enhancer-deficient, and IRF8-deficient mice. Taken together with the epigenetic profiling of mononuclear phagocyte lineage cells in these mice, the Irf8 +56 kb enhancer-mediated high Irf8 expression in hematopoietic progenitor cells promote type 1 classical dendritic cell (cDC1) differentiation, while low Irf8 expression in progenitors led to Ly6C+ monocyte development.

title: Loss of ESRP1 blocks mouse oocyte development and leads to female infertility
summary: Alternative splicing(AS) contributes to gene diversification through RNA-binding proteins, but AS regulation during germline development remains largely undefined. Here, we report a comprehensive set of mRNA splicing events mediated by epithelial splicing regulatory proteins 1(Esrp1) to regulate mouse oocyte development. Collectively, our data highlights that ESRP1-mediated AS program are required for oocyte development and female fertility maintainance.
design: MII oocytes from 6-week-old WT and Esrp1-KO females. RNA profiling data form both groups was collected from four biological replicates.

title: RNA-seq of SI adenoma tissue from ApcMin and ApcMin-PCdel Mice
summary: Adenomas derived from PCdel mice exhibited reduced expression of paneth cell marker genes as well as Wnt3.

title: Genome-wide identification of myoblast circular RNAs
summary: We performed deep RNA-sequencing on ribosomal-depleted RNA isolated from a 6-day differentiation time-course of murine C2C12 myoblasts. We uncovered a total of 37,751 unique circRNA expressed from 6943 hosting genes.

title: The differential gene expression of the dentate gyrus between WT and KO mice as well as between Fst knockout and overexpressing mice
summary: we aim to find the possible pathway and mechanism whereby Fst mediates neurogenesis and spatial learning by utilising RNA-seq to identify differential hippocampal gene expression between WT and KO mice as well as between KO and Fst overexpression mice
design: Three samples in each group and each sample was collected from three different mice.

title: Comparison of peroxide-inducible gene expression in cells with native or redox-insensitive Stat3
summary: To explore the biological role of Stat3 oxidation we created murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) that express either WT-Stat3 or a redox-insensitive mutant of Stat3 (Stat3-C3S). The Stat3-C3S cells differed from WT-Stat3 cells in morphology, proliferation and resistance to oxidative stress; in response to cytokine stimulation they displayed elevated Stat3 tyrosine phosphorylation and Socs3 expression, implying that Stat3-C3S is insensitive to oxidative inhibition.

title: 19-11-D Gene expression levels in Ninj1 KO BMDMs
summary: We have identified mouse Ninj1 as a protein responsible for plasma membrane integrity following cell death stimuli. Ninj1 KO BMDMs have a distinct bubble morphology wherein cell cytoplasmic contents fail to be released following cell death. To determine contributing factors to Ninj1 KO morphology, we performed RNAseq in WT and Ninj1 KO murine BMDMs with or without priming.
design: RNA was extracted RNAseq from primary mouse bone marrow derived macrophages (BMDMs) from WT C57BL/6 and Ninj1 KO mice

title: RNA-seq profiling of C/EBPβ-overexpressing myoblasts [proliferating myoblasts]
summary: We previously identified C/EBPβ as an inhibitor of myogenic differentiation and a regulator of muscle satellite cell self-renewal. We found that C/EBPβ is regulated during the transition from proliferation to growth arrest in myoblasts and overexpression of C/EBPβ in myoblasts promotes cell growth arrest in vitro and improves engraftment of satellite cells into the stem cell niche in vivo. To identify the molecular mechanism by which C/EBPβ regulates myoblast proliferation and growth arrest, we performed RNA-seq on C/EBPβ-overexpressing myoblasts.

title: RNAseq of mRNA from splenic and hepatic CD8 T cells in ND and CD-HFD mice
summary: In this study we want to compare the gene expression profile of CD44+CXCR6+ CD8+ T cells from the liver of ND and CD-HFD mice with hepatic CD44+CXCR6neg and splenic CD44+ CX3CR1neg CD8 T cells of ND and CD-HFD mice.  This comparison will reveal transcriptional signatures of hepatic CD44+CXCR6+ CD8+ T cells in CD-HFD responsible for causing liver pathology in NASH.
design: splenic and hepatic CD8 T cell populations in different diets (ND and CD-HFD)

title: Analysis of effects of TM4SF5 deficiency in inguinal white adipose tissue
summary: There are limited studies of TM4SF5, even though it plays a role in cell proliferation functions as lysosomal membrane amino acid sensor. In current studies, we aimed to study the role of TM4SF5 in mitochondrial homeostasis in adipocytes.

title: Transcriptome sequencing reveals high-salt diet-induced abnormal liver metabolic pathways in mice
summary: we analyzed the influence of a high-salt diet on liver by transcriptome sequencing. We found that after high-salt feeding, many metabolic abnormalities had formed based on transcriptome sequencing results. Analyses of differentially expressed genes revealed that at least 15 enzyme activities and the metabolism of multiple substances were affected by a high-salt diet. Moreover, a variety of signaling, and metabolic pathways, as well as biological functions, including some known pathways and many novel ones, such as retinol metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, steroid hormone biosynthesis, and signaling pathways, were involved in liver dysfunction due to a high-salt diet.
design: Liver mRNA profiles of  normal mice (fed with normal chow) and the high salt group (fed with sodium-rich chow (containing 6% NaCl)) for 6 weeks.

title: T11, AT3, PyMT-M, 2208L GEMM tumors treated with H3B-8800
summary: The objective is to identify splicing and expression changes that occur after spliceosome inhibition in triple-negative breast cancer using immune competent GEMM tumors.

title: RNAseq in Pten enhancer wild-type or deleted mouse T-ALLs
summary: C57BL6 mice harboring Pten enhancer (PE) conditional knockout NOTCH1-induced leukemias were treated with vehicle (control) or tamoxifen to induce isogenic deletion of PE. Here we report the gene expression profile of leukemic blasts obtained from the spleen from control- or tamoxifen-treated leukemic mice. GSEA analysis show a significant enrichment of Pten signature genes, consistent with a role of PE in regulating Pten expression.
design: RNAseq analysis of leukemic spleens in two genotypes and four or five samples per genotype.

title: Cooperation between distinct cancer drivers dictates inter-tumor heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma
summary: We generate multiple models of liver cancer to study heterogeneity at different levels

title: Transcriptomic analysis of mouse RTN neurons
summary: We report data from single cell sequencing analysis of individual RTN neurons harvested from brainstem slices

title: Tamoxifen treatment as a therapeutic approach in a murine model of X-linked myotubular myopathy (Mtm1-/y)
summary: In this study, we performed RNA sequencing on tibialis anterior muscle of male mice of 7 weeks of age. WT and Mtm1 deficient (Mtm1-/y) mice as well as tamoxifen-treated WT and tamoxifen-treated Mtm1-/y mice were sequenced.
design: The study is composed of 4 groups of mice: WT, Mtm1-/y, WT Tamox and Mtm1-/y Tamox. Each group was composed of triplicates or quadruplicates. The comparison of transcriptome profiles across the different genotypes was assessed in this study.

title: Genetic surexpression of human BIN1 as a therapeutic approach in a murine model of X-linked myotubular myopathy (Mtm1-/y)
summary: In this study, we performed RNA sequencing on tibialis anterior muscle of male mice at 7 weeks of age. WT and Mtm1 deficient (Mtm1-/y) mice were sequenced. The rescued mice, Mtm1-/y mice crossed with TgBIN1 mice (Mmt1-/yTgBIN1) and the associated control mice TgBIN1 were also sequenced.

title: Genetic downregulation of Dnm2 as a therapeutic approach in a murine model of X-linked myotubular myopathy (Mtm1-/y)
summary: In this study, we performed RNA sequencing on tibialis anterior muscle of male mice. WT and Mtm1 deficient (Mtm1-/y) mice as well as on Dnm2+/- mice and on Mtm1-/y mice crossed with Dnm2+/- (Mtm1-/yDnm2+/-) were sequenced. A longitudinal follow up was established by sequencing all the genotypes at E18.5, 2w and 7w.
design: The study is composed of 4 groups of mice: WT, Mtm1-/y, Dnm2+/- and Mtm1-/yDnm2+/-, for each age. Each group was composed from 2 to 5 replicates. The comparison of transcriptome profiles across different ages and different genotypes was assessed in this study.

title: Dnm2 downregulation by antisense oligonucleotide (ASO1) injections rescue a murine model of autosomal dominant centronuclear myopathy (Dnm2SL/+)
summary: In this study, we performed RNA sequencing on tibialis anterior muscle of male mice. WT (injected with ASO control) and Dnm2SL/+ (injected with ASO control) mice as well as ASO1 injected Dnm2SL/+ mice and ASO1 injected WT mice were sequenced at 7w of age. ASO1 targets specifically Dnm2 ARN.
design: The study is composed of 4 groups of mice: WT ASO Control, Dnm2SL/+ ASO Control, WT ASO1 and Dnm2SL/+ ASO1. Each group was composed from 3 to 6 replicates. The comparison of transcriptome profiles across the different genotypes was assessed in this study.  UPDATE: [07-01-2024] The title and treatment of GSM4859606 were corrected. The labels of the raw gene counts matrix were corrected.

title: Dnm2 downregulation by antisense oligonucleotide (ASO1) injections rescue a murine model of recessive centronuclear myopathy (Bin1mck-/-)
summary: In this study, we performed RNA sequencing on tibialis anterior muscle of male mice. WT (injected with PBS) and Bin1mck-/- (injected with PBS) mice as well as ASO1 injected Bin1mck-/- mice and ASO1 injected WT mice were sequenced at 7 weeks of age. ASO1 targets specifically Dnm2 ARN.
design: The study is composed of 4 groups of mice: WT PBS, Bin1mck-/- PBS, WT ASO1 and Bin1mck-/- ASO1. Each group was composed of quadruplicates. The comparison of transcriptome profiles across the different genotypes was assessed in this study.

title: Transcriptional analysis of CD8+ T lymphocytes isolated from syngeneic MC38 tumors and tumor-draining lymph nodes from mice fed high-fat or control diet
summary: Examination of transcriptional changes associated with diet-induced obesity in CD8+ T lymphocytes that infiltrate syngeneic MC38 tumors.
design: Transcriptional analysis of CD8+ T cells sorted 12 days post-implantation from subcutaneous MC38 tumors or tumor-draining lymph node in C57BL6/J mice. Dataset includes 8 samples sorted from tumor-draining lymph nodes in mice fed control diet, 5 samples sorted from tumor-draining lymph nodes in mice fed high-fat diet, 8 samples sorted from dissociated MC38 tumors in mice fed control diet, and 5 samples sorted from dissociated MC38 tumors in mice fed high-fat diet.

title: Transcriptional analysis of MC38 colorectal tumor cells sorted from mice fed high-fat or control diet
summary: Examination of transcriptional changes associated with diet-induced obesity in syngeneic MC38 tumors.
design: Transcriptional analysis of GFP+ MC38 colorectal cancer cells sorted 12 days post-implantation from subcutaneous MC38 tumors in C57BL6/J mice. Dataset includes 8 samples from mice fed control diet and 6 samples from mice fed high-fat diet.

title: Transcriptional analysis of CD45+ leukocytes isolated from syngeneic MC38 tumors from mice fed high-fat or control diet
summary: Examination of transcriptional changes associated with diet-induced obesity in tumor-infiltrating CD45+ leukocytes from syngeneic MC38 colorectal tumors.

title: RNA sequencing of naïve, Th1 and Th2 polarised live CD4+ T cells from CD4Cre+ and CD4Cre+DOT1LFL/FL mice
summary: RNA sequencing of naïve, Th1 and Th2 polarised live CD4+ T cells from CD4Cre+ and CD4Cre+DOT1LFL/FL mice

title: Single cell RNAseq analysis of organotypic brain slice microglia
summary: Single cell RNA sequencing analysis was performed on microglia isolated from brain slices  (timepoints: 1 day, 1 week or 3 weeks in culture), 2D in vitro cultured microglia, and acutely isolated adult microglia. Differences in gene expression were examined to determine relative similarity to acutely isolated adult microglia.

title: Impaired transcriptional profile in the hippocampus following loss of Kdm5a
summary: KDM5A encodes a histone lysine demethylase that removes methyl groups from lysine 4 of histone H3, resulting in repression of target genes. In order to identify KDM5A targets, we profiled transcripts from hippocampi of WT and Kdm5a -/- mice. Loss of KDM5A resulted in dysregulation of 450 genes (FDR-corrected P ≤0.05 and log2 fold change ≥|0.3|), of which 191 genes were upregulated and 259 genes were downregulated.
design: Hippocampal transcriptional profiles from 6-8-week old wild type (WT) and Kdm5a -/- (KO) mice were generated by sequencing of 5 biological replicates per genotype using Illumina NextSeq 500.

title: RNA-seq analysis of Actn2 knockout in mouse cardiomyocytes
summary: The goal of this study is to analyze the impact of Actn2 depletion on transcription during cardiomyocyte maturation in mouse

title: Transcriptome analysis of naive B cells from CD19Cre and CD19Cre_STAT6vt mice
summary: To investigate how activated STAT6 modulates B cells development and function in vivo, we characterized mice that express a constitutively active version specifically in B cells. CD19Cre_STAT6vt mice show spontaneous phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of STAT6 in B cells.  Based on the finding that STAT6vt accumulates in the nucleus of naïve splenic B cells in CD19Cre_STAT6vt mice, we next determined the changes of the global transcriptome by RNAseq analysis.
design: We isolated naïve B cells by cell sorting (CD19+ CD3neg PIneg, purity >95%) from three age matched CD19Cre_STAT6vt and three CD19Cre control mice, purified total RNA and performed transcriptome analysis using the Illumina platform.

title: Memory like NK cells display stem cell like properties after Zika virus Infection
summary: Here we show that Zika virus infection induces memory like NK cells that express CD27. This subset shared transcriptional changes with memory CD8 T cells, stem cells and stem like T cells. These NK cells with memory and stemness features which we term NK memory stem cells (SCMNK) demonstrated greater antiviral potential. Transcriptional data of SCMNK and non-memory NK cells is presented.

title: Effect of acute systemic inflammation on the Cerebral Vasculature in mice
summary: To capture the global gene expression patterns in the cerebral vasculature following acute systemic inflammation, we injected the mice with LPS and sacrificed them after 15 min, 30 min, and 4 hrs, followed by the isolation of the cerebral vessels. RNA was isolated from the vessel lysates, followed by library preparation and RNA sequencing.
design: mRNA profiles of cerebral vessels isolated from the brains of mice (C57BL6, Wild type, 2-3 months old)  injected (intra peritoneal) with 10mg/kg LPS for 15 min, 30 min and 4 hrs or PBS. (n=3 in each group, every sample in each group includes the cerebral vessels from one male and one female mice pooled together)

title: Skeletal muscle aging and pathways regulated by 15-PGDH inhibition
summary: To identify signalling pathways and genes regulated by 15-PGDH inhibition by SW033291

title: Effects of novel selective androgen receptor modulator, TEI-SARM2, on gene expression profile changes in skeletal muscle
summary: TEI-SARM2 is a novel selective androgen receptor modulator. To assess the effects of TEI-SARM2 on skeletal muscle, we generated myofiber specific ARKO using HSA-Cre and AR flox mice (mARKO). Male mARKO and littermate control (ARL2/Y) mice underwent ORX or not. Nine days after ORX, the mice were treated with TEI-SARM2 (10 mg/kg weekly, p.o.) or vehicle (weekly, p.o.) for another 2 weeks. After euthanasia, the bulbocavernosus (BC) muscles were collected and total RNA was extracted.
design: mRNA profiles of bulbocavernosus (BC) muscles obtained from control  and mARKO mice treated with 1) sham operation, 2) ORX and vehicle administration or 3) ORX and TEI-SARM2 administration, were generated by sequencing using Illumina Myseq separately for control and mARKO.

title: RNA-seq analysis of gestationally Cd-exposed hepatic transcriptome
summary: We report the RNA-sequencing analysis of hepatic RNA isolated from CD-1 mice following gestational exposure to 500ppb CdCl2. We show that gestational Cd exposure alters the hepatic gene expression of female, but not male offspring in numerous pathways related to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction leading to endoplasmic reticulum stress that ultimately drives metabolic disruption of insulin signaling.
design: Examination of three different timepoints and one exposure group

title: Abi1 gene dose study in PyVT breast tumors
summary: To execute RNA-Seq analysis of PyMT breast tumors studied in animals with and heterozygous and homozygous states of Abi1 gene

title: Transcriptomic landscape of radiation-induced murine thyroid proliferative lesions
summary: This study aims at the identification and characterization of early-state radiation-associated neoplastic processes by histologic and transcriptomic analyses of thyroid tissues derived from a mouse model. Comprehensive histological examination of 246 thyroids (164 exposed, 82 non-exposed) was carried out. Proliferative and normal tissues from exposed cases and normal tissue from non-exposed cases were collected by laser-capture microdissection, followed by RNAseq transcriptomic profiling using a low input 3`-library preparation protocol, differential gene expression analysis and functional association by Gene Set Enrichment Analysis.

title: Expression profile of mouse embryonic stem cells upon knockdown or overexpression of YAP
summary: We  looked at the expression profiles of embyonic stem cells (ESCs) 48 hours after YAP siRNAs transfection, to knockdown YAP expression, or after pCAG-YAP transfection, to over-express YAP protein. Total RNA was isolated from three independent experiments and analyzed by RNA-seq.
design: mRNA profile of ESCs knockdown for YAP expression (siRNAs) vs CTR cells (scrambled) and mRNA profile of ESCs overexpressing YAP  (pCAG-YAP plasmid) vs CTR cells (pCAG-GFP). Each condition has three independent biological replicates.

title: Antigen-specific and bystander epidermal CD8+ resident memory T cells
summary: RNAseq analysis of epidermal OT-I Trm generated by VV-OVA infection or DNFB-pull

title: RNA-seq of primary mouse B cell progenitor populations after activation with LPS
summary: Naive resting B-cells were purified from bone marrow from C57BL/6 mice using flow cytometry sorting. Naive B cells were activated with LPS and harvested 3 hours, 10 hours or 33 hours after the LPS treatment. Expanded activated B cells (CD22+ CD138-) and plasmablasts (CD22- CD138+) were  also harvested on day 4 post-stimulation.

title: Identification of a Novel PP2A Regulator, WNK1, as Critical For Uterine Function
summary: We report the transcriptomic profile of uterine tissues obtained from the control (Wnk1f/f) and Wnk1 cKO (PGRCre/+;Wnk1f/f) mice during pseudopregnancy day 4.5.
design: RNA-seq analyses were conducted on whole uterus during the receptive phase of pseudopregnancy.

title: Transcriptome sequencing analysis of LncMyod-knockdown satellite cells by RNA-seq
summary: To understand the effect of LncMyod knockdown on cultured satellite cells, we isolated satellite cells from mouse hindlimb and cultured them in vitro with siRNA treatment targeting LncMyod. Following RNA-seq showed that loss of LncMyod leads to difficiencies in myogenic differentiation.

title: Transciption profiling of leptin receptor-expressing neurons in the Nucleus of the Solitary Tract
summary: This study aims to identify and compare unique transcription profiles of neurons in the NTS that express the leptin receptor. We conducted single-cell patch RNA-sequencing experiments to classify neurons first by their unique firing properties and, second, transciptional profiles. We found two unique cellular populations: type1 and type2 distinguishable by firing patterns and transciption profile.

title: Retrograde labelling and RNA deep sequencing of olfactory bulb projection neurons [bulk RNA-seq]
summary: To characterize the molecular diversity of olfactory bulb projection neurons we used viral targeting and Fluorescence Activated Nuclei Sorting (FANS) to enrich for piriform cortex-projecting or AON-projecting neurons, and bulk RNA deep sequencing (bulk RNA deep seq) to comprehensively characterize their transcriptomes.

title: Transcriptomic analysis from lateral ganglionic eminence (LGE) of wild type and Gsx2 germline knock-out mice.
summary: RNA-seq analysis was used to identify genes that are differentially expressed between wild type and Gsx2 null mouse LGEs.

title: RNA sequencing of wild type and FXR KO CD8+T cells in fed/fasted LCMV-infected mice
summary: Conditional ablation of FXR in T cells was achieved with CD4-Cre Nr1h4fl/fl mice. Twenty thousend congenically marked naive (CD44- CD62L+) WT and FXR KO T cells carrying the OT-I transgenic TCR were cotransferred into lymphoreplete hosts. Recipients were challenged with LCMV-OVA and allowed to feed Ad libitum (AL) or fasted (Fs) for 24h beginning at 6pm on D5 post-infection. Splenic CD44+ effector cells of each genotype were FACS-purified (double-sorted) at the end of the starvation period.
design: Effects of genotype (WT vs FXR KO) and feeding status (AL vs Fs)

title: Profiling Kupffer cells with different origins in NASH
summary: Kupffer cells (KCs) self-renew by local proliferation in the adult independently from monocytes (Mos). However, how they maintain during chronic metabolic disorders such as non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) remains ill-defined. We characterized KCs during NASH and observed diversity in the KC pool, with a significant fraction of monocyte-derived KCs (MoKCs). Here, we aim to uncover the transcriptional landscapes of KCs subsets found in a mouse model of methionine and choline deficient (MCD)-diet induced non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH).

title: Analysis of gene expression changes in the spinal cord during chronic pain.
summary: Purpose: The goal of this study is to examine the DEGs in the spinal cord of schiatic nerve cuff model mouse using RNA-seq compared with control (sham).

title: Spatial RNA sequencing of regenerating mouse hindlimb muscle
summary: We report a series of spatial transcriptomics datasets of regenerating mouse muscle tissue generated with the 10x Genomics Visium platform.

title: Radiation dose-fractionation effects on immune modulation in murine mammary tumors
summary: Radiation therapy (RT) induces pleiotropic effects on the tumor immune microenvironment, but how these changes are modulated by radiation dose-fractionation is not well understood. Our in vivo data murine data suggests that while changes evoked by RT in the tumor immune compartment are largely concordant between radiation regimens, several key immunological processes are differentially regulated by radiation dose-fractionation.
design: Wildtype female C57BL/6 mice were injected with AT3-OVA triple negative mammary tumor cells orthotopically into the mammary fat pad and received local RT to the tumors using either the 3x4Gy regimen or the 1x20Gy regimen. Tumors were harvested at days 5 and 13 post completion of RT, processed into single cell suspensions and stained for the pan-leukocyte marker CD45.2. CD45.2+ immune cells were sorted by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and underwent RNA extraction. Only samples with an RNA integrity number (RIN) of greater than 8.5 were processed for library preparation. Mock-irradiated tumors from mice anaesthetized as per their irradiated counterparts were used as controls (3x0 Gy and 1x0 Gy, respectively).

title: Comparing mRNA expression of Myc/NrasG12V and Myc/Akt1 driven liver tumors
summary: To analyze mRNA expression of Myc/NrasG12V and Myc/Akt1 driven liver tumors (HCC), we generated HCCs with elevated MYC expression and activated Raf-MEK-ERK or Akt1 signaling. To trigger tumor development, we co-delivered transposable elements encoding for Myc and oncogenic NrasG12V or myristoylated Akt1 via hydrodynamic injection into the hepatocytes of C57BL/6 wildtype mice and analyzed the transcriptomes of the developed tumors.
design: mRNA expression of Myc/NrasG12V and Myc/Akt1 driven liver tumors was compared via mRNAseq analysis

title: Comparing mRNA expression between carrier treated and sorafenib treated Myc/NrasG12V liver tumors
summary: To profile determinants of sensitivity and resistance towards the multikinase inhibitor sorafenib in liver cancer (HCC), we generated HCCs with elevated MYC expression and activated Raf-MEK-ERK signaling. To trigger tumor development, we co-delivered transposable elements encoding for Myc and oncogenic NrasG12V via hydrodynamic injection into the hepatocytes of C57BL/6 wildtype mice. To characterize the response of Myc/NrasG12V HCCs towards sorafenib, we analyzed their transcriptomes after three weeks of sorafenib or carrier treatment.

title: Mechanical Regulation of Stem Cell Proliferation and Fate Decisions by their Differentiated Daughters
summary: RNAseq analysis of suprabasal cells in the epidermis of control and K10rtTA;TRESpastin (which depolymerize microtubules) at E16.5 were performed. We observed the premature differentiation of the barrier and increased actomyosin contractility in suprabasal differentiated cells upon microtubule disruption compared to control, and proved the increased actomyosin contractility caused by microtubule depolymerization leads to basal stem cell hyperproliferation during epidermal development.

title: RNA-sequencing of Control and Bisphenol A (BPA) exposed mice livers.
summary: To elucidate the molecular perturbations underlying the connection of low-dose prenatal BPA exposure to cardiometabolic diseases, we assessed the liver transcriptome in both male and female mouse offspring exposed to 5ug/kg/day BPA and corn oil (control) during gestation.
design: Liver samples were dissected from mice offspring at 24 weeks and flash frozen then stored at -80C. RNA was extracted using the Qiagen MiRNeasy Mini Kit. There were 4 groups: 1) Male corn oil (control)  2) Male BPA exposed 3) Female corn oil (control) 4) Female BPA exposed.  There were 4 samples per group (Total samples =16).

title: Differential gene expression in the tumorigenic liver of Nod2-/- and wild type mice
summary: We report that Nod2, a pattern recognition receptor, protects from high fat diet-dependent liver malignancy and this protection is accompanied by changes in gene expression for cell proliferation, inflammation and steroid biosynthesis.
design: We compared RNA populations in the liver from WT and Nod2-/- mice treated with a carcinogen and maintained on high fat diet for 30 weeks.

summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) from proliferating primary myogenic progenitor cells (MPCs) were incubated on myotubes for 12 and 24 hours

title: Single Cell Sequencing Reveals Artifactual Gene Expression Following Dissociation in All CNS Cells

design: Three groups, FAK-WT, FAK-null and FAK-kinase dead, with three biological replicates per group.

title: Screening of miR-379 target RNAs by comparison of WT and miR-379 KO mouse primary kidney mesangial cells by using CLASH technique [RNA-Seq]
summary: We screened for miR-379 targets in primary mesangial cells from wild-type vs. miR-379KO mice using unbiased CLASH sequencing approach and identified the redox protein thioredoxin (Txn1) and mitochondrial fission-1 protein (Fis1).

title: Early removal of senescent cells protects retinal ganglion cells loss in experimental ocular hypertension
summary: Experimental ocular hypertension (IOP) induces senescence of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) that mimicks events occurring in human glaucoma. An established transgenic p16-3MR mouse model in which the systemic administration of the small molecule ganciclovir (GCV) selectively kills p16INK4a-expressing cells was used to compare  transcriptomes of retinas from IOP and control eyes in GCV-treated and non-treated mice, to investigate how experimental removal of senescent p16INK4a-positive cells impacts retinal cells in conditions resembling glaucoma.
design: All six mice carried the p16-3MR transgene. High IOP was induced in one eye of each of the 6 mice and the other was a normal IOP controls. Three mice were subsequently (the same day) treated with GCV and the other three were mock treated. GCV  injections were repeated daily for a total of three days, at which point the mice were sacrified, retinas were dissected and total RNA was isolated for transcriptomic analyses.

title: Effect of c-Myb Deficiency in Irf4/8-/- large pre-B cells
summary: Differential gene expression analysis comparing c-Myb-sufficient and -deficient Irf4/8-/- large pre-B cells. The results of this study are the first to demonstrate a role for c-Myb during the large pre-B cell stage of B lymphocyte development. The results provide insight into roles for c-Myb in regulating components of glucose metabolism in large pre-B cells as well as the differentiation of large pre-B cells to the small pre-B cell compartment.

title: Expression profiling of tumor endothelial cells [single cells]
summary: Blood (BEC) and lymphatic (LEC) endothelial cells were isolated from MT-ret tumors and 10x Genomics-based single-cell RNA-seq analysis was performed.

summary: Lymphatic endothelial cells (LEC) were isolated from MT-ret tumor tissue 12h after treatment with an Ang2-blocking antibody or control-IgG

summary: RNA sequencing of mouse islets from mice containing a pancreas-specific deletion of Glis3, and control littermates. Also, ChIP-seq analysis of Glis3 binding using a Glis3-eGFP mouse (endogenous Glis3 fused to enhanced GFP) and GFP antibody.

title: Transcriptome analysis of mouse embrynic fibroblast cells lacking multiple core clock genes
summary: We established a cell line lacking endougous CRY, PER, and NR1D proteins (CPN_KO).  By comparing the transcriptome of CPN_KO cells and the cells expressing CRY proteins (PN_KO), genes affected by CRY were analyzed.   Parental cells expressing NR1D proteins (CP_KO) were also analyzed to identify genes regulated by NR1D proteins.

summary: Spleens were harvested from B6.Sle1.Yaa at 2, 4, and 7 months of age or from LCMV infected mice 8 days post infection. RNA-seq was employed to assess transcriptional changes in these cells throughout disease progression.

summary: We report the application of RNA-sequence in Primary PTECs, by obtaining the sequence from cisplatin treated wild-type PTECs infected with Ad-FXRα2 or Ad-VP16

title: Deletion of the gene encoding the N-methyl-D Aspartate Receptor GluN1 subunit in Schwann cells causes ultrastructural changes in Remak bundles and hypersensitivity in pain processing
summary: Mouse  DRGs (n=3 per genotype)  were isolated from a novel mouse model with conditional deletion of Glun1 in Schwann cells (GluN1-)  and corresponding  littermate controls (Glun+).  P0Cre recombinase is the driver. Transcriptome profiling of DRGs revealed 138 differenially regulated genes in Glun1- mice.  On third of the regulated genes are known to be involved in pain processing.

title: The identification of differentially expressed genes in granulosa cell specific Cbfb and Runx2 double knockout mice
summary: The removal of RUNX1/2 and CBFb affects the expression of many genes involved in ovulation and CL formation in mice

summary: We utilize RNA-Seq to evaluate how loss of Sestrin1,2, a conserved set of stress-inducible proteins, alters the metabolism and quiescent state of young (2-3 months) Muscle Stem Cells (MuSCs) during the regenerative response.

title: Identification of Hepatic Genes Regulated by ATF3 using Next Generation Sequencing
summary: This study aimed to investigate how many genes were regulated by hepatocyte ATF3. C57BL/6J mice were injected intravenously with adeno-associated virus (AAV) expressing human activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) under the control of an albumin promoter (AAV8-ALB-ATF3) or AAV8-ALB-Null). After 8 weeks, liver samples were used for RNA sequencing using Illumina NextSeq 500. Over 3000 genes were found to be up- or down-regulated by ATF3.
design: Ten weeks old C57BL/6J mice were intravenoulsy injected with AAV8-ALB-ATF3 or AAV8-ALB-Null (control) (n=8 per group). After 8 weeks, total RNA was extracted and cDNA libraries were prepared. RNA sequencing was carried out using Next-Seq 500. Data were analyzed using Illumina Softwares in BaseSpace.

title: Gene expression profiling of the vomeronasal organs in mice selectively bred for high voluntary wheel running activity and non-selected controls
summary: To examine the impact of selective breeding for voluntary wheel running activity on gene expression in the vomeronasal organ (VNO), RNAseq analysis was conducted in the VNO of 4 High Runner and 4 Control lines.

summary: Renca, a murine renal cell carcinoma, and B16F10, a murine melanoma, were transcriptionally profiled in a study designed to accompany an in vivo CRISPR screen to identify novel immunotherapy dependencies.

title: Quercetin promotes in vitro maturation of oocytes from humans and aged mice
summary: The flavonol compound quercetin is considered to be an anti-aging agent due to its cytoprotective actions as an antioxidant. The RNA sequencing analysis of oocytes after in vitro maturation from aged mice identified many genes altered by quercetin treatment and suggested that such treatment has a pronounced impact on genetic programs associated with mitochondrial dysfunction.
design: 15 MII stage oocytes after IVM from three mice were considered one group, and three replicates were assessed per group. Samples included groups collected with or without 10 μM quercetin treatment.

title: The effect of CDK6 expression on the murine transcriptome
summary: We performed RNA-seq analyses in BCR-ABL+ cells either expressing or lacking CDK6. 3 replicates per group were analysed.

title: Typical western diet exacerbates dystrophic neurite pathology in APP/PS1 and APP/PS1/Tau mouse models by reducing the clustering of microglia around β-amyloid plaques
summary: Here, we studied the interaction between dietary (TWD) and genetic factors (APPswe/PS1dE9 and tau P301L mutations) and their effect on memory, brain pathology, global gene expression and on insulin-Akt-GSK3β pathway in brain of mice with four different AD-linked genetic backgrounds: wild-type (AwTw), APPswe/PS1dE9 (A+Tw), P301Ltau (AwT+), and triple transgenic (A+T+).
design: The study comprised of 45 female mice, 12 wild-type (AwTw), 11 APP/PS1 transgenic (A+Tw), 12 tau P301L transgenic (AwT+) and 10 transgenic for both APP/PS1 and tau P301L (A+T+).

title: RNA extracted from the left ventricle of 3 different mouse heart disease models, wild type, mdx, and mdx sln+/- hearts
summary: We report that ablation of one SLN allele positively affects mouse mdx DMD heart failure model mice by several metrics including intracellular calcium handling.

title: Transcriptional response in ileum tissue from wild-type and Fat1+/- male mice
summary: Males were placed onto an all liquid diet with gradually increasing amounts of ethanol as follows:  no ethanol for 2 days, 1% (v/v) for 2 days, 2% for 2 days, 4% for 1 week, 5% for 1 week, and 6% for 3 weeks.  At the end of the experiment, one group from each genotype was injected with 5 mg/kg LPS.  Mice were then euthanized 24 hours later.

title: Effects of FOXN1 or AFF4 deficiency on gene expression in the skin
summary: Loss-of-function mutations in Foxn1 or Aff4 cause similar defects in skin morphology.  To determine whether these similar phenotypes result from similar changes in gene expression, skin from wild-type, Foxn1-null, or Aff4 conditional knockout (cko) mice was analysed by RNA-seq at a time when the animals were attempting to grow their first hair coats (P6).
design: RNA preparations from Foxn1-null or Aff4-cko mutants were compared to RNA preparations from their respective wild-type littermates.

title: SEZ cells populations
summary: Characterization of neural stem cells (NSC) from the adult rodent subependymal niche by flow cytometry and traceable nucleoside retention assays have indicated the co-existence of activated and quiescent NSC in this niche. Single-cell deep-sequencing has further revealed different NSC molecular states with regards to cell-cycle gene expression: quiescent, primed for activation, and fully activated. Here, we provide a multi-level procedure to classify all cells of the subependymal niche, without the need for reporter mice, into populations with coherent transcriptomes that can be functionally assayed. Our strategy reveals that primed NSC are slowly proliferating cells that contribute to NSC cultures and that neurospheres contain NSC which retain a primed-like molecular signature and exhibit slow cycling and long-term self-renewal. Our strategy provides a way to functionally assay NSC heterogeneity and to study quiescence levels in NSC populations.

summary: Several cell cycle genes were altered between Dll1+ and Dll1- population of tumor cells

summary: We found that fibroblasts derived from lung metastases display specific gene signatures related to distinct functional enrichments, including stress, ECM remodelling, and inflammation.

summary: The gene Ift88 is a gene critical for primary cilium biogenesis, the objective this study was to determine the transcriptome changes in Mitral leaflets in the absence of the gene.

title: Time-course transcriptomic profiling of C57BL/6 mouse neurons from the dorsal root ganglion before and after a carrageenan injection into the left hind paw
summary: Carrageenan injection induces tissue inflammation and high mechanosensitivity. Dorsal root ganglions contain the cellular body of the sensory neurons which project their axon to the periphery, monitoring this inflammation and transmitting the mechanical stimuli to the spinal cord. To explore whether the sensory neurons underwent transcriptional changes and how long these changes lasted, we injected carrageenan into the left hind paw of mice and sequenced the dorsal root ganglions related to this area 1, 3 and 30 days after the injection.

title: Quantitative Analysis of ERR gamma-driven pancreatic acinar cell transcriptome
summary: The goal of this study is to compare NGS-derived pancreatic acinar cell-based transcriptome profiling (RNA-seq) to evaluate ERR gamma-driven transcriptional program

title: Transcriptional profiling of naïve and in vitro activated B cells from WT and DOT1L KO mice
summary: We studied the role of the histone methyltransferase DOT1L in B cell development and differentiation. Here we generated RNA-seq data naive B cells from (WT) MB1+/-;Dot1L+/+ and Dot1L KO (MB1+/-;Dot1Lfl/fl) mice. This data was to define tissue specific expression signatures and it was compared with H3K79me2 ChIP-seq data from the same subsets.
design: RNA-seq from MACS sorted CD19+ naïve and actiavted B cells WT and Dot1L KO mice

summary: The goal of this study was to compare expression profiles of mouse Kras G12D Trp53 -/- lung cancer cells that have inactivated MGA compared to controls

title: Next Generation Sequencing of lung homogenate mRNA from 8-12 week male C57BL/6 mice following Sham, Carbon Black, Ozone, or Carbon Black-Ozone Co-exposure.
summary: While investigation of a single inhaled toxicant may be useful, the additive effects of toxicants interacting within the body can only be modelled through co-exposure. The purpose of this study is to understand how inhalation of carbon black and ozone alters the transcriptome, and if co-exposure incites unique, genome-wide changes in the lungs.
design: C57BL/6 mice (8-12 weeks old) were exposed to carbon black (10 mg/m3) and/or ozone (2 ppm) for a duration of (3 hours) over a single exposure (Day 1) or four independent exposures (Day 4). Lungs were removed, RNA isolated, and mRNA sequencing performed using the Illumina HiSeq. Libraries were built with the TruSeq® Stranded mRNA Library Prep Kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA) and run on the HiSeq 2500 (Illumina) in 51bp paired end reads. Fastq files were mapped and quantified using the mapping-based mode of Salmon 1.1.0.

title: Exploitable, highly context-specific astrocytes
summary: To investigate the functional heterogeneity of astrocytes from a defined brain region, we designed 14 experimental manipulations including Huntington's disease models, pathological challenges, ionic and GPCR signaling alterations, and analyzed the transcriptomic profiles of striatal astrocytes. From the analyses, we have identified context-specific changes of striatal astrocytes.
design: Total 48 samples from 24 adult mice were used in this data set. Astrocyte RiboTag AAV was injected into the striatum to extract RNA specifically from striatal astrocytes. We ablated dopaminergic neurons by MPTP, used an OCD mouse model (SAPAP3 knockout), and activated Gi-GPCR pathway in striatal astrocytes of R6/2 mice. After tissue homogenization, RNA was purified from (i) cleared lysate as the input sample, and (ii) astrocyte-specific ribosome-associated RNA precipitated via a hemagglutinin (HA) tag as the IP sample.

title: Exploitable, highly context-specific astrocytes
summary: To investigate the functional heterogeneity of astrocytes from a defined brain region, we designed 12 experimental manipulations including Huntington's disease models, pathological challenges, ionic and GPCR signaling alterations, and analyzed the transcriptomic profiles of striatal astrocytes. From the analyses, we have identified context-specific changes of striatal astrocytes.
design: Total 80 samples from 40 adult mice were used in this data set. Astrocyte RiboTag AAV was injected into the striatum to extract RNA specifically from striatal astrocytes. We designed several manipulations to ablate MSNs by quinolinic acid (QA), to induce neuroinflammation by lipopolysaccharide (LPS), to reduce potassium and calcium signals and to activate Gs-GPCR pathway in striatal astrocytes. After tissue homogenization, RNA was purified from (i) cleared lysate as the input sample, and (ii) astrocyte-specific ribosome-associated RNA precipitated via a hemagglutinin (HA) tag as the IP sample.

summary: Deletion of Lmna, encoding nuclear membrane protein LMNA, specifically in mouse cardiac myocytes activates BRD4 and leads to heart failure, arrhythmias, myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis, and premature death, which were partially rescued upon inhibition of BRD4.
design: RNA-seq from Cardiac myocytes from 6 control  (WT) and 6 Myocyte-Specific Lamin A/C Null Mice (Myh6-cre:LmnaF/F)

summary: We provide differentially gene expression between wt and Dhx9-/- CD8 T cells from LCMV infected mice.

title: Transcriptomic profiling of melanomas treated with BRAF inhibitor
summary: Since tumor early response is a timing sensitive progress, accurate time points for biopsy collection will provide a fundament for the investigation of the correlation between angiogenesis and BRAFi resistance. To this end, we recapitulated the clinical therapeutic process with a mouse model. SMM102, a BRAFi sensitive mouse cell line, was subcutaneously inoculated on both flanks of C57BL/6 mice. Mice were treated with BRAFi and sacrificed at different time point.
design: C57BL/6J mice (female, 6-8 weeks old) were subcutaneously injected with 1x105 SMM102 cells, two injections per mouse. Once tumors volumes reached 150-300 mm3, mice were treated with vehicle or PLX4032 (50 mg/kg, 5 days per week) by intraperitoneal injection (IP). Mice were sacrificed at day 3 and 6 for vehicle group. And for PLX4032 group, mice were sacrificed at day 3, 6, 18 and 27.

summary: We show that Ror2 mediated non-canonical Wnt signaling in the dental mesenchyme plays a critical role in cell proliferation and thereby regulates root development size in mouse molars. Furthermore, Cdc42 acts as a potential downstream mediator of Ror2 signaling in root formation.

There is also evidence that dendritic cells express IL33, however its function in these cells is not well understood.  To investigate the distinct function of IL33 in dendritic cells, deep sequencing of mRNA transcripts was conducted on FACS sorted DCs in mice lacking Il33 expression in CD11c expressing cells compared to control mice.

summary: Conclusion: Otud1-/- mice are more sensitive to azoxymethane(AOM)-Dextran sulfate (DSS) induced colon tumorigenesis

At day 81, Then distal tumor-filled colon was taken out and the RNA is extracted by Trizol method, followed by eukaryotic RNA-seq and associated analysis

title: Comparative RNAseq of Mouse Parp3+/+ and Parp3-/- Neural Stem Progenitor Cells (NPSC)
summary: To identify the biological pathways underlying impaired differentiation of Parp3-deficient NPSC to astrocytes, RNAseq of the Parp3+/+ and Parp3-/- astrocytes were performed 4 days upon differentiation. Briefly, NPSC were isolated from the forebrains of Parp3+/+ and Parp3-/- 8-day-old mice. Viable single cells were induced to differentiate into astrocytes for 4 days and samples were collected for total RNA isolation and RNA sequencing.

title: Cortical single-cell RNA sequencing of the microglia specific TREM2 inducible mouse models
summary: We induced TREM2 expression at 2 months of age in our TREM2 mouse models and harvested the animals at 4 months of age. The single cells from the cortex were isolated and subjected to the single-cell RNA seq to investigate the effects of TREM2 on the transcriptomic profiles at single cell level in healthy condition. Our data revealed that TREM2-WT expression triggered the downstream mTOR/EIF2 signaling pathways and activated microglia by elevating Apoe expression; whereas TREM2-R47H had no effects on mTOR/EIF2 signaling pathway and minor impact on activating microglia antigen presentation pathway.
design: Four mice (2 males and 2 females) were analyzed for each of the four groups, including TREM2-WT-Ctrl, TREM2-WT-Induced, TREM2-R47H-Ctrl, and TREM2-R47H-Induced.

title: Cortical single-cell RNA sequencing of the microglia specific TREM2 inducible mouse models in the early stage of amyloid deposition
summary: We induced TREM2 expression at birth in our 5xFAD/TREM2 mouse models and harvested the animals at 3.5 months of age. The single cells from the cortex were isolated and subjected to the single-cell RNA seq to investigate the effects of TREM2 on microglia transcriptomic profiles in the early stage of amyloid development. Our data showed that TREM2-WT, to a lesser extent of TREM2-R47H, restricted the disease associated microglia (DAM) signature at this stage.
design: Six mice (3 males and 3 females) were analyzed for each of the four groups, including 5xFAD/TREM2-WT-Ctrl, 5xFAD/TREM2-WT-Induced, 5xFAD/TREM2-R47H-Ctrl, 5xFAD/TREM2-R47H-Induced .

summary: Purpose of study is to assess changes in gene expression profiles of mesenchymal stem cell upon expression of H2BE71K/Q, H2BE76K/Q and H2BE113K/Q

summary: Immune evasion is a hallmark of KRAS-driven cancers, but underlying mechanism and clinical implications remain unclear.

title: Cardiac fibroblast proliferation rates and collagen expression mature early in life and do not change with advancing age [RNA-Seq]
summary: RNA sequencing from mouse hearts or PDGFR⍺ cardiac fibroblasts along time of aging.

title: Gene expression-based, mouse primary BC CML after knockdown of AMD1 gene.
summary: We report the gene expression profiling of mouse BC CML model which were knockdown with either shControl or shAMD1 constructs. By obtaining RNA from primary BC CML cells from those mice (n: 3 for each shRNA),we find that thousands gene were dysregulated by AMD1 knockdown.

title: Transcriptome analysis of CD45-CD31+ endothelial cells in ischemic hindlimb muscle after IL-35 injection
summary: We report the first time of the transcriptome difference between IL35- and PBS-injected ischemic muscle after hindlimb ischemia, specifically in isolated CD45-CD31+ endothelial cell

title: Gene expression profiles of WT and Vil-CREPTKO intestinal cyrpts
summary: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) residing in the crypts are critical for the continual self-renewal and rapid recovery of intestinal epithelium. The regulatory mechanism of ISCs is not fully understood. Here we report that CREPT, a recently identified tumor-promoting gene, is preferably expressed in the crypts, where the ISCs reside, but not in the villi. To explore the function of CREPT in ISCs, we isolated crypts to perform Next generation sequencing.

title: Antagonistic role of Hnf4a and FoxO1 metabolic networks through enhancer interactions in beta-cell function [RNA-seq]
summary: To investigate the relationship between key beta-cell transcription factors Hnf4a and Foxo1.

title: Reshaping Circadian Metabolism in the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus and Prefrontal Cortex by Nutritional Challenge
summary: We compared the transcriptome of Suprachiasmatic Nucleus in C57BL/6J mice fed a high-fat diet or normal chow through an entire circadian cycle: 6 time points (TP) every four hours.
design: RNA-seq analysis of the Suprachiasmatic Nucleus of mice fed high-fat diet versus normal chow fed mice.

title: Estrogen-related receptor γ agonist DY131 ameliorates lipopolysaccharide-induced acute liver injury
summary: DY131 is a pharmacological agonist of the orphan receptor estrogen-related receptor (ERR) γ which plays a crucial role in regulating energy generation, oxidative metabolism, cell apoptosis, inflammatory responses, etc. However, its role in acute liver injury is unknown. In the study, we evaluated the effect of DY131 on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced liver injury. Transcriptomics analysis revealed that the dysregulated pathways associated with inflammation and metabolism were significantly reversed by DY131 in LPS-treated mice, providing more evidence in favor of the protective effect of DY131 against LPS-induced liver injury.

title: Single-cell RNA transcriptomics of thymic iNKT cells from C57BL/6 and Hivep3-/- mice
summary: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of murine thymic iNKT cells from two independent C57BL/6 mice and two independent Hivep3-deficient mice

title: RNAseq of splenic dendritic cells from 1 week-old and adult  Clec9a-Cre Rosa-Tomato mice
summary: We use bulk RNA sequencing of sorted cells to characterize the gene expression profiles of splenic TOM+ cDC2 and TOM- DC2 from 1 week-old mice as well and of TOM+ cDC2 from adult mice. We aim to reveal transcriptional differences based on ontogeny and developmental age. Sequencing results revealed that the developmental age rather than cell origin is a major determinantof the transcriptomic differences observed between young and adult cDC2.

title: Identifying differentially expressed genes in Zmat3 knockout cells
summary: The goal of the study was to identify genes whose expression is Zmat3 depedent using RNA-seq.

title: KLF10 deficiency in CD4+ T cells triggers obesity and insulin resistance
summary: Gene expression profiling of CD4+ T regs from WT and CD4-KLF10-KO mice on a high-fat diet.

title: Metabolic Effects of Air Pollution Exposure and Reversibility
summary: In this study, we modeled early life air pollution exposure using C57BL/6J male mice on a controlled chow diet, exposed to real-world inhaled concentrated PM2.5 (~10x ambient level/ ~60-120g/m3) or filtered air (FA) over 14 weeks.  We investigated PM2.5 effects on phenotype, transcriptome and chromatin accessibility, compared the effects with a prototypical high-fat diet (HFD) stimulus, and examined the effects of cessation of exposure on reversibility of phenotype/genotype.
design: RNA sequencing and ATAC-seq were performed to compare the transcriptome and epigenome of air pollution exposed mice and high-fat diet.

title: TET1 KO affects Sox9 function [growth plate tissue]
summary: We report that TET1 mediated 5hmC deposition is necessary for Sox9 function in embryonic cartilage development
design: We examine the transcriptional changes after TET1 KO in E17.5 mouse chondrocytes

title: RNA sequencing discerns sub-populations of pancreatic β-cells and dynamics of gene expression in partial pancreatectomy model
summary: We employed single-cell RNA sequencing of islets in young mice subjected to partial pancreatectomy (PPTx). Four clusters of pancreatic beta cells including a subpopulation of replicating beta cells. Pseudo-time course analysis clarified the gradual changes in gene expression from non-replicating beta cells to replicating ones. Upstream analysis visualized the transcriptional networks associated with beta cell replication by PPTx.
design: Pancreatic islets were isolated from young mice 2 days after PPTx or without PPTx. Cells were dispersed by trypsin and went to single cell RNA-seq. Data were processed by dimensional reduction and clustering. Subpopulations in pancreatic islet cells and differentially expressed genes were analyzed. Cell cycle analysis and expression of cell cycle genes identified one cluster as replocating beta cells. Pseudo time analysis were performed and gradual change of gene expression from non-replicating beta cells to replicating beta cells were visualised. Upstream analysis were conducted using genes differentially expressed in each subpopulation and different timepoint in pseudo-time.

title: Single-cell Transcriptome Analysis Dissects the Replicating Process of Pancreatic Beta Cells in Partial Pancreatectomy Model.
summary: We employed single-cell RNA sequencing of islets in young mice subjected to partial pancreatectomy (PPTx). Four clusters of pancreatic beta cells including a subpopulation of replicating beta cells. title: Determine in vivo the contribution of distal intestinal segments to calcium homeostasis and bone mineralization
summary: To explore this question, we will use three different male mouse models including VDR KO mice and transgenic mice with hVDR only expressed in the distal intestine (KO/VDR-Tg). All the mice which are C57BL6J background will be raised until 2-3 months old with standard chow diet (n=3 mice per genotype group). Compared to the KO/VDR-Tg mice without any injection, the same type of mice will be administered 1 ng/g bw 1,25(OH)2D3 at 48, 24 and 6 hours prior to termination to determine both early and late effects of 1,25(OH)2D3.
design: Mouse data comprising RNA-Seq from 21 samples was obtained: 11 from the colon (4 VDR knockout replicates, 3 VDR uninjected replicates, 4 VDR vitamin D treated replicates) and 10 from the ileum (4 VDR knockout replicates, 3 VDR uninjected replicates, 3 VDR vitamin D treated replicates).

title: Single cell RNA sequencing reveals functional heterogeneity and sex differences of glioma-associated brain macrophages
summary: Single cell RNA-seq analysis of CD11b+ cells sorted from murine syngeneic gliomas, indicating distinct activity of microglia, infiltrating monocytes/macrophages and CNS border associated macrophages. It demonstrates a molecular heterogeneity in the innate immune response in gliomas. Differently expressed genes were identified in activated microglia from glioma-bearing mice of different sex, and profound overexpression of the MHCII genes was observed in male microglial cells.

title: Transcriptional profile of male and female embryonic day 18 (E18) C57Bl6/J mouse dorsal forebrain after chronic maternal infusion with arginine vasopression (AVP) or saline throughout gestation.
summary: This experiment assessed transcriptional changes in embryonic dorsal forebrain in male and female offspring to determine the sex-specific mechanism(s) by which chronic gestaitonal exposure to arginine vasopression (AVP), a mouse model of the hypertensive gestational disorder preeclampsia, alters neurodevelopment.
design: RNA was isolated from male and female E18 dorsal forebrain following maternal infuson throughout gestation with vasopressin or saline via a subcutaneous osmotic minipump.

title: Acute effects of beta2-adrenergic receptor activation on macrophage transcriptome
summary: The study was designed to investigate the acute effects of B2AR receptor activation on global gene expression changes in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Fenoterol was chosen as B2AR agonist, but our earlier experiments using B2AR antagonists and B2AR knockout cells indicated that norepinephrine signal predominantly via B2AR in macrophages.

title: Noise exposures causing hearing loss generate proteotoxic stress and activate the proteostasis network
summary: We investigate how noise insults affect the cochlea with proteomics and functional assays. Quantitative proteomics reveals that exposure to loud noise causes proteotoxicity. We identify and confirm hundreds of proteins that accumulate, including cytoskeletal proteins, and several nodes of the proteostasis network. Transcriptomic analysis reveals that a subset of the genes encoding these proteins also increase acutely after noise exposure, including numerous proteasome subunits.

title: Quantification of transcriptional changes during in vivo mouse erythropoiesis by nascent RNA-sequencing
summary: We isolated erythroid progenitor cells at various stages of differentiation from mouse fetal liver using flow cytometry. We metabolically labelled RNA from purified progenitor populations with 4-thiouridine (4sU) for 45 minutes in ex vivo culture, then extracted cellular RNA. Nascent RNA was biotinylated by reaction of the incorporated thiol groups with MTS-Biotin, then purified using streptavidin nanobeads and sequenced.

summary: Transcriptonal analysis of Tregs reveal role of LAG3 in stability and function of Tregs in an inflamed CNS

Tissue were excised and microdissected for RNA Seq analysis.

title: Bulk sequencing of isolated endothelial cells in AD
summary: We report the application of using next-generation sequencing to quantify gene expression differences in cerebral endothelial cells between APP/PS1 and Ctrl littermates.

title: Differential gene expression in a mouse model for pediatric high grade glioma encoding for H3.3-G34R mutation
summary: This experiment was designed to study the effect of the histone H3.3-G34R mutation on the transcriptome of tumor cells and immune-infiltrating cells, in a high grade glioma mouse model.

summary: Plasmodium chabaudi infected mice were drug-treated on day 14 post-infection with an i.p. injection of CQ (10mg/kg) and pyrimethamine (10mg/kg) followed by CQ (6 mg/ml) and pyrimethamine (70 mg/ml) containing water for 5 days. Spleens were removed 12 weeks after completion of drug treatment. Spleens from drug-treated naive mice were used as controls.

title: Spleen glia are a transcriptionally unique glial subtype interposed between immune cells and sympathetic axons
summary: Non-myelinating glia in visceral organs have not been well characterized. It Is likekely they have uniqe functions in the organs in which they reside. This is interesting in immune organs such as the spleen in which glia ensheath nerves that come in close contact with immune cells. However, glia in the spleen have not been well characterized. We report here an in-depth anatomical and transcriptional characterization of spleen glia.

title: The effect of beta-glucan - induced trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of bone marrow granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMP) in tumor-bearing mice
summary: Induction of trained immunity by beta-glucan has been shown to promote transcriptomic alterations in myeloid cells. Progenitors in the bone marrow are also affected by trained immunity and also regulate anti-tumor immune responses . In this study, we performed RNA sequencing in GMP from tumor-bearing mice in order to investigate the impact of trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of myeloid progenitors in the tumor setting.
design: WT mice were pretreated with a single dose of 1 mg of β-glucan from Trametes versicolor (Invivogen) in PBS or with PBS vehicle alone (control) and were then injected subcutaneously with 3 x 105 B16-F10 melanoma cells into the right flank. Bone marrow GMP (Lin—c-Kit+Sca1—CD16/32+CD34+) were sorted 14 days after tumor cell injection and RNA sequencing analysis was performed.

title: The effect of beta-glucan - induced trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of bone marrow granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GMP)
summary: Induction of trained immunity by beta-glucan affects myeloid cells and their bone marrow progenitors. In particular, broad alterations in the transcriptome of  trained myeloid cells have been demonstrated.  In this study, we performed RNA sequencing in GMP from beta-glucan treated mice, as compared to control-treated mice, in order to investigate the impact of trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of GMP.
design: WT mice were treated with a single dose of 1 mg of β-glucan from Trametes versicolor (Invivogen) in PBS or with PBS vehicle alone (control) and after seven days bone marrow GMP (Lin—c-Kit+Sca1—CD16/32+CD34+) were sorted and RNA sequencing analysis was performed.

title: The effect of beta-glucan - induced trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN)
summary: Induction of trained immunity by beta-glucan has been shown to promote transcriptomic alterations in myeloid cells. Neutrophils are involved in the immune response against tumors and can promote or inhibit tumor growth. In this study, we performed RNA sequencing in TAN from mice in order to investigate the impact of trained immunity on the transcriptomic profile of neutrophils in the tumor setting.
design: WT mice were pretreated with a single dose of 1 mg of β-glucan from Trametes versicolor (Invivogen) in PBS or with PBS vehicle alone (control). After 7 days, mice were injected subcutaneously with 3 x 105 B16-F10 melanoma cells into the right flank. Neutrophils (CD45+CD11c-CD11b+Ly6c-Ly6g+) that were infiltrated in the tumor were sorted 14 days after tumor cell injection and RNA sequencing analysis was performed.

title: Comparative bulk RNAseq analysis of label-retaining chondrocytes (LRCs) of the growth plate versus their progeny

summary: The mRNA m6A reader YTHDF2 is overexpressed in human acute myeloid leukaemias.  To understand the role of YTHDF2 in normal haematopoiesis and ageing, we performed SMART-seq on haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) derived from young and aged (1 year old) mice.  In parallel, to identify transcripts likely methylated in HSCs we performed meRIP-seq analysis of c-Kit+ cells.
design: In young mice, two samples per mouse were taken from 4 WT vs 4 KO mice, but since replicate samples taken from each mouse behaved as biological replicates, they were treated as such. In aged mice, two samples were taken per mouse from 4 WT vs 5 KO mice, and again, because replicate samples from the same mouse acted as biological replicates, these samples were treated as such. Please note that the 'aged_WT99_HSC_B' sample has low read counts and is excluded from further analysis.

title: Gene expression of optic nerve head astrocytes in aged and glaucomatous mouse
summary: Microbeads (experimental glaucoma) or saline solution (controls) were injected into right anterior chamber of young adult mice to induce high intraocular pressure in glaucoma group. In addition, 13 week old and 40 week old naïve C57bl/6 mice were also examined.

summary: We report results of transcriptional profiling of ex vivo MC38 murine organotypic tumor spheroids following programmed death-1 (PD-1) blockade compared to isotype control IgG treatment by bulk and single-cell RNA-sequencing after 6 days of treatment. Additionally, we report results from single-cell RNA-sequencing of MC38 tumors treated in vivo with PD-1 blockade versus isotype control IgG to validate ex vivo workflow.

title: Transcriptome changes of endothelial cells in mouse breast tumors by STING activation II
summary: In order to identify transciptomic changes of endothelial cells (Ecs) in response to STING activation, endothelial cells were soted using FACS and RNA-seq was performed.  We compared ECs from 3 models; normal mammary fat pad, MMTV-PyMT spontaneous breast tumor, implanted breast tumor. Mice were anesthetized with isoflurane and euthanized by cardiac puncture followed by cervical dislocation. Intestines were flushed with ice cold PBS and frozen in liquid nitrogen.

summary: Analysis of gene expression in RPE from Mertk KO, Mertk WT, Bai1-Tg+, and Bai1-Tg- mice. The hypothesis was that gene expression profile would differ with Mertk expression and Bai1-Tg expression.
